pages.title: What Mynt is
pages.summary: Lovable for finance apps: products composed from regulated primitives, apps on top built by agents and verified by Mynt.
pages.markdown:
## The problem Mynt removes

Shipping a finance app means a long stretch of work before the first customer sees a screen. Which licence covers the product? Which regulator, which filings, which disclosures? Who integrates identity checks, e-signature, credit bureau and bank data, again? And once the app exists, who proves it shows every mandated document word for word and never leaks a key?

Mynt answers these from one place:

1. A builder composes a product out of regulated building blocks.
2. Mynt works out the regulation that follows, and which licences cover each part.
3. The builder asks for an app in plain words.
4. Coding agents build it, Mynt verifies it, and Mynt hosts it.

## Two ideas behind everything

### A financial product is a composition

Nobody designs a financial product from scratch on Mynt. You compose one from regulated building blocks called **primitives**. A primitive is a product line (credit, payments, insurance and eight others) joined to an action on it (issuance, sale, servicing and six others):

- a recurring deposit is a recurring payment mandate plus a term deposit;
- a foreign-currency transfer is a currency exchange plus a payment.

Because the product is made of primitives, its **regime** follows from them. The regime is the regulation that applies to a product: which regulators supervise it, which licences may provide each part, and which obligations, filings and controls apply. Mynt works this out from its regulatory model, which is data that Mynt admins keep: regulators, licence types, law, and governance, risk and compliance (GRC) registers.

Mynt then checks the product against its regime: the firm behind it, the parties to each part, and their GRC folders. A part must be covered by a verified licence, the firm's own or a sponsoring licence provider's, in each place the product is offered.

Each product also carries its own compliance records: who is responsible for what, the policies and controls, the evidence, and the disclosures that go back to the regulator. Changes are versioned and written to an audit trail.

Changing a product means composing it again, not rebuilding it. Add a part, change who provides it or tighten a term, and the new definition is checked against the regime before it goes live.

### Agents build; Mynt verifies

Agents do the work on Mynt: designing, pricing, building, reviewing, prospecting. Not one of them grades its own work.

- **Every build is verified in a clean sandbox the agent never touched.** Tests, lint and types, a secrets scan, a dependency audit, a software bill of materials (SBOM) and every required disclosure are checked before a pull request is opened. A failed check blocks the pull request.
- **An independent security audit runs when the operator turns it on** (`BUILD_AUDIT=maxwell`). It is off by default, and it is separate from the checks above, which always run.
- **Agents are steered by folders, not by prompts in code.** Each agent's instructions, skills and scripts live in `core/workspaces/<agent>/`, which becomes its working directory. Its skills are human-written ones found on GitHub and vendored with their licence and source.
- **Secrets never enter a sandbox or a hosted app.** Agents reach the model through Mynt's proxy with a token that dies with the run. A hosted app sends a placeholder, and the real key is added on the way out.
- **Every cost is counted.** Sandboxes, model spend and hosting are recorded from metered figures against per-build and monthly caps. A figure that can't be measured is never shown as $0.
- **CI builds and runs the starter app on every push.** It scaffolds the app from a freshly generated SDK, compiles `api/`, `web/` and the Expo app, builds the images and runs them hardened (read-only, no capabilities) before checking that they serve.

## How it works, end to end

| Stage | Who | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Compose | A builder | Picks the primitives, writes the product definition (terms, pricing, customer segments, servicing) and tests it. The product starts as an idea |
| Cover | A licence provider, or the builder's own firm | Each part is covered by a verified licence. A builder without licences asks a licence provider to sponsor the product |
| Review | A Mynt admin | Reviews firms and their licences, with a governance desk of review agents that prepares each case |
| Promote | The builder | Moves the product through idea, staging and production. Mynt checks the regime at each step |
| Build | A team of coding agents | Plans the app, then builds `api/`, `web/` and `mobile/` as one Docker Compose project, on SDKs generated for exactly those products |
| Verify | Mynt | Runs its own checks in a clean sandbox the agents never touched, and only then opens the pull request |
| Host | Mynt | Gives the app a VM of its own, with containers under gVisor, outbound access only to the hosts it needs, and a public HTTPS address for each service. The app's key is added at the edge |
| Go live | The builder | Promotes the app through staging to production. Production needs a signed program agreement with every sponsoring licence provider |
| Use | A customer | Uses the app on the web, on a phone or in a chat |

**What the builder types.** In the MCP client they already use, or in Mynt Studio:

> Build a savings app on the recurring deposit, with a web app and an Expo mobile app.

**What the agents do.** The coding team has seven agents: an architect plans; server, web and mobile engineers build their parts; a read-only compliance reviewer checks every product's contract and build terms (documents shown word for word, consent before the action that needs it, no banned phrase, no open proxy to Mynt); QA runs every journey against the sandbox; a release engineer ships the Compose project.

While the agents work, the builder can open the sandbox in VS Code, run commands in it and watch the diff grow. Once the app is hosted, they can read its logs, run commands in it and SSH into its VM. Mynt hands back only when it must: connecting a repository, an approval, a credential.

**What a customer sees.** A customer says what they need and gets a product card back. This illustration is on a US product, the Dollar Holding Account that ships as an example definition:

```text
You:   I want to keep $500 in a dollar account that I can cash out any time.
App:   Got it. Should it come from your linked bank account?
You:   Yes.
App:   DOLLAR HOLDING ACCOUNT · READY
       Add $500.00 from your bank account
       [ Accept ]  [ Look for more options ]
```

Customers see US dollars only. The United States is the only region products run in today.

**The agents.** The hosted agents are steered by eight agent workspace folders under `core/workspaces/`:

| Folder | The agent |
|---|---|
| `coding-build` | The coding team that builds apps |
| `build-audit` | The optional independent security audit of a build |
| `product-desk` | The product desk: term sheets and feasibility analysis in a firm's own model repository |
| `algorithm-explorer` | The product desk's algorithm explorations |
| `governance-review` | The governance desk, which reviews firms, licences and products for Mynt admins |
| `connector` | The business-development agent |
| `program-audit` | The white-box audit of a Solana program before mainnet |
| `program-red-team` | The black-box red team of a Solana program before mainnet |

## Who Mynt is for

Mynt covers eleven product lines, grouped by economic function: credit, securitization, payments, account operations, custody and settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees and trade, exchange, derivatives and information.

There are six kinds of user. A **builder** is one role with two names in code, `developer` and `innovator`; these docs say builder.

| Who | What Mynt gives them |
|---|---|
| **Consumers** | Products and offers they can use, and a way to ask for what doesn't exist yet |
| **Builders** | Composition of products from regulated primitives, term sheets and feasibility analysis in their own model repository, versioning, licence checks and distribution. And apps on top of products: SDKs, APIs, webhooks, a sandbox mode, campaigns, and coding agents that build apps, which Mynt verifies and hosts. Builders needn't be licensed |
| **Licence providers** | Firms holding the licences. They sponsor builders' products under them, in the jurisdictions they cover, set covenants on them, and can revoke a sponsorship. Their engineers connect their ledger with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/partners.md) |
| **Vendors** | A marketplace for standard services (identity, KYC, account data, bureau, e-signature and others) that builders plug into their products, tested by Mynt before they are listed |
| **Liquidity providers** | Firms and funds that put capital into products' pools. They get a withdrawal queue with stated notice and reserve rules, and health readings for each product. Mynt never holds funds |
| **Mynt admins** | The regulatory model (regulators, licences, law, GRC), a governance desk that reviews firms, licences and products, the platform admin in Mynt Studio, and `ops_status` for what needs attention |

What each role can do, and how the roles nest, is in [Roles and tools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/roles-and-tools.md).

## Ground rules

- **Secrets by name only.** Keys live in the server's environment, are never printed, and never enter a sandbox, a hosted app or a pull request.
- **Keys stay out of reach.** An app's key lives only on a server Mynt hosts, and even there it is added on the way out, never stored on the VM. Web and mobile apps run on short-lived client sessions.
- **Products follow their contracts.** Only the actions a product lists, where they may run; every required document shown word for word; consent before the action that needs it.
- **Agents never grade their own work.** Verification runs in a clean sandbox, and only its result decides whether a build ships.
- **No open proxy to Mynt.** On Mynt's hosting, anything an app sends to Mynt's server-side routes carries its key, so apps forward only client-session routes.
- **Customer data in one vault.** It is encrypted (AES-256-GCM), collected only after consent, erasable on request, and never in the app's own database or logs.
- **Isolated by default.** Each hosted app has a VM of its own, its containers run under gVisor, and it can reach only the hosts it needs.
- **Dollars only for customers.** A builder's customers see and send US dollars: amounts, fees, totals, statuses, arrival times and references. Wallets, tokens, chain names, addresses and stablecoin symbols never reach an app. The USDC on Solana underneath is the licensed ramp partner's settlement rail, and Mynt refuses any service type that would show a device otherwise.
- **Money moves only on approved rails.** Every movement passes one check before it is recorded. Mynt authorises and records movements; licensed firms move the money. See [Money rails](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md).
- **Nothing is guessed.** A cost that can't be measured is never shown as $0.

pages.title: Authentication & roles
pages.markdown:
## Who does what

### Consumer

A consumer uses financial products: enrols, answers offers and asks for products that don't exist yet.

- Enrolment: `enroll_in_product`, `list_my_enrollments`, `cancel_enrollment`, `upgrade_enrollment`
- Offers from campaigns: `list_offers` (see [Campaigns](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#campaigns))
- Product requests: `request_product`, `list_my_product_requests` (see [Product requests](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-requests))

### Builder

A builder (`innovator` or `developer`) does two jobs with one role.

It composes financial products. A builder acts for a firm (`create_entity`) and registers the licences the firm holds (`register_license`), which a Mynt admin verifies against the regulator's register (`review_license`). A product declares the firm's role on it in `action`: `issuance`, `sale` or `repackaging`, with `underlying_product_ids` for the last two.

Publishing a product needs a verified, in-date licence covering each of its components. The licence is either the firm's own or a licence provider's, under an approved sponsorship of that component.

It also builds apps and software development kits (SDKs) on products. An app never issues a product, holds funds or collects financial data itself. Onboarding, identity checks and payments hand off to the product's own flow (`deep_link`, `initiate_onboarding`; see [Hand-offs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#hand-offs)).

Products:

- Compose and publish: `create_product`, `update_product`, `test_product`, `publish_product`, `unpublish_product`, `list_my_products` (see [Products](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md))
- Definitions: `set_product_definition`, `get_product_definition`, `check_product_definition`, `set_product_composition` (see [Product definitions](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-definitions))
- Stages: `get_product_promotion_checks`, `promote_product`, `demote_product` (see [Product stages](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-stages))
- Out of the way: `archive_product`, `unarchive_product` (see [Archiving a product](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#archiving-a-product))
- Versions: `create_product_version`, `update_product_version`, `list_product_versions`, `diff_product_versions`, `restore_product_version`, `list_product_activity`, `upgrade_enrollments` (see [Versioning](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#versioning))
- Distribution and earnings: `get_product_distribution_metrics`, `report_handoff_outcome`, `get_product_take_rate` (see [Hand-offs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#hand-offs) and [Take rates](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#take-rates))
- Product requests: `list_product_requests`, where requesters appear only under a pseudonymous id, and `respond_to_product_request`, which offers one of your published products and is audited (see [Product requests](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-requests))
- Product ideas and the product desk: see [Product ideas](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-ideas) and [The product desk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#the-product-desk)
- Sponsorship: `request_sponsorship`, `list_my_sponsorships` (see [Sponsorship](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#sponsorship))
- The firm: `create_entity`, `get_my_entity`, `register_license`, `set_entity_facts`, `add_party`, `end_party` (see [Legal entities](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#legal-entities))

Apps:

- Apps: `create_app`, `update_app`, `list_my_apps`, `preview_app`, `publish_app` (see [Apps](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#apps))
- Access to products: see [Building on a product](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#building-on-a-product)
- Builds, repositories and hosting: see [Coding-agent builds](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#coding-agent-builds), [Repositories](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#repositories) and [Hosting](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#hosting)
- Campaigns: `create_segment`, `list_my_segments`, `create_campaign`, `update_campaign`, `lint_campaign`, `launch_campaign`, `pause_campaign`, `end_campaign`, `list_my_campaigns`, `get_campaign_metrics` (see [Campaigns](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#campaigns))
- Keys: `create_api_key`, `list_api_keys`, `rotate_api_key`, `revoke_api_key` (see [Keys](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#keys))
- Webhooks: `create_webhook`, `list_webhooks`, `delete_webhook`, `rotate_webhook_secret`, `list_webhook_deliveries` (see [Webhooks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#webhooks))
- Sandbox mode and releases: `create_test_consumer`, `simulate_handoff`, `release_app`, `list_app_releases`, `rollback_app`, `get_app_metrics` (see [Sandbox and releases](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#sandbox-and-releases))
- SDKs, journeys and modules: see [SDKs and experiences](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#sdks-and-experiences), [Journeys](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#journeys) and [Developer modules](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#developer-modules)
- Solana programs: see [Solana programs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md)

Workspaces, agreements and risk:

- Workspaces: `list_workspaces`, `create_workspace`, `rename_workspace`, `list_workspace_members`, `invite_to_workspace`, `revoke_workspace_invite`, `change_member_role`, `remove_workspace_member`, `leave_workspace`, `relink_workspace_org`, `archive_workspace`, `unarchive_workspace` (see [Workspaces](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#workspaces))
- App stages: `get_promotion_checks`, `promote_app`, `demote_app`, `set_app_target_states`, `request_promotion_signoff`, `get_workspace_attention` (see [Stages and promotion](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#stages-and-promotion))
- Agreements: `propose_app_agreement`, `update_agreement_scopes`, `respond_to_app_agreement`, `sign_app_agreement`, `terminate_app_agreement`, `list_app_agreements`, `get_agreement_signing_link`, `download_agreement_document` (see [App agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#app-agreements))
- Customers: `get_app_customers`, `set_app_target_segments` (see [Target customers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#target-customers))
- Oversight audits: `list_agreement_audits`, `get_agreement_audit`, `submit_agreement_audit_evidence`, `respond_to_agreement_audit_finding` (see [Oversight audits](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#oversight-audits))
- Service levels: `list_agreement_slas`, `add_agreement_sla`, `retire_agreement_sla`, `record_sla_breach`, `resolve_sla_breach` (see [Service levels](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#service-levels))
- Risk registers, for apps and products: `add_risk`, `update_risk`, `list_risks` (see [Risk registers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#risk-registers))
- One risk in full, and what its keeper adds under it: `get_risk`, `add_risk_factor`, `update_risk_factor`, `remove_risk_factor`, `add_risk_treatment`, `update_risk_treatment`, `add_risk_control`, `update_risk_control`, `retire_risk_control`, `link_risk`, `unlink_risk` (see [One risk in full](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#one-risk-in-full))

Vendor services and pools:

- Vendor services: `list_service_types`, `list_vendor_offerings`, `subscribe_vendor_service`, `list_my_vendor_subscriptions`, `set_subscription_live`, `unsubscribe_vendor_service` (see [Subscriptions](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#subscriptions))
- Services (a builder reads a service of its workspace; creating one takes the vendor role): `get_service`, `list_my_services`, `get_service_type_contract`, `request_service_type`, `list_service_type_requests` (see [Services](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/services.md))
- Results from vendor services: `create_firm_webhook`, `list_firm_webhooks`, `delete_firm_webhook` (see [Firm webhooks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#firm-webhooks))
- Liquidity pools on its products: see [Liquidity pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#liquidity-pools)

### Licence provider

A licence provider (`license_provider`) is a firm that holds licences, verified by Mynt admins, and sponsors builders' products under them. It approves, declines or revokes sponsorship of a product's component under a licence it holds, in the jurisdictions that licence covers. Its firm is added by hand by a Mynt admin.

- Sponsorship: `list_my_licenses`, `list_sponsorship_requests`, `approve_sponsorship`, `decline_sponsorship`, `revoke_sponsorship`, `list_sponsored_products` (see [Sponsorship](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#sponsorship))
- Onboarding: `get_regulated_firm_onboarding` (see [Onboarding a regulated firm](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#onboarding-a-regulated-firm))
- The firm: `get_my_entity`, `register_license`, `set_entity_facts`, `add_party`, `end_party`. Its roster fills the stakeholders its licences mandate (see [Legal entities](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#legal-entities))
- Agreements apps propose to its firm: `list_app_agreements`, `respond_to_app_agreement`, `sign_app_agreement`, `terminate_app_agreement`, `get_agreement_signing_link`, `download_agreement_document` (see [App agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#app-agreements))
- Agreements it proposes to workspaces: `propose_workspace_agreement`, and `update_agreement_scopes` while one is proposed (see [Scopes](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#scopes))
- Program agreement templates: `upload_agreement_template`, `list_agreement_templates`, `retire_agreement_template` (see [E-signature](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#e-signature))
- Oversight audits it runs: `add_agreement_audit_requirement`, `retire_agreement_audit_requirement`, `open_agreement_audit`, `record_agreement_audit_finding`, `resolve_agreement_audit_finding`, `close_agreement_audit`, `list_agreement_audits`, `get_agreement_audit` (see [Oversight audits](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#oversight-audits))
- Service levels: `add_agreement_sla`, `retire_agreement_sla`, `record_sla_breach`, `resolve_sla_breach`, `list_agreement_slas` (see [Service levels](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#service-levels))
- Risk registers of the products it sponsors: `list_risks` and `get_risk`, read-only (see [Risk registers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#risk-registers))
- Covenants: `set_covenant`, `list_covenants`, `delete_covenant`, `list_covenant_breaches`, `acknowledge_breach`, `release_covenant_pause` (see [Covenants](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#covenants))
- Alerts to its firm: `create_firm_webhook`, `list_firm_webhooks`, `delete_firm_webhook` (see [Firm webhooks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#firm-webhooks))
- Its ledger and product health: see [Partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit) and [Product health](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#product-health)
- Money rails and pools on sponsored products: see [Money rails](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md) and [Liquidity pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#liquidity-pools)

### Vendor

A vendor offers standard services that builders plug into their products instead of each integrating them: identity checks, business verification, bank account verification, bureau reports, smart-contract audits and the Mynt Ramp. A vendor is a peer of builders, neither above nor below them. Mynt Studio calls vendors "service providers".

- Offerings: `list_service_types`, `create_vendor_offering`, `update_vendor_offering`, `run_practice_conformance`, `run_conformance`, `list_my_offerings` (see [Offerings and conformance](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#offerings-and-conformance))
- Onboarding: `get_vendor_onboarding` (see [Onboarding a vendor](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#onboarding-a-vendor))
- Services built on Mynt, the third kind beside apps and financial products: `create_service`, `archive_service`, and with builders `get_service`, `list_my_services`, `get_service_type_contract`, `request_service_type`, `list_service_type_requests` (see [Services](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/services.md)). Building one also takes the builder's tools (`start_build`, `deploy_app`, `promote_app`)
- Subscribers: `list_my_subscribers`, `reveal_subscription_secret`, `rotate_subscription_secret` (see [Subscriptions](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#subscriptions))
- The Mynt Ramp, for the firm that runs it: `set_ramp_adapter`, `link_ramp_partner_customer` (see [The Mynt Ramp](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#the-mynt-ramp))
- The firm: `get_my_entity`, `register_license`
- Agreements with apps: see [App agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#app-agreements). A vendor has no agreement templates: its terms are its offerings' standard terms

### Liquidity provider

A liquidity provider (`liquidity_provider`) is a firm or fund, added by a Mynt admin, that puts capital into products' pools and takes it out. It watches each product's health to decide where capital goes. It gets its own tools and none of a builder's or a consumer's.

See [Liquidity pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#liquidity-pools), [The withdrawal queue](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#the-withdrawal-queue) and [Product health](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#product-health).

### Mynt admin

A Mynt admin (`admin`) runs Mynt itself, from inside Mynt: regions, product types, the regulatory model, who may sign in, firms and oversight. Admin tools sit beside the builder, vendor and licence-provider tools an admin also holds, except the seven licence-provider tools named in [How roles nest](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/roles-and-tools.md#how-roles-nest).

- Regions and product types: `define_region`, `define_product_category`, `recompute_product_derived` (see [The regulatory model](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#the-regulatory-model))
- Who may sign in: `list_whitelist`, `invite_user`, `revoke_user` (see [Invite-only sign-in](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#invite-only-sign-in))
- Firms: `register_firm`, `add_entity_member`, `remove_entity_member`, `recover_firm_member`, `run_firm_checks`, `get_regulated_firm_onboarding` (see [Firms and licence review](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#firms-and-licence-review))
- Oversight: `audit_log`, where each entry carries its `class`, `list_all_campaigns`, `admin_pause_campaign`, `admin_set_product_status` (see [Oversight](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#oversight))
- Take rates: `define_take_rate`, `list_take_rates` (see [Take rates](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#take-rates))
- Any workspace's members, by its owners' rules: `admin_invite_workspace_member`, `admin_change_workspace_member_role`, `admin_remove_workspace_member`, `admin_revoke_workspace_invite` (see [Members and invitations](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#members-and-invitations))
- Risk registers: `admin_list_risks`, and Mynt's own with `add_risk`, `update_risk` and `list_risks` on the `platform` subject, and the tools under one risk (`get_risk` reads any register's risk for an admin) (see [Risk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md))
- Risk grading: `get_risk_grading`, `set_risk_grading` (see [Risk grading](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#risk-grading))
- App ideas for the Build page: `create_app_idea`, `update_app_idea`, `retire_app_idea`, `seed_app_ideas` (see [Coding-agent builds](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#coding-agent-builds))
- Product ideas: `create_product_idea`, `update_product_idea`, `retire_product_idea`, `seed_product_ideas` (see [Product ideas](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-ideas))
- Vendors: `define_service_type`, `load_service_types`, `suspend_vendor_offering`, `set_mynt_ramp`, `set_ramp_adapter`, `link_ramp_partner_customer` (see [Vendors and the marketplace](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md))
- Requested service types: `list_service_type_requests`, `decline_service_type_request`, and `define_service_type` with `from_request` (see [Asking for a service type](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/services.md#asking-for-a-service-type))

The rest of an admin's work is in [Platform administration](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md).

## How roles nest

Tools are registered per user, so a client only sees the tools its roles allow. `whoami` shows the roles an account was granted and the effective roles they include.

| Role | Also includes |
| --- | --- |
| `developer` | `innovator` and `consumer` |
| `innovator` | `developer`, and so `consumer` |
| `admin` | `innovator` (the builder, and so `consumer`), `vendor` and `license_provider` |
| `vendor` | nothing |
| `license_provider` | nothing |
| `liquidity_provider` | nothing |
| `consumer` | nothing |

What follows from that:

- Every Mynt admin is also a builder, a vendor and a licence provider, and every builder is a consumer.
- One exception: seven licence-provider tools act as a member of the firm itself, and they go only to that firm's licence providers, never to a Mynt admin. They are `approve_partner_kit_change`, `confirm_partner_ledger_endpoints`, `decide_firm_member`, `register_partner_test_signing_key`, `reveal_partner_ledger_secret`, `rotate_partner_ledger_secret` and `upload_partner_ledger_file` (see [Licence providers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md)).
- A Mynt admin is not a liquidity provider: Mynt's staff don't commit capital.
- Vendors, licence providers and liquidity providers stand beside builders. Each gets the catalogue tools, its firm's record and its own tools only. None of them can publish products or build apps.
- A Mynt admin can grant one person several roles.
- `innovator` and `developer` are both kept so that existing users and invitations keep working. `whoami` shows both among the effective roles.

### Licence-provider powers need standing at the firm

Holding `license_provider` is not enough on its own. An account that belongs to a firm acts as a licence provider only once it has standing there:

- A firm's first licence provider has standing at once.
- After that, a new account waits until one of the firm's licence providers accepts it (`decide_firm_member`).
- Until then the account gets no licence-provider tool, and makes no sponsorship, covenant or licence decision.

See [Partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit) for how members are accepted and recovered.

## Tools everyone gets

Everyone gets the catalogue tools, including guests who connect without a token. They are read-only.

| Tool | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `whoami` | The current user, the roles granted and what those include. A guest can only browse |
| `list_products` | Published financial products, filtered by product line, category, region, risk level or a free-text query |
| `get_product` | One product in full, by its id. A builder can also fetch its own unpublished products |
| `list_categories` | Product lines, categories, regions and risk levels of published products, with counts |
| `list_product_categories` | The product types products can have, and the product lines each is used in |
| `list_apps` | Published apps that builders have made around financial products |
| `list_regions` | The regions products can be offered in, with their regulators |
| `get_region` | One region's regulators, regulatory ecosystem, legal procedure per product line and official sources |
| `get_regulator` | One regulator: what it supervises and every licence it grants, with that licence's governance, risk and compliance (GRC) data |
| `list_legal_instruments` | A region's law in two branches, legislative and judiciary |
| `find_licenses` | The licences in a region that permit an action on a product category for a customer persona |
| `list_regulated_product_types` | A region's regulated product types and the regulators that supervise each |
| `get_product_regime` | The primitives a product is made of and what each falls under: product types, regulators, licences, law, providers and mandated stakeholders |
| `get_template` | A regulator's template for a record a licensee must keep, with its field schema |
| `list_template_defaults` | The default field schema each template kind starts from |

Everyone can also read the resource `mynt://catalog`, the published product catalogue as JSON.

The regulatory tools are explained in [The regulatory model](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#the-regulatory-model), and `list_products` and `get_product` in [Products](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md).

## Invite-only sign-in

A Mynt server that uses an identity provider lets in only people who were invited. Being able to sign in with the provider is not enough.

### Who may sign in

- Each request's access token is verified, and the caller's verified email must be on Mynt's list of invited people.
- The entry on that list also decides the caller's roles.
- Removing it cuts the person off on their next request. What they created stays.

There are three ways onto the list.

| Way | Who does it | Roles it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An admin's invitation | A Mynt admin, with `invite_user` | Any of the seven roles, one or several |
| A workspace invitation | A workspace member, with `invite_to_workspace` | `consumer`; `developer` on accepting a developer invite (see [Getting onto Mynt through a workspace invite](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#getting-onto-mynt-through-a-workspace-invite)) |
| Public sign-up, when open | The person themselves | `consumer` |

### Admin invitations

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `invite_user` | Allows an email to sign in with the given roles, or changes the roles of someone already invited |
| `revoke_user` | Stops an email from using Mynt |
| `list_whitelist` | Lists who may sign in and with which roles, the users who have signed in, and whether public sign-up is on |

- The list is kept in step with the identity provider's allowlist, so people who aren't invited can't sign up at all.
- Mynt refuses any change that would remove the last admin.
- An invitation made in the identity provider's own dashboard can carry roles too, in the user's public metadata as `mynt_roles`. Any of the seven roles is accepted there. On the person's first request Mynt adds them to its list with those roles and logs `invite_via_clerk`.

The operator's steps, the command line and the settings are in [Sign-in with Clerk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#sign-in-with-clerk).

### Public sign-up

A Mynt admin can open sign-up with `set_public_signup` (`enabled: true`).

- Anyone who signs in with a verified email then joins as a `consumer`. Mynt writes a consumer invite for them, so they show in `list_whitelist` and can be revoked like anyone else.
- Higher roles still come only from `invite_user`.
- `revoke_user` also blocks the email from signing up again, until an admin invites it once more.
- Turning it on turns the identity provider's allowlist off, and turning it off turns the allowlist back on. Both are best effort; Mynt's invites decide access either way.
- Closing sign-up stops new people joining. People already in keep their invites.
- The operator's `clerk setup` command follows the setting.

## Front doors and their credentials

`core/src/http.ts` routes every request by path. Each door has its own authentication, and none of them accepts another's credential.

### MCP

| Path | Who calls it | Authenticates with |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /mcp` | People, through any MCP client or Mynt Studio | With Clerk configured: a Clerk OAuth access token for an invited user. Without Clerk: a local `fpm_` token, or no token for a read-only guest |
| `POST /mcp` | A connector agent run | Its own run token (`Bearer mynt_bd_…`), valid while the run is active. It gets the catalogue tools and the connector's own tools, nothing a person's role would give |
| `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource*`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server*` | MCP clients discovering sign-in | None. Served only with Clerk configured |

Locally, `mynt serve` speaks MCP over stdio for one user instead (`FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN`).

### The runtime API

`/v1` and everything under it is handed to `core/src/runtime-api.ts`, which routes it further.

| Path | Who calls it | Authenticates with |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/*` (server routes) | A builder's server (`api/`) | A per-app key (`mynt_live_…` or `mynt_test_…`), stored only as a SHA-256 hash |
| `/v1/client/*` | A customer's browser or phone | A client session secret (`mcs_…`), valid for at most an hour and scoped to products and actions |
| `/v1/vendor/callback/<subscription>` | A vendor finishing an asynchronous action | A `Mynt-Signature` HMAC with the subscription's signing secret |
| `/v1/hosting/bootstrap`, `/v1/hosting/policy`, `/v1/hosting/commands` | A hosted VM's agent, in gateway mode | A one-time bootstrap token, then the tenant's agent token |
| `/v1/ramp-adapters/*` | A ramp partner, for an offering Mynt runs through an adapter | The partner's own webhook signature scheme (`core/src/ramp-adapters/`) |

### Other paths

| Path | Who calls it | Authenticates with |
|---|---|---|
| `/agent/*` | An agent inside its sandbox, reaching the model | A run token that dies with the run (`core/src/agent-proxy.ts`, `core/src/agent-meter.ts`) |
| `POST /webhooks/clerk` | The identity provider, with organization, membership and invitation events | The provider's signature, checked with `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Each event id is handled once. Off when the secret isn't set |
| `/esign/webhook` | The e-signature service | The service's own signature scheme. Each event is handled once |
| `GET /esign/frame-origins` | Mynt Studio | None. It lists the origins signing pages may be framed from, and names no secret |
| `GET /confidential/attestation?nonce=…` | A licence provider checking the confidential service | None. Mynt relays the host's attestation unchanged, with the releases in effect. One request a second across all callers |
| `/ramp-sandbox/*` | Mynt itself, for a ramp offering pointed at the sandbox | Requests Mynt signed (`core/src/ramp-sandbox.ts`) |
| `/vendor-sandbox/<offering id>` | A vendor practising before its own test endpoint exists | Practice requests signed with that offering's conformance secret (`core/src/vendor-sandbox.ts`); never the real conformance test |
| `/bd/unsubscribe` | Anyone the connector emailed | The unsubscribe link itself |
| `GET /llms.txt`, `/.well-known/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` | AI assistants | None. Plain text, no customer data (`core/src/llms-txt.ts`) |
| `GET /` | Anyone | None. One line pointing at `/mcp` and `/llms.txt` |
| `/healthz` | Load balancers | None. It pings the database |

Anything else answers 404 with a line naming the MCP endpoint.

## How tools are registered per role

`createServer(store, user, ctx)` in `core/src/server.ts` builds a fresh MCP server **per signed-in user** and registers only the tools that user's roles allow. A client never sees a tool it can't call.

There are seven roles (`ROLES` in `core/src/store.ts`): `consumer`, `developer`, `innovator`, `vendor`, `license_provider`, `liquidity_provider` and `admin`. `developer` and `innovator` are two names for one role, the builder: each implies the other.

Roles nest (`IMPLIES` and `effectiveRoles` in `core/src/store.ts`):

| Role | Also holds |
|---|---|
| `admin` | builder (so also consumer), `vendor` and `license_provider`. Not `liquidity_provider`: Mynt's staff don't commit capital |
| builder (`developer`, `innovator`) | `consumer` |
| `vendor`, `license_provider`, `liquidity_provider` | Nothing else. They stand beside builders with their own tools only |
| `consumer` | Nothing else |

A guest (no token) gets the read-only catalogue tools. A licence provider's powers also need standing at its firm (`rolesWithStanding` in `core/src/store.ts`).

Each feature module owns its tools and registers them from `server.ts`. Grouped as the reference files are:

| Area | Modules that register tools | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Catalogue, consumers | `core/src/server.ts`, `core/src/product-requests.ts` | [Roles and tools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/roles-and-tools.md) |
| Products | `core/src/server.ts`, `core/src/product-stages.ts`, `core/src/definition-tools.ts`, `core/src/versions.ts`, `core/src/marketplace.ts`, `core/src/product-ideas.ts`, `core/src/desk.ts`, `core/src/explore.ts`, `core/src/take-rates.ts` | [Products](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md) |
| Apps and builds | `core/src/server.ts`, `core/src/builds.ts`, `core/src/build.ts`, `core/src/app-kinds.ts`, `core/src/app-ideas.ts`, `core/src/repo-approvals.ts`, `core/src/hosting-tools.ts`, `core/src/gtm.ts` | [Apps and builds](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md) |
| Runtime | `core/src/runtime.ts`, `core/src/journeys-tools.ts`, `core/src/modules.ts` | [Runtime API](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md) |
| Workspaces | `core/src/workspaces.ts`, `core/src/promotions.ts`, `core/src/attention.ts`, `core/src/workspace-compliance.ts`, `core/src/workspace-pnl.ts`, `core/src/linked-accounts.ts`, `core/src/chat-sessions.ts` | [Workspaces and sign-in](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md) |
| Vendors | `core/src/vendors.ts`, `core/src/vendor-onboarding.ts`, `core/src/ramp-adapters/index.ts` | [Vendors and the marketplace](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md) |
| Licence providers | `core/src/sponsorships.ts`, `core/src/marketplace.ts` (firms and rosters), `core/src/covenants.ts`, `core/src/partner-kit.ts`, `core/src/product-health-tools.ts`, `core/src/firm-notices.ts`, `core/src/firm-check-tools.ts`, `core/src/regulated-firm-onboarding.ts` | [Firms, licences and licence providers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md) |
| Agreements | `core/src/app-agreements.ts`, `core/src/agreement-esign.ts`, `core/src/esign-settings.ts`, `core/src/agreement-audits.ts`, `core/src/agreement-slas.ts` | [Agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md) |
| Risk | `core/src/risk-register.ts`, `core/src/risk-detail.ts`, `core/src/risk-grading.ts`, `core/src/risk-models.ts` | [Risk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md) |
| Money and liquidity | `core/src/money-rails.ts`, `core/src/liquidity-tools.ts`, `core/src/treasury-tools.ts` | [Money rails](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md), [Liquidity pools and on-chain treasuries](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md) |
| Solana | `core/src/solana/tools.ts`, `core/src/solana/mainnet-gate.ts` | [Solana programs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md) |
| Confidential computing | `core/src/confidential/governance.ts` | [Confidential computing](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/confidential-computing.md) |
| Mynt admins | `core/src/admin.ts`, `core/src/platform-admin.ts`, `core/src/platform-keys.ts`, `core/src/platform-settings.ts`, `core/src/ops.ts`, `core/src/review.ts`, `core/src/bd.ts`, `core/src/app-removal.ts` | [Platform administration](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md) |

Some modules register only when their service is configured: hosting, developer modules, the product desk, explorations, coding-agent builds, Solana, the mainnet gate, product health, covenants, the treasury, the connector and the governance desk each come from `ctx`.

`core/src/tool-catalogue.ts` reads the live registry for each role and writes the tool reference the docs site shows (`docs/site/tools.json`); `core/src/llms-txt.ts` does the same for `/llms-full.txt`. Neither is written by hand, so neither can drift from the server.

Every admin action, and every sensitive action by anyone, is written to `audit_log` with who did it. `core/src/audit-classes.ts` gives each entry its class: security, financial, obligations or workspace.

pages.title: Your first app
pages.markdown:
## Compose, test, promote

Financial products go through the same three stages as apps: idea, staging and production. They move one step at a time, and back down, with the same tool shapes.

| Tool | Call |
| --- | --- |
| `get_product_promotion_checks` | `{ product_id, to_stage }` |
| `promote_product` | `{ product_id, to_stage }` |
| `demote_product` | `{ product_id, to_stage, reason }` |

Only the product's owner moves it; for Mynt's reference products, a Mynt admin does. Every check is Mynt's own, from its records, never what an app or agent reports.

Each move is in the audit trail: `product_promoted`, with the checks it passed and `via` (`promote_product` or `publish_product`), or `product_demoted`, with the reason.

### From idea to production

1. **Create.** `create_product` saves a draft, visible only to its creator. Its stage is idea.
2. **Test.** `test_product` runs the checks:
   - required disclosures: a description, a regulator and at least two features;
   - valid enums;
   - product-line rules: credit uses `cost_of_credit` and risk `not_applicable`; insurance uses protection, guaranteed or market-linked returns;
   - a misleading-claims check, which fails market-linked products that promise "guaranteed", "assured" or "risk-free" returns.
3. **Move to staging.** `promote_product` to staging needs that test passing on what would go live, unchanged since.
4. **Move to production.** `promote_product` to production publishes the product. It needs what publishing has always needed:
   - the latest test passed and the product hasn't changed since;
   - its v2 definition still checks out;
   - a verified licence covers it: the firm's own, or a licence provider's sponsorship of every component the firm doesn't provide itself;
   - its underlying products are published.
5. **Move back.** `demote_product` from production to staging takes the product out of the catalogue as `unpublish_product` does, and keeps it open to sandbox builds. From staging to idea closes it to sandbox builds.

### What staging allows

A product in staging is open to sandbox builds only.

- `list_buildable_products` with `environment: "sandbox"` lists it. Each item carries its `stage`.
- `create_app` and `update_app` accept it on an app in Ideas or Staging.
- Its builds get it, in the build spec and the generated SDK.
- `get_product_sdk` returns its kit marked `sandbox_only`.

No production app may use it:

- `update_app` refuses it on a production app.
- `promote_app` to production fails its licence check ("is in staging (sandbox builds only)") until the product is in production.
- The runtime API serves only products in production, because each product's frozen developer contract is made when it is published. Runtime calls in sandbox mode on a staging product wait for production.

Editing a staging product keeps it in staging. It needs `test_product` again before production.

### Publishing and unpublishing

- `publish_product` still works: it is a promotion to production, straight from an idea too, because production's checks include staging's. It gives the same refusals.
- A production product's pending draft version (`create_product_version`) goes live the same way, while the product stays in production.
- When a product leaves production, existing enrolments are kept, new ones are blocked, and products built on it pause their sales.
- `unpublish_product` hides a product; it then counts as an idea.

### How the stage is stored

Only staging is stored: `products.stage` is nullable and holds `staging` or nothing. A published product is in production and anything else is an idea. Publishing clears the column.

## What a developer ships

```text
my-app/
├── compose.yaml          api + web (+ mobile web export), hardened: read-only, no capabilities, no host network
├── .env.example          the app key and webhook secret, for api/ only
├── api/                  server: sessions, contracts, webhooks, server-side actions
├── web/                  web app: the journey runner, secure inputs, hosted flows
├── mobile/               Expo app (or Kotlin / Swift / Flutter), same journeys on a client session
├── solana/               optional: an Anchor program (smart contract) and its tests
└── packages/mynt-sdk/    the generated SDK
```

SDKs are generated for TypeScript, React Native, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter and Python.

**Solana programs.** When an app needs a program on Solana, the agents write it next to the app and Mynt takes it from there. It rebuilds the program itself with Anchor's verifiable build in a clean sandbox, tests it on a local validator, deploys exactly those bytes, upgrades it from later verified builds, and sends the program's events to the firm's webhooks.

Mynt signs on devnet. Mainnet stays off until a Mynt admin configures its signer (a key in Mynt's vault, a key-custody service, or a multisig), and every mainnet deploy passes the mainnet program gate first. Customers never see any of it: they see dollars. See [Solana programs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md).

## Promote the app

### Stage

`list_my_apps` gives each app a `stage`: `idea`, `staging` or `production`. A new app starts as an `idea`. Its stage changes only by promotion and demotion, never by its builds or hosting on their own.

Apps that existed before promotions kept the stage Mynt derived for them then: `production` if published and running on Mynt's hosting, `staging` if it had a build Mynt verified or a deployment that wasn't live, else `idea`.

### Promotion

An app moves one step at a time, `idea` to `staging` to `production`, after checks Mynt computes itself from its own records: the builds it verified, the audit it ran, its hosting's state, licences and sponsorships, keys, webhooks, the mainnet program gate and Mynt admins' sign-offs. Nothing the app or an agent reports counts.

| Tool | Who | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_promotion_checks({ app_id, to_stage })` | Any member | Returns the checks for the next stage up |
| `set_app_target_states({ app_id, states })` | Owners and admins | Sets the US states the app serves (`us-ny`, …, `us-dc`) |
| `promote_app({ app_id, to_stage })` | Owners and admins | Runs every check again and moves the app up |
| `demote_app({ app_id, to_stage, reason })` | Owners and admins | Moves the app one step down |
| `request_promotion_signoff({ app_id })` | Owners and admins | Asks a Mynt admin to sign off a production promotion |

In a frozen or archiving workspace, `promote_app`, `demote_app` and `request_promotion_signoff` are refused until an owner relinks or unarchives it.

### Reading the checks

`get_promotion_checks` returns:

```json
{
  "app_id": "…",
  "from_stage": "staging",
  "to_stage": "production",
  "checks": [{ "id": "build_verified", "label": "…", "status": "pass", "detail": "…", "fix": { "label": "…", "href": "…", "tool": "…" } }],
  "can_promote": false,
  "needs_admin_signoff": true,
  "signoff": { "status": "none" }
}
```

- `to_stage` must be the next stage up.
- `status` is `pass`, `fail`, `warn` or `pending`. Pending means Mynt can't tell yet: it blocks like a fail, and is never shown as a pass.
- `fix` is optional: `{ label, href?, tool? }`, where `href` is a Studio path.
- `can_promote` is true when every check passes, or warns where the warning is advisory. Every staging check's warning is advisory. In production only the warnings of `build_verified`, `audit_passed` and `audit_findings` are (`ADVISORY_PRODUCTION_CHECKS`); any other production warning blocks.

### Checks to move to staging

| Check | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `build_verified` | The latest build passed Mynt's verification in a clean sandbox. Pending while one runs; a warning when a newer build failed |
| `audit_passed` | Mynt's independent audit found no critical or high findings, or none ran on that build |
| `app_runs` | The app is healthy on Mynt's hosting, if deployed there. Pending while deploying; a failure when stopped or its hosting isn't running; a warning when not deployed or running an older build |

### Checks to move to production

Production needs the staging checks, with these differences and additions.

| Check | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `hosting_healthy` (in place of `app_runs`) | The app is running on Mynt's hosting, and the build it runs is the latest verified build that every other check and the sign-off are about. Anything else fails |
| `audit_passed` | As for staging, but a warning when no independent audit ran, and a failure then when the app needs sign-off |
| `licences` | Target states are set (none fails). In each of them, every product the app uses is published, its sales are not paused, and it is covered by a licence in force for its action, under an approved sponsorship where a licence provider provides it |
| `program_agreements` | A signed program agreement is in force today with the licence provider sponsoring each product the app uses, covering that product. See [Production needs program agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#production-needs-program-agreements) |
| `webhooks` | Each webhook is on, its secret is held by a current member, and its last delivery did not fail. Pending until a delivery has reached it, for example from a sandbox hand-off |
| `audit_findings` | The newest audited build has no critical or high findings, even one newer than the verified build. With no independent audit there are none to read: a warning, or a failure when the app needs sign-off |
| `program_gate` | When the app has Solana programs or its verified build carries some: each is on mainnet, deployed through the program gate, with no open vulnerability flag. Pending while a review runs |
| `admin_signoff` | Only when `needs_admin_signoff`: a Mynt admin approved this build |

### Promoting and demoting

`promote_app` runs every check again inside one transaction holding the app's lock, and refuses unless `can_promote`. A change since someone looked is caught then.

- The audit trail records `app_promoted` with the build, its source hash, the build its hosting ran and the checks it passed. The same is kept on the app's stage record.
- Members don't promote. They see the same checks and ask an owner or admin.

`demote_app` moves the app one step down, recorded as `app_demoted` with the reason.

- Demoting a production app is refused while it has active live API keys. The caller revokes them first (`revoke_api_key`, the hosted runtime key too). Demotion never revokes them itself, so nobody loses live access by accident.
- It then unpublishes the app (`unpublished: true`).
- Hosting and webhooks stay as they are.

### Production gates real money

Only an app whose stage is `production` may:

- hold a live API key (`create_api_key` and `rotate_api_key` for a live key);
- make a live runtime API call, with a live key or a client session minted with one (`403 app_not_in_production` otherwise);
- publish (`publish_app`, `release_app`).

Ideas and staging apps run on sandbox keys. Each refusal says "Promote this app to Production first".

`deploy_app` gives a hosted app a live runtime key only when it is in production and published, else a sandbox one. So a production promotion doesn't ask for a live key: live keys come after it.

Live webhook events (hand-offs completing, failing, reversing) can only follow live calls, so they come from production apps. One that follows after a demotion (a reversal of an earlier live transfer) is still delivered, never dropped.

Live keys are issued and rotated under the app's stage lock, the same one promotion and demotion take, so a new live key and a demotion can't interleave.

When this gate arrived, existing apps were placed once, each move recorded in the audit trail as `app_stage_grandfathered` with why:

- an app live right then (published, with an active live key or an unexpired real customer session) went to production, so nothing live broke;
- an app live before but not then (a live key, even revoked; published; real customers' sessions or hand-offs) went to staging if it was an idea, so it reaches production only through `promote_app`'s checks;
- the rest stayed as they were.

### Production sign-off

A production promotion needs a Mynt admin's sign-off when the app moves value:

- it has Solana programs beyond devnet, or its verified build carries programs; or
- a product it uses is covered by a firm with an approved money rail.

How it works:

1. An owner or admin asks with `request_promotion_signoff({ app_id })`. The request is for the latest verified build, and only once that build is the one running on Mynt's hosting. Asking again for the same build returns the open request.
2. Mynt admins see requests with `list_promotion_signoffs`.
3. A Mynt admin decides with `decide_promotion_signoff({ id, approve, note? })`. An admin never decides one they asked for themselves, and never one for an app in a workspace they are a member of, in any role.

A sign-off is for one verified build (its id and source hash) and the basis that made it necessary. The `basis` is the app's programs beyond devnet, whether its build carries programs, and the ids of the approved money rails behind its products. All of it is recorded with the sign-off.

- A newer verified build, or a change to that basis without one, makes `signoff.status` `none` again and needs a new sign-off.
- A request whose build or basis changed before it was decided can't be decided: it is marked superseded.

`signoff` is `{ status: none | requested | approved | rejected, by?, at? }`.

## Production needs program agreements

An app moves to `production` only with a **signed program agreement** with every licence provider sponsoring **each product it uses**, covering that product. This is the `program_agreements` promotion check. See [Stages and promotion](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#stages-and-promotion).

### Which licence providers

- Every licence provider with an approved sponsorship of the product counts, wherever it sponsors the product and whichever states the app serves.
- A product no licence provider sponsors is covered by its own firm's licences and needs no agreement.
- One agreement may cover several of the app's products from the same licence provider.
- A product with two sponsoring licence providers needs an agreement with each.

### In force

An agreement counts when:

- its `status` is `signed` (both sides signed);
- `effective_from` is unset, or on or before today;
- `effective_to` is unset, or today or later (the last day it runs).

A `vendor` or `data_sharing` agreement doesn't count.

### The check

`get_promotion_checks` gives it as `{ id: "program_agreements", label: "Signed program agreement with each product's sponsor", status, detail, fix?, coverage }`.

- Each missing pair fails the check in plain words: `No signed program agreement with <sponsor> for <product>`.
- Why the nearest agreement doesn't count follows in brackets. The reasons are:
  - `proposed, waiting for <sponsor> to accept`
  - `<sponsor> accepted it; waiting for your signature`
  - `its signed agreement takes effect on <date>`
  - `its signed agreement ended on <date>`
  - `it was ended on <date>: <reason>`
  - `<sponsor> declined it`
- `fix` is optional. It is `Propose agreement` (`propose_app_agreement`, the app's Agreements tab).
- `coverage` lists each pair: `{ product_id, product_name, sponsor_entity_id, sponsor_name, covered, agreement_id, agreement_status, note }`.
- With nothing to agree, the check passes as "Not applicable".

### The app's view

`list_app_agreements({ app_id })` also returns `program_coverage` (the same pairs) and `production_gate: { met, missing, flagged }`, with the app's `stage`.

### Ending after go-live

An agreement that is terminated or expires after the app reached production doesn't move the app back. The app keeps running, and:

- `production_gate.flagged` is true;
- its production checks fail, so the workspace's attention list has a `promotion_checks_failing` item naming the missing agreement;
- `ops_status` lists it under `apps.production_without_program_agreements` with an attention line.

There is no event channel to an app's workspace. App webhooks carry runtime events, whose list the generated SDKs pin. So the attention list is how the workspace hears of it.

### The other firm's side in the attention list

Each acceptance, decline, signature and termination by the other firm in the last 14 days is an `app_agreement_update` item in the workspace's attention list, linking to the app's Agreements tab.

| Priority | When |
| --- | --- |
| High | It ended a program agreement |
| Medium | Another agreement ended or was declined, or an agreement waits for an owner's or admin's signature |
| Low | Otherwise |

Where the agreement is signed by e-signature, the same list has:

- the other firm's signature on the document;
- the document completed, signed by both sides (low);
- the document declined at signing (medium);
- the document expired or cancelled at the service (high for a program agreement).

The `program_agreements` check's "waiting for your signature" or "waiting for <sponsor>'s signature" reads the document's signatures.

pages.title: Products & primitives
pages.markdown:
## A product is a composition

Nobody designs a financial product from scratch on Mynt. You compose one from regulated building blocks called **primitives**. A primitive is a product line (credit, payments, insurance and eight others) joined to an action on it (issuance, sale, servicing and six others):

- a recurring deposit is a recurring payment mandate plus a term deposit;
- a foreign-currency transfer is a currency exchange plus a payment.

Because the product is made of primitives, its **regime** follows from them. The regime is the regulation that applies to a product: which regulators supervise it, which licences may provide each part, and which obligations, filings and controls apply. Mynt works this out from its regulatory model, which is data that Mynt admins keep: regulators, licence types, law, and governance, risk and compliance (GRC) registers.

Mynt then checks the product against its regime: the firm behind it, the parties to each part, and their GRC folders. A part must be covered by a verified licence, the firm's own or a sponsoring licence provider's, in each place the product is offered.

Each product also carries its own compliance records: who is responsible for what, the policies and controls, the evidence, and the disclosures that go back to the regulator. Changes are versioned and written to an audit trail.

Changing a product means composing it again, not rebuilding it. Add a part, change who provides it or tighten a term, and the new definition is checked against the regime before it goes live.

## Product lines, actions and primitives

### Product lines

Product lines group products by economic function, not asset class: what a product does for the person or firm using it. Every product has one `product_line`.

| Line | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `credit` | Lending and debt instruments, issued or bought: cards, personal, home, auto, education and gold loans, BNPL, working-capital loans, leasing, government and corporate bonds, T-bills, commercial paper |
| `securitization` | Pooling assets into securities: PTCs, ABS/MBS, direct assignment, co-lending pools, REIT/InvIT unit issuance, asset reconstruction |
| `payments` | Moving money: acceptance, payouts, mandates, wallets, remittances, CBDC |
| `account_operations` | Holding and running money: savings, current, term and recurring deposits, sweep accounts, money-market accounts, certificates of deposit, cash management |
| `custody_settlement` | Safekeeping and settlement: custody, depositories, clearing and CCPs, escrow, trustees, vaults |
| `wealth` | Investment exposure: mutual funds (money-market and liquid funds too), ETFs, equities, PMS/AIF, REIT/InvIT units bought as an investment, government savings schemes, and retirement products such as pensions, provident funds, 401(k)s and IRAs |
| `insurance` | Term and whole life, health, motor, home, travel, ULIPs, annuities |
| `guarantees_trade` | Bank guarantees, letters of credit, surety, credit and deposit guarantee schemes, factoring, supply-chain and export finance |
| `exchange` | Currency conversion, securities trading and execution, commodities and bullion trading, digital assets |
| `derivatives` | Forwards, swaps, futures, options |
| `information` | Credit bureaus, account aggregators, ratings, KYC registries, market data |

Products stored under the four lines Mynt started with (credit, wealth, insurance and the old treasury line) are moved onto these eleven once, when the server starts; published products stay published and their test reports are re-run. Old treasury products go by category: deposits to `account_operations`, bonds and money-market instruments to `credit`, derivatives to `derivatives`, and mutual funds to `wealth`. REIT and InvIT units go to `securitization`.

### Compositions

A product that spans functions is a composition of primitives, not a line of its own.

- A cross-border transfer is an exchange primitive (the currency conversion) plus a payments primitive (moving the money).
- Retirement is wealth plus a statutory wrapper.
- Commodities are an underlying, not a line.

### Primitives and the perimeter

The primitive is the line itself. A product component is a line with an action, in a country.

Collateral, customer segment and purpose aren't attributes of the primitive. They are the product's business context: collateral, for instance, is a source of value in underwriting.

What a component falls under in a country is its perimeter: every regulated product type there whose category is on that line and which allows the action. Who supervises the component, which licences may provide it and the law recorded against it all follow from that perimeter. `get_product_regime` shows the result for a product.

### The nine regulated actions

Each regulated product type lists the actions that can be taken on it. A component names one of them.

| Action | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `issuance` | Creating it as the issuer |
| `sale` | Distributing it for its issuer |
| `purchase` | Buying it |
| `secondary_sale` | Selling it on after purchase |
| `repackaging` | Bundling it into something else |
| `advice` | Advising on it |
| `servicing` | Running it after the sale: collections, reconciliation, record-keeping |
| `underwriting` | Taking on its risk or guaranteeing its placement |
| `assessment` | Producing an independent rating, valuation, index, actuarial certification, audit or accreditation of it |

### The firm's role on a product

`create_product` takes an `action` too, and it is a different list. It says what the firm does with the product as a whole:

- `issuance`: the firm is the issuer.
- `sale`: the firm distributes another issuer's products.
- `repackaging`: the firm bundles others' products.

For `sale` and `repackaging`, `underlying_product_ids` names the published products it builds on. The nine regulated actions above apply to a product's components, not to this field.

### Underlying and wrapper

Two optional attributes describe the primitive itself:

- `underlying`: what it is made of. One of `cash`, `securities`, `commodities`, `real_assets`, `receivables`, `risk`, `data` or `digital_assets`.
- `wrapper`: a statutory or tax structure around it. One of `statutory_pension`, `tax_advantaged` or `government_scheme`.

### Fields and filters

Each product has: `id`, `name`, `product_line`, `category`, `region`, `risk_level`, `liquidity`, `typical_horizon`, `return_type`, `regulator`, `description`, `key_features`.

`list_products` filters by `product_line`, `category`, `region` (a country code such as `US` or `IN`, or `global`), `risk_level` or free text. `list_categories` returns counts for each. `get_product` returns one product in full.

## Product definitions

A product's full definition is a JSON document that follows [`core/schemas/financial-product.v2.schema.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/financial-product.v2.schema.json). Builders and their agents read the schema over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the resource `mynt://schemas/financial-product.v2`.

| Tool | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `check_product_definition` | Validate a definition without saving it |
| `set_product_definition` | Validate and save it |
| `get_product_definition` | Read the saved definition (the working copy) with its current check result. A live product also shows the definition hash pinned at publish |
| `set_product_composition` | Set only the components and the parties behind them, without a full definition |

### What a definition contains

- **Components**, each a line with an action, joined by typed composition links. The link types are:
  - `funds`, `settles_into`, `converts_into`, `repays_from`, `co_funds`
  - `guarantees`, `secures`, `covers`, `wraps`
  - `requires`, `excludes`, `feeds_data`, `services`
  - `discovers_price_for`, which makes an exchange component a marketplace
- **Business context around them:** customer segments, core algorithms, risk models, partner handoffs, terms, rates, fees, limits, servicing policies, lifecycle events and costs.
- **Connections:** every link between nodes is a typed connection with its own schema. No node holds lists of other nodes' ids.
- **Upstream records by reference:** the register's personas and items, the owner's licences, roster parties and governance, risk and compliance (GRC) records are connection targets. They are never copied in.

### How a definition is checked

`check_product_definition` validates a definition, and `set_product_definition` validates it before saving. The checks are:

- the JSON Schema;
- that every connection end resolves, including upstream records, which must be real and current;
- the composition rules:
  - the allowed primitive and action at each end of a link;
  - exactly one provider per component;
  - a partner handoff to every party that provides a component;
  - exactly one primary risk model per algorithm;
  - every risk model governed by a GRC record, owned by an internal party.

Every error comes back at once.

A valid definition checked against a product (`product_id`) also lists `publish_blockers`: what the product's regime would refuse at publish. Examples are an uncovered component, or a mandated stakeholder who isn't bound to the component it serves.

Variants (a template plus a patch) can't be saved yet. Save the resolved product as `plane.role: "standalone"`.

### What saving does

- It sets the product's composition and parties, so the regime, the publish checks, pins and drift all keep working.
- It sets the catalogue record from the definition's projection, so existing tools, SDKs and apps keep reading the same fields.
- On a live product, it goes into the draft version.

### Handoffs to a vendor's standard service

A `handoff_to_party` connection may name `attributes.vendor_subscription_id` and, for readers, `service_type`. The subscription is the firm's subscription to a vendor's offering. Then:

- the party must be that subscription's vendor (subscribing adds it to the roster);
- `consent_purpose` must be the service type's;
- the handoff's `sends.required` must include the service type's required inputs, so devices can collect them.

The handoff's client action is then served by the vendor. Both attributes are optional, and definitions without them are unchanged. See [Vendors and the marketplace](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md).

### At publish

The definition is checked again at publish, since parties, licences and records may have changed. Its hash is then pinned as `pins.definition_hash`, and handoffs bound to vendor subscriptions as `pins.vendor_bindings`.

### The developer contract

Publishing a defined product freezes its developer contract: exactly what app builders build against. `get_developer_contract` returns it, and so does `get_product_sdk`. `check_product_definition` previews it.

The contract contains:

- **Offers** per customer segment: eligibility, terms, rates, fees and customer-facing limits, with segment overrides applied.
- **Actions:**
  - `view_offers`;
  - each partner handoff, as the provider's hosted flow on the customer's device, with its consent purpose and typed inputs and outputs;
  - each customer-triggered lifecycle event, as an idempotent server call.
- **Lifecycle events** an app can listen to, the **consent purposes** it must hold and the **documents** it must show.

It never contains algorithms, risk models, fraud and velocity controls, costs, revenue shares or the parties behind the product.

Each version's contract carries a `contract_hash`, which changes whenever the contract does.

### Product GRC folders

Each product has its own GRC folder: `file_grc_record` and `get_grc_folder` with `product_id`. This is where, for example, the governance of the product's risk models lives.

## Base products

A product can be built on others instead of declaring what they already provide.

- A v2 definition lists its bases in `builds_on`: a `product_id`, and optionally the components the base `funds` and those that `settles_from` back through it.
- Saving the definition sets the product's `underlying_product_ids`.
- The composed product inherits the base's coverage. In each state it is offered in, every base must be published, not drifted, and covered there. Otherwise publishing is blocked there with a `builds_on:<product id>` blocker that names the base's reason.
- Its live version pins each base. It drifts when a base drifts (naming the base's states), is offered somewhere else, or is unpublished.

The first base product is US money transmission, [`core/schemas/examples/us/money-transmission.v2.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/examples/us/money-transmission.v2.json). It is owned by the ramp partner's firm and offered in the states where that firm holds a money transmitter licence. Dollar products such as [`dollar-account.v2.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/examples/us/dollar-account.v2.json) are built on it.

## Coverage per state

Some countries license state by state: US money transmission and virtual-currency business are examples. The regulatory model then says where each licence counts.

### How the model records coverage

- States are ISO 3166-2 codes written lowercase, like entities' incorporation: `us-ny`, `us-ca`. The country code `us` is the whole country.
- A state regulator carries `jurisdiction`, and its licence types cover only that state.
- A national regulator's licences cover the whole country.
- A licence type may set `covers` (a list of codes, or `["us"]`, for example for a federal charter that pre-empts state licensing for what it grants), with a `coverage_note` giving the basis.
- A type issued separately in many states sets `issued_per_jurisdiction: true`. The firm registers one held licence per state (`register_license` with `jurisdiction`).
- A licence type with `covers: []` covers nowhere by itself. The FinCEN money services business registration is one: each state's money transmitter licence requires it.
- A licence type may `require` others. A held licence counts only when its holder also holds each prerequisite, verified and in force. An entry may list several ids, any one of which will do. The prerequisite is pinned with the licence.

### How a product is checked

A product lists where it is offered with `offered_in`, on its v2 definition or on a component in `set_product_composition`: `["us-ny", "us-ca"]`, or `["us"]` for the whole country, which needs a licence covering all of it.

Each component is then checked in each state. It is covered there when its provider holds a verified, in-force licence that grants it and covers that state. The provider is the firm itself, a party on its roster, or a licence provider sponsoring the component.

Publishing is blocked for every pair of component and state with no cover; `publish_blockers` carry `jurisdiction`.

Without `offered_in`, the country is checked as a whole, so regions without states are unchanged.

## What Mynt stores on each product

So that coverage and take rate are exact and cheap to read, Mynt keeps two results of its own checks on every product, with `derived_at`.

| Field | Holds |
| --- | --- |
