**The wallet control.** A linked wallet shows the wallet app's own icon and name once a browser wallet has connected it, else a wallet icon and the short address. Its menu names the network once, shows the full address with **Copy address**, offers **Connect wallet** while the wallet app isn't known, links to Earn for your roles (**Manage pools** for builders, **Provide liquidity** for liquidity providers), and **Manage linked accounts**.

The network is shown only when the address fits it; anything else says "Unknown network". Linking itself happens on the identity provider's account page; Studio never embeds a sign-in.

### Signing in and out

A visit to any page while signed out goes straight to Mynt's sign-in and comes back to that page. The only pages that don't need sign-in are the docs (`/docs` and `/connect`), where a failed sign-in lands (`/signin-error`) and where signing out lands (`/signed-out`, with **Sign in again**).

## Dashboard

The home page (`/`) has two views. A builder sees the builder view. A liquidity provider sees the investor view. Someone with both roles picks one from the header's breadcrumb ("Dashboard / Builder"); the choice is remembered in this browser.

### The builder view

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Needs attention | A strip at the top: what needs you, most severe first, each with a severity, a title, a detail and a link to the Studio page that fixes it. With nothing to show, the strip isn't shown |
| Key figures | Money moved, Build spend, Hosting and Apps live, each with its change on the last period, then Average build cost and Average build time |
| Money moved and Costs | Two charts, one above the other, under one toolbar row: a search of apps by name, App, App stage and Date range. The toolbar narrows the charts only |
| Recent activity | The newest entries of the workspace's audit trail, linking to Audits |

Money moved is the gross of settled live movements through your apps. It is not earnings, which Mynt doesn't measure yet. A period Mynt has no figure for is a gap in the chart, never 0.

With no apps yet, the page says so and points to Build. Where the figures come from is in [Profit and loss](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#profit-and-loss) and [Attention](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#attention).

### The investor view

For liquidity providers, in the same style:

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Needs attention | Only the items about investing (pools, positions, deposits, withdrawals, the treasury), and only when there are any |
| Key figures | Committed, Settled, Pending in, Available to withdraw, Queued for withdrawal, Paid out, Pools held and Returns. Committed and Paid out carry their history. Returns is the wind-down surplus claimed on chain; pools on rails pay none. With both sources, a line under the figures splits them into Devnet and Rails |
| Toolbar | A search of pools by name, Pool, Source (Devnet or Rails) and Date range (the last six months to start). It narrows the two charts only |
| Capital in | A chart of on-chain deposits by when they settled |
| Paid out | A chart, under Capital in, of withdrawal requests' paid amounts by when they became payable |
| Recent financial activity | The ten newest entries of the financial class of the audit trail (when, kind, summary, status). **View all** opens `/audits?tab=financial` |

Positions, pools, withdrawals and wallets in detail are on [Earn](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#earn). A builder also has the wallet control in the page header.

A figure Mynt can't measure is a gap, never 0. Positions on rails carry no dated history, so with only those every period of both charts is a gap.

## Build

Build is the `/new` page and the **Build** button in every header. A labelled **Type** menu in the composer picks what is being built:

| Type | What it is |
|---|---|
| **App** | An app for customers, built on financial products |
| **Financial product** | A regulated product composed from primitives |
| **Service** | A service other builders plug in, listed in the Marketplace |

The choice is kept in the address (`?type=app`, `product` or `service`) and remembered in this browser. Links with `?product=` or `?thread=` open as before.

### Building an app

1. Describe what you want to build in the composer.
2. Pick the products it builds on, from the composer's Products picker or the **Products** tab. Both share one selection.
3. Send. Studio creates the app on the picked products in the selected workspace, starts its first build with your message as the goal, and opens the app's workspace on that build.

The first build runs on Mynt's own spend cap; Studio has no cap control. Until the message can be sent, the reason is the disabled Send button's tooltip. The same request sent twice creates one app.

The right side has two tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Templates** | App ideas for each of Mynt's app kinds. **Use** fills the composer and picks the idea's products. An idea with no published product to build on says so |
| **Products** | The products you may build on, and your own products with their stage |

A few ideas also show as chips under the composer. How app kinds and ideas work is in [Kinds and ideas on the Build page](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#kinds-and-ideas-on-the-build-page).

### Building a service

A service is the third kind of thing built on Mynt (see [Services](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/services.md)).

1. Pick **Service** in the Type menu.
2. Pick the service type and region, in place of the products picker. Each type shows the licence it needs. **Request a service type** asks Mynt's admins for one that doesn't exist (`request_service_type`).
3. Describe it and send. Studio creates the service (`create_service`), starts its first build, and opens `/services/<id>`.

The right side has two tabs: **Service types**, and **Requested service types** with each request's status.

A service needs the vendor role. Without it the Service choice stays visible, the page says "Ask a Mynt admin for the vendor role", and Send is disabled.

### The Products tab

Each product shows a flag for each country it is offered in and its stage (Idea, Staging or Production). A product can be picked for an app once it is in Staging (for sandbox builds) or Production.

On your own products, the row has the labelled actions for its stage:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Create product** | Opens one sheet with the product's fields. The new product is listed as an Idea |
| **Move to staging**, **Move to production** | Opens the approval sheet with Mynt's checks for the next stage |
| **Move back** | Moves the product to an earlier stage |
| **Archive**, **Unarchive** | Opens the archive sheet. The **Archived** filter lists your archived products |

Mynt's refusals, such as a licence or sponsorship that is needed, are shown in Mynt's words.

### Creating a financial product by chatting

In Financial product mode the chat is an assistant that drafts a product with you:

- It asks for what is missing, choosing only from Mynt's regions, regulators, categories and published products.
- Its draft shows in the chat as a card. **Review and create** opens the Create product sheet filled with the draft, every field editable. Confirming creates the product once.
- The Templates tab and the chips show product ideas here. A chip starts the chat with the idea; a row's **Use** opens the sheet filled with it.

`/create-product` in the composer switches to this mode, and `/build-app` switches back. `/create-product <description>` sent from App mode goes there with its description. A message in App mode that clearly asks for a product only offers **Create product instead**: what is sent in App mode is always a build.

A product created here opens its own [product workspace](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#the-product-workspace). Product chats are kept on Mynt for you, so they reopen in any browser you sign in from. See [Product ideas on the Build page](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-ideas-on-the-build-page).

### Builds

`/builds` lists every coding-agent build across your apps, newest first: key figures, then a table with search, filters for app and status, a date range and **Export CSV**. Cost and time are shown as measured, or "Not measured" with Mynt's reason. The page isn't in the sidebar; search finds it.

## The app workspace

Opening an app (`/<app id>`) shows the chat with Mynt's coding agent on the left and the app's tabs on the right. On a phone one side shows at a time.

### The chat

- A message steers the app's running build, or starts a new build with the message as its goal.
- The reply streams what the agent does: its words as it writes them, its commands and file edits as cards, and its reasoning as a collapsible block.
- While a session build is open, the composer has **Ship**, which finishes the build so Mynt can verify it.
- A message sent while the build is being verified is held ("Queued — sent when verification finishes.") and sent afterwards. It can be removed while it waits.
- Opening a past build rebuilds its conversation: its goal, the messages steered into it, its activity and how it ended.
- Only one build starts at a time per app, whoever starts it.

Typing `/` in the composer lists commands: one per tab (`/preview`, `/products`, `/agreements`, `/customers`, `/security`, `/pnl`, `/sdk`, `/activity`), `/risk` (the risk register, on Security & risk), `/ship`, `/fix` and `/add`.

How builds work is in [Coding-agent builds](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#coding-agent-builds).

### The app's tabs

Each tab is read live from Mynt for this app only: when it is opened, when the page comes back into view, and every 30 seconds while it is visible. It shows when it was last read and has **Refresh**.

| Tab | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Preview** | The app running: a build's live preview while it is being coded, else the preview Mynt made when it verified the build |
| **Products** | The products this app uses, each with its stage and the licence providers sponsoring it, by state. An app holds no licences of its own; its products do |
| **Agreements** | The program agreements Production needs, the app's agreements with firms, and its vendor contracts, with **Propose agreement** for owners and admins |
| **Customers** | The customer personas this app targets, from its products, and introductions in progress |
| **Security & risk** | The app's risk register (**Add risk**, **Review risk**; each risk with its inherent, control and residual scores, and a row opening [the risk's detail](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#a-risks-detail)), Mynt's build checks and security events, and the signals Mynt measures around the app: fraud, its vendors, conduct and its products |
| **P&L** | Money moved and costs for this app, with the statement |
| **SDK** | Each product's integration kit: action, access, permitted actions, fields, contract and hand-off |
| **Activity** | The app's builds and its audit events |

There is no Licences tab on an app. Licence coverage is on each product's Compliance tab, and agreements are on the app's Agreements tab and the [Licences](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#licences) page.

What the Agreements tab holds is described in [The app's Agreements tab](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#the-apps-agreements-tab), and the risk register in [Risk in Studio](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#risk-in-studio).

### The app's top bar

Inside an app, the page header is replaced by the app's own bar:

- **Back**, then the app's name and stage.
- The stage control: **Promote to Staging** or **Promote to Production** (the next stage only) and, for owners and admins of the workspace, **Move back**.
- The app's hosting state and **Put online**.
- The preview's controls: back, forward, reload, the path, its width (desktop, tablet or phone) and open in a new tab.
- The build's measured cost and time.
- Search, the GitHub and wallet controls, Build, Docs and the theme switcher, as in the page header.

### Promoting an app

**Promote to Staging** and **Promote to Production** open a side sheet with Mynt's checks for the next stage. Each check has a status in words (and a red, amber or green mark), its detail and its fix: a link to a Studio page, or the tool that does it.

- **Promote** is enabled only when Mynt says the app can be promoted and you are an owner or admin of the app's workspace. Members see the checks, and that an owner or admin promotes.
- When Mynt asks for a Mynt admin's sign-off, the sheet shows its status, with **Request admin sign-off** until it has been asked for.
- **Move back** goes only to an earlier stage, with a reason.

The checks themselves are in [Stages and promotion](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#stages-and-promotion). Production needs a signed program agreement with every sponsoring licence provider; see [Production needs program agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#production-needs-program-agreements).

### Put online in the top bar

The top bar shows where the app stands on Mynt's hosting: **Online at** its address (a link), **Deploying**, or **Not online**. Once the app has a build Mynt verified, it also has a labelled button:

| Button | When |
|---|---|
| **Put online** | The app isn't hosted yet |
| **Put the new build online** | The app runs an older build |
| **Hosting details** | The app already runs this build |

The sheet shows the build, the repository and commit it deploys, and what happens: Mynt's hosting builds exactly that commit on the app's own machine, the app gets its own public address, and its Mynt key is added at Mynt's edge, never stored on the app's machine.

A build that pushed to no repository can't be hosted. The sheet says so and offers **Choose repository**; the app's next build pushes there. The chat's composer offers the same **Put online** once a build has shipped. The full behaviour is in [Put online](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#put-online).

## The service workspace

A service's workspace is `/services/<id>`: the builder chat on the left, as for an app, and its tabs on the right.

### The service's header

The header shows the service's name, its stage and its offering's status in words (for example "Needs conformance" or "Listed in the Marketplace"). Its labelled actions:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Promote to Staging**, **Promote to Production** | Opens the approval sheet with Mynt's checks for a service. Production lists it in the Marketplace |
| **Move back** | Moves it to an earlier stage. Out of Production unlists it |
| **Put online** | Hosts its newest verified build. Mynt then tests that build itself |
| **Archive**, **Restore** | Opens a confirm sheet (`archive_service`) |

### The service's tabs

Each tab is a read view. Changes are the labelled buttons.

| Tab | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | The service's details (with the build serving, a new build being tested beside it, and whether it is open to sandbox testing, with the offering id to share) and its checklist, each step with its button: Put online, Ask the builder to add it, Run practice test, Run conformance, Set standard terms, Move to production. A blocked role step says to ask a Mynt admin |
| **Contract** | The service type and region; what it takes in and gives back, as field tables (Field, Type, Required, Description); the endpoint Mynt derives; the signing rule; fixtures |
| **Conformance** | Practice runs, real runs and tests of new builds that didn't take over, in one table (When, Kind, Build, Result, Cases passed, Run by). A row opens its cases, then its transcript as a table (Case, Mynt sent, It answered, Mynt expected), for practice runs too. **Run practice test** and **Run conformance** |
| **Terms & pricing** | The standard terms versions (Version, Scope, Summary, Pricing, Set on, Set by, the document). **Set standard terms** |
| **Subscribers** | Firm, App, Terms version accepted, Since, Live or sandbox, Agreement status. Shown to the offering firm's own people; a workspace member from another firm reads "Not shown" with the reason |
| **Reliability** | Calls, error rate, response time and incidents from Mynt's own records. A figure Mynt doesn't record reads "Not measured" with the reason, never 0 |
| **Security & risk** | The same view as an app's, for the service |
| **Activity** | Builds, deploys, stage moves, conformance runs and terms changes (When, What, Detail, By) |

A service has no Products, Agreements, Customers, P&L or SDK tab.

- **Ask the builder to add it** sends a prepared message into the service's chat: "Add Mynt's vendor service endpoint for <service type>".
- The Build column shows the build each real run tested. A run from before Mynt recorded it reads "Not recorded", unless it is the passing run that stands.
- A transcript leaves out the signing secret, the signature's digest and any credential. A run from before transcripts were kept says so instead of showing an empty one.
- A new build that failed Mynt's test reads "Conformance, new build" and "Didn't pass: removed". Its row opens what happened in words: the build that was serving kept serving.
- **Put online**, **Archive** and **Restore** are for the workspace's owners and admins at the firm that offers the service. Mynt refuses anyone else and says why.

## The product workspace

A financial product has its own workspace at `/products/<id>`, laid out like an app's: the product's chat on the left and its tabs on the right. It opens from the stage folders, from the Build page, and right after a product is created.

### The product's header

The header shows the product's name and stage, then the labelled actions, each opening its sheet:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Move to staging** | Opens the approval sheet with what Staging needs |
| **Move to production** | Opens the approval sheet with what Production needs |
| **Move back** | Moves the product to an earlier stage |
| **Archive** | Archives the product |
| **Unarchive** | Brings an archived product back |

What each stage needs and allows is in [Product stages](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-stages), and archiving in [Archiving a product](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#archiving-a-product).

### The product's tabs

Each tab is a list of sections, and each section a table. A section Mynt can't fill says why. Tabs are read live, as an app's are.

| Tab | Sections |
|---|---|
| **Terms** | From the product definition: Terms, Rates, Fees, Limits, Lifecycle events, Servicing policies and Costs |
| **Customers** | Customer segments, and Target market and eligibility |
| **Risk** | The product's risk register first (**Add risk**, **Review risk**; each risk with its inherent, control and residual scores, and a row opening [the risk's detail](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#a-risks-detail)), then Risk models, Decisioning and underwriting, Covenants, Open breaches, Sales paused by a covenant, and Product health |
| **Compliance** | Sponsorship, Regulatory obligations, Disclosures and documents, and What the next stage needs |
| **Integrations** | Partner hand-offs, Vendor services, Connections and Partner ledger |
| **Apps** | Apps built on this product, each linking to its app workspace |
| **Activity** | Versions, and Stage moves, drift and archiving |

### The product's chat

The chat is the product chat whose draft created the product. A product made without a chat gets a new one. It is kept on Mynt, as the Build page's product chats are. Its slash commands show the tabs (`/terms`, `/customers`, `/risk`, `/compliance`, `/integrations`, `/apps`, `/activity`).

## Licences

Licences (`/licences`) is where builders and licence providers work on their agreements with each other. It has four tabs:

| Tab | Address | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Business Agreements** | `/licences` | Program and data-sharing agreements |
| **MSA** | `/licences?tab=msa` | Master services agreements (MSAs), and a licence provider's agreement templates |
| **SLA** | `/licences?tab=sla` | Service-level agreements (SLAs), with their commitments and breaches |
| **Audit Obligations** | `/licences?tab=audit-obligations` | The oversight audits licence providers run on apps, read-only |

Every tab is open to both roles and shows your side: a licence provider sees its firm's agreements, a builder the selected workspace's, and someone with both roles sees both, each row saying its side.

### Agreements on the first three tabs

Business Agreements, MSA and SLA are one list over their kinds of agreement:

- A full-width search, **Filters** (status, kind where the tab has more than one, scope, and your side when you are on both), a Proposed date range, **Import** (disabled, saying why) and **Export CSV**.
- Columns for the app, the other party, products, kind, scope, status, effective dates, document and actions.
- The tab's own action: **Propose agreement**, **Propose MSA** or **Propose SLA**. Either side proposes. A licence provider may start from one of its templates.
- The other side accepts or declines, and both sign, by e-signature where it is set up. While your own proposal is still proposed, **Change scope** changes what it covers.

A row opens **Review agreement**: a card of the agreement's details, the labelled actions for your side (Accept, Decline, Withdraw, Change scope, Sign, End agreement, Download signed copy), then tabs, each a table: Products and Signatures, and on an SLA, **Commitments** and **Breaches** (with Add commitment, Record breach, Retire commitment and Resolve breach).

Under the MSA table, a licence provider has **Agreement templates**, with **Upload agreement template** and **Retire**.

### Where licence coverage went

The licence table and coverage map are no longer on this page. Licence coverage is on each product's Compliance tab. The old addresses (`/coverage`, `?view=`, `?tab=coverage`, `?tab=licences`) come back to `/licences`, and `?tab=agreements` opens Business Agreements.

The rules behind agreements are in [Agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md), and this page is described from the agreements side in [The Licences page](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#the-licences-page).

## Marketplace

Marketplace (`/marketplace`) lists standard services from vendors, which Studio calls service providers. Each service is offered under the vendor's standard terms. A workspace subscribes by accepting them: there is no negotiation, the vendor bills directly, and Mynt never bills or holds money for it.

- The list has a full-width search, one **Filters** popover (region, category and service type), **Import** and **Export CSV**, over a table paged 25 rows at a time.
- A row opens its details in a side panel: a card of the key facts, then the tabs Overview, Standard terms, Pricing, Prerequisites, Conformance and Regions, each a table.
- **Subscribe** opens the Subscribe sheet: you pick the apps the service is for, tick that you accept the standard terms, and confirm. Mynt checks again that the terms are the current version and that you are an owner or admin of each app's workspace.

See [The marketplace and standard terms](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#the-marketplace-and-standard-terms).

## My services

My services (`/vendor`) is a vendor's own area, shown only to accounts with the vendor role.

- **The onboarding checklist** is a card at the top: the firm's steps, then each service's. Every step has its status in words, what it waits on, and a labelled button where Studio can do it: **Create service**, **Edit service**, **Run conformance**, **Set standard terms** or **List service**. Steps only Mynt can do say what they wait for.
- **The firm's services** are a list below it: a full-width search, **Import**, **Export CSV** and **Create service**, over a paged table.
- A service opens its details: a card with its labelled actions, then the tabs Conformance runs, Terms versions and Subscribers, each a table.

See [Onboarding a vendor](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#onboarding-a-vendor).

Services built on Mynt are listed here too, marked "Built on Mynt". Such a row opens the service's workspace at `/services/<id>`; other rows open their details as before. A **Requested service types** table shows the status of each service type you asked Mynt for, with a **Request a service type** button.

## My firm

My firm (`/firm`) is a regulated firm's own area. It is shown only to accounts Mynt granted the licence-provider role, with standing at their firm. A Mynt admin's roles imply the role without a firm, so an admin sees My firm only when the role was also granted.

From top to bottom:

- **The firm's card**: its status, regions, LEI, FinCEN MSB registration number, NMLS ID, whether it can sponsor now, and its firm id to share with builders. One line says where the real-company check stands, in words with a mark, and when the registers were last asked. **Set firm facts** opens a sheet for the three identifiers. The firm's other identifiers are kept as they are, and its legal name is Mynt's to correct.
- **The onboarding checklist**, "Getting ready to sponsor": every step has its status in words, what it waits on, and a labelled button where Studio can do it (**Set firm facts**, **Register licence**, **Add party**, **Review request**). Steps only Mynt can do say what they wait for.
- **Six tabs**, each a list: a full-width search, **Import** (disabled, saying why), **Export CSV** and the tab's own action, over a paged table.

| Tab | Address | Shows | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Licences** | `/firm` | The firm's licences: type, regulator, where it was issued, number, dates, status in words, where it covers, sponsorships under it | **Register licence**: the licence type from the regulatory model for the firm's regions, its number, the state where the type is issued per state, and its dates |
| **Sponsorship requests** | `/firm?tab=requests` | Requests waiting for a decision, then approved sponsorships: product, component, builder, where asked and approved | **Review request** on a waiting one (Approve sponsorship or Decline request, with a note); **Revoke sponsorship** on an approved one, with a reason |
| **Sponsored products** | `/firm?tab=sponsored` | Every approved sponsorship: the product and whether it is live or drifted, the component, the builder, the licences and where. Read-only | |
| **Roster** | `/firm?tab=roster` | Required roles nobody fills, then the parties and what each fills | **Add party**, also on each unfilled role's row; **End party** |
| **People** | `/firm?tab=people` | Licence providers, other members, accounts waiting to be accepted, and people invited who haven't signed in | **Decide** on a waiting account (Accept member or Decline member) |
| **Notices** | `/firm?tab=notices` | What changed at the firm, newest first. Read-only. Opening the tab marks them read | |

Review request says so when the real-company check hasn't passed: Approve sponsorship is off, with the reason, and Decline request still works.

Mynt acts for the caller's own firm in every one of these, and Studio's routes check that a sponsorship, licence, party or member request belongs to that firm before they send anything. Mynt's refusals are shown in its own words: an admin account can't revoke a sponsorship or decide who joins, even one that belongs to the firm.

Still done with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools: a party's qualification facts, a covenant breach on a revocation, the partner kit and the firm's webhooks. Agreement templates are on [Licences](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#licences).

See [Onboarding a regulated firm](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#onboarding-a-regulated-firm).

## Audits

Audits (`/audits`) sorts the workspace's records into five tabs. Each is its own table with one toolbar row: a full-width search, the tab's filters as compact controls, and **Export CSV**. A filter that is on shows on its control ("Status · overdue").

| Tab | Address | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **App security** | `/audits` | Build audits and their findings, program gate results and vulnerability flags, with severity and status |
| **Licence obligations** | `/audits?tab=obligations` | Each licence's regulatory obligations for the products it covers: met, at risk or overdue, with evidence |
| **Agreement audits** | `/audits?tab=agreements` | The oversight audits licence providers run on the workspace's apps under program agreements |
| **Financial activity** | `/audits?tab=financial` | Money movements, live transactions, liquidity commitments and withdrawals, rail use and refusals |
| **Workspace activity** | `/audits?tab=workspace` | Membership, roles, keys and settings |

App security, Financial activity and Workspace activity are the workspace's audit trail by class. Mynt filters them by kind, member, app and date range, a page at a time.

### Licence obligations

Each row is one obligation in the regulator's own terms: the licence provider by name, the regulator and licence type, a status (met, at risk, overdue or unknown, as a dot and the word), the reason an unknown one is unknown, a due date and a summary of the evidence. It filters by licence provider, regulator, status and product. When any agreement audits are overdue it shows a line with **Show overdue agreement audits**.

### Agreement audits

Agreement audits are a tab of their own so that the regulator's obligations keep their register's schema.

- Rows: the agreement, the app, the audit with its cadence, its kind, due date, status in words (with "Overdue" beside it when it is past due and not closed) and findings ("1 open of 2").
- Filters: agreement, counterparty, app, kind and status. The date range is the due date. `?agreement=<id>` opens the tab filtered to one agreement.
- A row opens a sheet: a card of the audit's details, your actions as labelled buttons, then the tabs Findings, Evidence and History.

| Who | Actions |
|---|---|
| A licence provider | **Open audit**, **Record finding**, **Resolve finding**, **Pass**, **Fail**, **Waive**, and **Add audit requirement** in the toolbar |
| The app's owners and admins | **Submit evidence** (an `https` link with its SHA-256) and **Respond to finding** |

The rules are in [Oversight audits](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#oversight-audits) and [Compliance and the audit trail](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#compliance-and-the-audit-trail).

## Earn

Earn (`/earn`) is for liquidity pools. Builders and liquidity providers see it. It is laid out like an app's workspace: an assistant on the left and tables on the right.

One line sits under the composer: "Not investment advice · Mynt never holds your funds". Amounts are US dollars.

### The assistant

The assistant starts as "What do you want to earn?" with example chips. It reads only what you may see (pools, their health, your positions and withdrawals) and is never able to move anything.

- It can show matching pools in the Pools tab.
- It can draft a commitment or a withdrawal. A draft is only a card. Nothing is sent until you click **Review** and then **Approve**.
- **Past conversations**, the round button at the chat's top right, lists your earlier Earn conversations, newest first, with **New conversation** at the top. They are kept on Mynt for you (at most 200), so they reopen in any browser.
- Its slash commands are `/pools`, `/strategies`, `/history` and `/new` for everyone; `/invested`, `/commit` and `/withdraw` for liquidity providers; `/my-pools` and `/propose` for builders.

Without a model configured, the assistant says "AI is not configured" and the tables still work.

### The tabs in Earn

| Tab | Address | Who | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pools** | `/earn?tab=pools` | Everyone on Earn | Every pool open to you, with a **Matched · All · Invested** switch |
| **My pools** | `/earn?tab=my-pools` | Builders | Your firm's products' pools |
| **My strategies** | `/earn?tab=my-strategies` | Everyone on Earn | What the assistant drafted, each with its approval status, **Review** and **Decline** |

Each tab has one toolbar row: search, one **Filters** button counting what is picked ("Filters · 2", with **Clear all** in its popover), **Export CSV** and the tab's action.

**Pools.** Each row shows the pool's product line, state, lock-in or notice period, minimum reserve, verified health, whether it is sandbox or cleared for real money, and its commitment limits. Yield reads "Not available yet", because Mynt doesn't measure it. A liquidity provider never sees its own firm's pools here.

- **Commit capital** takes dollars and the US state the capital moves from. It is disabled, with the reason, outside the pool's limits, before approval, while the pool is paused or closed, and for a real pool that isn't cleared ("Sandbox only — not yet cleared for real commitments").
- A row where you hold a position shows **Your position** (settled), queued and paid amounts, and any withdrawal requests still waiting. **Invested** lists only those pools.
- **Details** opens a sheet with the position's committed, settled, queued, paid and available amounts, and your firm's withdrawal requests with their place in the queue, earliest payment date and why each waits.
- **Withdraw** opens **Request withdrawal**, which shows the notice period, and that payment is first in, first out and only as far as the latest verified health snapshot keeps the pool above its minimum reserve.

**My pools.** Each pool shows its state (proposed and awaiting the licence provider's approval, sandbox, sandbox only until cleared, or cleared), status, rails, minimum reserve, notice period, commitment limits, latest health snapshot and withdrawal queue length. The **Approval** column shows its steps: Proposed, Sponsor approved, Admin approved (skipped for sandbox), Open. Mynt doesn't show a pool's capital to its builder, so that column says so. **Propose pool** is offered only on a component an approved licence provider sponsors.

### Approvals

Approvals look the same everywhere: a status as a dot and its words ("Needs your approval", "Sign in wallet", "Sending…", "Sent", "Declined", "Failed"), and steps. **Review** opens the approval sheet: the steps, a summary of what will happen (amount, pool, terms, the wallet, and the reserve and notice effects), then **Approve**, which sends it once, and **Decline**.

### The wallet picker

The wallet picker sits in the composer's toolbar. It lists your verified linked wallets with their devnet USDC and SOL balances, or "Not measured". **Connect wallet** lists the wallets found in this browser; connecting signs nothing. **Link wallet** goes to your account page. The choice is remembered in this browser.

### On-chain deposits and withdrawals

A pool with an on-chain treasury shows "On-chain treasury" and **Devnet**. Studio offers on-chain deposits on devnet only.

1. A draft for the pool names your wallet and shows **Deposit from** that wallet (or, for a withdrawal, **Withdraw to** it).
2. Clicking it asks Mynt to prepare the transaction. The card shows Mynt's own summary: pool, amount, wallet, lock-in, notice and expiry.
3. **Sign in** your wallet hands the unsigned transaction to your own browser wallet, which must be connected to exactly the chosen linked wallet. Your wallet signs and sends it. Nothing in Studio signs.
4. The card shows the signature and follows the transaction until it is confirmed, then reads positions and balances again.

Other things the card says:

- **Unverified build**, when the pool's treasury program isn't a build Mynt verified.
- **Deposits paused: approvers changed**, when Mynt flagged that the treasury's approvers changed on chain. Deposits to it are refused.
- "Refreshing…", when the transaction was prepared more than 45 seconds before signing and is prepared again. It is signed only if Mynt's new summary is the same; otherwise the new summary is shown to confirm.
- Mynt's refusals in plain words, with the date Mynt names for a deposit in review or locked in.

An on-chain position shows what is held, queued and available, then each deposit on its own line with when it unlocks. **Withdraw** on an available deposit opens an amount in USDC and the same flow, for that deposit only.

How pools, the queue and treasuries work is in [Liquidity pools and on-chain treasuries](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md).

## Settings

Settings (`/settings`) is the selected workspace's page. It has four tabs, each a table with one toolbar row (a full-width search, labelled actions and the tab's own action), paged 25 rows at a time.

| Tab | Address | What it shows and does |
|---|---|---|
| **Members** | `/settings` | The workspace's members. Owners and admins invite by email (**Invite member**, as admin or member), change roles and remove members. Everyone else sees the list only. Ownership isn't changed from here |
| **Invitations** | `/settings?tab=invitations` | Pending invitations, which owners and admins withdraw (**Withdraw**). Mynt shows them only to owners and admins |
| **Apps** | `/settings?tab=apps` | Every app in the workspace with its stage, owner, last build and links |
| **Repositories** | `/settings?tab=repositories` | Your own connected GitHub repositories, each with its approval and note, and **Connect repository** |

There is no General tab. Renaming and archiving a workspace are in [the workspace switcher's menu](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#the-workspace-switcher). An unknown tab in the address, or the old General tab (`?tab=settings`), opens Members. The old addresses `/workspace` and `/members` open Settings.

E-signature is not set up here. It is in the platform admin, under Platform settings; `/settings?tab=esign` redirects there.

The rules are in [Members and invitations](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#members-and-invitations) and [Repositories](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#repositories).

## Platform admin

The platform admin (`/platform`) is for Mynt admins only. It has its own layout, not Studio's: its own sidebar with eight sections (Overview, Workspaces, Regulated firms, Vendors, Audit trails, Risk models, Risk register and Platform settings) and **Back to Studio** at its foot. Licences are reviewed inside Regulated firms, on its Licences tab (`/platform/firms?tab=licences`).

In Studio, only accounts Mynt says hold the `admin` role get the **Platform admin** entry above their name in the sidebar. For everyone else `/platform` is a 404.

Each section is described in [The platform admin in Studio](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#the-platform-admin-in-studio). Three of its pages are about risk:

| Page | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `/platform/risk-register/<id>` | One risk in full: Mynt's own, or an app's or a product's opened from the register's table (read-only). See [A risk's detail](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md#a-risks-detail) |
| `/platform/risk-models/<id>` | One of Mynt's risk models, with its health in words and the risks linked to it |
| `/platform/settings` | [Platform settings](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#platform-settings), four tabs that are each one table: Key vault, Operational settings, E-signature and Risk grading |

## Docs and search

### Docs

The **Docs** button in every header opens `/docs`: Mynt's documentation, built from this repository's Markdown and from the server's own tool list. It is public, so it opens without signing in. Signed in, it shows inside Studio's sidebar and header.

`/connect` is the docs' page for connecting your own MCP client to Mynt, with a picker for the client you use.

### Search

The header's search box ("Search...", with its ⌘K key; an icon button named Search on a phone) opens the command bar. So does Cmd+K, or Ctrl+K.

- With nothing typed it lists Studio's pages, the workspace's apps and your financial products, each under its section's heading, and a **Members** and an **Audit actions** entry that open their own lists.
- Typing finds any of them, and also what sits under them: an app's tabs (shown as "the app › the tab"), members and audit actions.
- Arrow keys move, Enter opens, Esc closes (or steps back out of a list). The bar's foot says so.
- Mynt admins also find the platform admin's sections there.

Search has a **Services** group, beside apps and products, and finds a service's tabs by what they hold.

### Ask AI

Type a question in the command bar and **Ask AI** is the first result: a few words, or one word ending in a question mark, of at least 6 characters. Enter closes the bar and opens the Ask AI panel with that question already asked.

**The panel** is a fixed size: 60% of the screen's height and a third of its width, centred, and never narrower than 22rem. Below the `sm` breakpoint (640px) it fills the screen. It has a header (**New chat**, close), the conversation, which scrolls, and the question field pinned at the foot.

- **Asking.** Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. The field grows to five lines and takes 400 characters, with a count near the limit. While an answer is coming, **Send** is **Stop**.
- **Follow-ups.** Each new question is answered with the conversation so far (the last 20 turns, as text). **New chat** clears it. The conversation is kept in memory for the visit: close the panel and the bar offers "Ask AI: back to the conversation". Nothing is kept after you leave the page.
- **Steps.** Above each answer, one line says what Ask AI is doing ("Reading apps and their stages…") and then what it took ("Used 3 reads · Thought for 6s"). It opens into the steps in order: the model's thinking as it wrote it (nothing is shown when the model returned none), and each read with its name in words, the tool's name, its arguments, whether it is running, done or failed (with Mynt's message), how long it took and what it returned ("4 apps"). **Show result** opens the read's reply as JSON, cut to 4,000 characters, with anything that looks like a secret replaced.
- **Citations.** Every statement of fact cites a numbered source. A source is the record the fact came from where Studio has a page for it (an app, an audit action's filtered trail), and otherwise the page that holds the read. Each answer numbers its own sources. A citation is a small chip: hover or focus shows the source's title and when it was read, and a click opens it and closes the panel. The sources are listed under the answer. A citation with no source is dropped, and an answer with a statement that cites nothing says "Some statements have no source." Nothing is added to the answer for it.
- **Copy answer** copies the answer's text. **Ask again** re-asks the last question in its place.
- The answer follows the stream as it is written. Scroll up and it stops following; **Jump to latest** brings it back.
- Ask AI reads through Mynt's tools as you, never with an app key, and only with read tools.
- Questions and answers are never logged, and the conversation is never stored: the browser sends it again with each follow-up.
- You may ask 20 questions an hour, one at a time; a follow-up is a question. Past that it says so.
- The answer comes from the first model that answers: the configured model, then the fallback model.
- With no model configured the bar has no Ask AI entry, and search keeps working.

The platform admin's search has its own Ask AI, for Mynt admins. See [Search and Ask AI](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#search-and-ask-ai).

pages.title: Licences & partners
pages.markdown:
## Licence providers and sponsorship

A builder needn't hold licences. A licence provider is a firm that does.

### Setting up a licence provider

1. A Mynt admin adds the firm by hand: `register_firm`, `invite_user` with the `license_provider` role, and `add_entity_member`. Someone who hasn't signed in yet joins the firm when they first do.
2. The firm registers its licences with `register_license`.
3. A Mynt admin verifies them with `review_license`, as for any firm.

The firm's people share its firm id with builders out of band. There is no directory of firms.

`get_regulated_firm_onboarding` shows the firm, and Mynt's admins, how far along it is: see [Onboarding a regulated firm](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#onboarding-a-regulated-firm).

### Asking and deciding

1. **The builder names the licence provider** as a component's provider: `{ by: "sponsor", entity_id }` in `set_product_composition`, or `component_provided_by` set to `{ kind: "sponsor", id }` in a v2 product definition.
2. **The builder asks** with `request_sponsorship`: the product, the component, the licence provider's firm id and the jurisdictions (by default, where the component is offered). One request may be pending per component and licence provider. Asking again later adds jurisdictions.
3. **The licence provider decides.** `approve_sponsorship` names its held licences, which must be verified and in force, and the jurisdictions they cover. `decline_sponsorship` refuses. `revoke_sponsorship` withdraws an approved sponsorship.

A registration that covers nowhere by itself, like the FinCEN registration, isn't named in `approve_sponsorship`. It counts automatically as the named licences' prerequisite.

### Sponsorship tools

A sponsorship's status is `pending`, `approved`, `declined` or `revoked`.

| Tool | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request_sponsorship` | Builder | Asks a licence provider to sponsor one component |
| `list_my_sponsorships` | Builder | The firm's requests and their status, with `covenant_pauses` |
| `list_my_licenses` | Licence provider | The licences the firm holds, whether each is in force, where it covers, and the approved sponsorships under it |
| `list_sponsorship_requests` | Licence provider | Builders' requests (pending by default), with the firm's own `your_firm_legitimacy` |
| `approve_sponsorship`, `decline_sponsorship` | Licence provider | Decide a request |
| `revoke_sponsorship` | Licence provider | Withdraws an approved sponsorship; takes an optional `breach_id` |
| `list_sponsored_products` | Licence provider | Every approved sponsorship by the firm |

### The regime rule

A sponsored component is covered in a jurisdiction only by a licence of that licence provider which meets all of these:

- an approved sponsorship names it for that jurisdiction;
- it is verified and in force;
- it grants the component;
- it covers the jurisdiction;
- the licence provider's own prerequisites are held.

Anywhere else the component is blocked ("Ramp Partner Inc (sponsor) doesn't sponsor this in us-ca"). With no approved sponsorship at all it is blocked everywhere.

A builder with no licence and no sponsoring licence provider is blocked too ("Your entity holds no verified licence granting this").

### Mandated stakeholders

Mandated stakeholders are the licensee's. The regulatory model attaches them to the licence type, and the licence is the licence provider's, so they must be filled on the licence provider's roster. This is enforced: a gap blocks publishing, as it does for the owner's own licences.

They aren't bound to the builder's product, since they aren't on the builder's roster. The builder still names its own `product_owner`.

### Pins and drift

Publishing pins each covering sponsorship (with the jurisdictions it covers), the licence provider's licences and its stakeholder parties, and the licence provider's firm.

Revoking the sponsorship, or the licence provider's licence lapsing or being suspended, drifts the product, naming the jurisdictions.

The stored `regime_summary` shows `provided_by: "sponsor"`, the licence provider's name, and on each covered jurisdiction a note such as "Covered by Ramp Partner Inc's Money transmitter licence (New York Banking Law Article 13-B) (sponsored)".

### What test_product says about licences

`test_product` doesn't warn a builder that holds no licence when it needn't hold one:

- If the builder provides no component itself and every component is covered by a sponsoring licence provider (or a partner), `licence_held` passes and names who covers what ("Example Money Transmitter (placeholder) sponsors 'transmission' in us-ny, us-ca").
- While a sponsorship is still pending, it warns only that the composition isn't covered yet. The reason says the request is waiting for the licence provider's decision, not to ask again.
- A builder providing a component itself is still warned when it holds no licence.

## Firm checks

Is the licence provider a real company? Mynt checks it itself, against public sources, and never takes the firm's word for it.

### Running the checks

- A Mynt admin runs the checks with `run_firm_checks` (entity id).
- Every licence provider's firm is re-checked monthly (`FIRM_CHECKS_EVERY_DAYS`, default 30). A source that was down is retried daily.

Each answer is kept, newest first, with its source, URL, `retrieved_at`, the fields it matched, a status and a SHA-256 hash of the answer in a stable form, so a changed record shows as a changed hash. The status is `match`, `mismatch`, `not_found` or `unavailable`.

### Sources

**`gleif_lei`: GLEIF's LEI record**

- What Mynt asks: `GET https://api.gleif.org/api/v1/lei-records/<LEI>`, using the firm's `lei` identifier. A malformed LEI is never sent.
- Matched against the firm's legal name, its jurisdiction (GLEIF's `US-DE` against its incorporation), the entity's status (`ACTIVE`) and the LEI's status.
- LEI statuses that count: `ISSUED`, `PENDING_TRANSFER` or `PENDING_ARCHIVAL`. `LAPSED`, `RETIRED` and the rest are a lapse.
- The registration authority and number are recorded.
- Terms: free, no key. The data is CC0 ([LEI Data Terms of Use](https://www.gleif.org/en/meta/lei-data-terms-of-use)).

**`fincen_msb`: FinCEN's MSB Registrant Search list**

- What Mynt asks: the list's own "View/download … in Excel" export at [msb.fincen.gov](https://msb.fincen.gov/). It is tab-separated text, holds every current registrant and is updated weekly. One download serves six hours of checks.
- Matched against the firm's legal name, and the registrant's state against the states of the firm's legal and head-office addresses in its matching LEI record. Without an LEI record, a single registrant of that name matches; several are `not_found` rather than a guess.
- Terms: a US government record. FinCEN offers the export "for the benefit of the financial institutions … to integrate into their data processing systems". Mynt fetches only that file, never the search pages.

Requests go through Mynt's outbound helper (`core/src/vendor-call.ts`: HTTPS only, no private addresses, no redirects, a time limit and a size cap) to those two fixed hosts only.

### What is verified by hand

Two things are not fetched:

- The FinCEN list carries no registration numbers.
- NMLS Consumer Access has no API anyone may use, and its terms forbid downloading what it shows. NMLS's paid B2B Access is the sanctioned route.

So the firm's FinCEN registration number (identifier `us_fincen_msb`, or its registered FinCEN licence) and its NMLS ID (identifier `us_nmls`) are listed under `verify_by_hand` with the page to check them on. The firm's state licences stay verified by a Mynt admin with `review_license`.

### The rule

`approve_sponsorship` is refused until the licence provider's firm passes the rule set by `SPONSOR_LEGITIMACY_RULE` on the server:

| Value | A licence provider may sponsor when |
| --- | --- |
| `lei_or_msb` (default) | its latest LEI answer or its latest FinCEN answer is a `match`, and neither is a mismatch or a lapse |
| `lei_and_msb` | both are a `match`, with no mismatch or lapse |
| `lei` or `msb` | that one is a `match`, with no mismatch or lapse |
| `off` | always: no gate and no drift. For staging with the placeholder firm only, which isn't a real company |

How answers count:

- "Latest" skips `unavailable` answers. An outage keeps the last real answer and is never held against the firm.
- A lapse is a source that matched before and now finds nothing (the firm dropped off FinCEN's list), or an LEI whose status lapsed.
- Answers count only for the firm's current facts. A new LEI or legal name needs a fresh run.
- The refusal says which checks failed and what to do.

`get_regulated_firm_onboarding` says where the check stands before anyone tries to approve (see [Onboarding a regulated firm](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#onboarding-a-regulated-firm)). `get_my_entity`, the admin's `list_entities` and each of `list_sponsorship_requests` show the result as `legitimacy` (`your_firm_legitimacy` in the requests): whether it passes, why not, each source's latest status, URL and time, and what to verify by hand.

### Drift from a failed check

A mismatch or lapse found later drifts every published product the firm sponsors, as its licence lapsing would. The change has `kind: "legitimacy"`, the firm's id, `now` naming the flags (`flagged:fincen_msb:lapsed`), and the jurisdictions its sponsorships covered. A later match clears it.

Nothing extra is pinned, so products published before these checks existed are covered too.

### Paid checks later

A state's Secretary of State good standing, officers and registered agent need a paid source. The US region has a `kyb_business_verification` service type for that (`core/schemas/service-types/us/`; vendors such as Middesk or Baselayer can offer it once it is wired in). It is data only for now: nothing calls it.

## Onboarding a regulated firm

`get_regulated_firm_onboarding` shows where a regulated firm (a licence provider's firm) stands on the way to sponsoring, as one ordered checklist. It only reads. Each step is done with the tools it names, which decide as before.

| Caller | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| A licence provider of the firm, with standing there | Their firm's: no arguments, or their own `entity_id` |
| A Mynt admin | Any firm's (`entity_id`), and every regulated firm's progress (`all_firms: true`: firms with a licence provider, with one invited who hasn't signed in yet, or with a sponsorship request) |

A licence provider reads only its own firm. An account still waiting to be accepted at its firm has no standing, so it doesn't have the tool. Builders, vendors, liquidity providers and consumers don't have it either.

### Steps and their statuses

Each step has a `key`, a `title`, a `status`, a `detail` in plain words, the `tool` that does it, `by` (`firm`, `admin` or `builder`), `informational` and `facts`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `done` | The step is complete |
| `next` | The first thing the firm's own people can do now. At most one |
| `not_started` | The firm's to do, after the next one |
| `blocked` | Waiting on Mynt, on a public register, or on an earlier step. The detail says which, for example "Waiting for Mynt to verify your licence fincen_msb 31000123456789" |

While the firm isn't `active`, and before it has a licence provider, nobody there can act: every step not yet done is `blocked`, and its detail starts with what it waits for.

### The regulated firm's checklist

Seven steps count towards progress, in this order:

| Step | Done when | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `firm_registered` | The firm is on Mynt and `active` | Blocked on an admin (`register_firm`, `set_entity_status`) |
| `licence_provider_members` | Someone at the firm has the licence-provider role, with standing (`facts.members`, and `facts.licence_providers` by name). The detail also counts those waiting to be accepted (`facts.waiting`, decided with `decide_firm_member`) and those invited who haven't signed in (`facts.invited`) | Blocked on an admin (`invite_user`, `add_entity_member`). "Mynt invited 1 person with the licence-provider role. Waiting for them to sign in" when they were added before signing in |
| `firm_facts` | The firm's record has what the rule looks it up by: its LEI (identifier `lei`), its FinCEN MSB registration number (identifier `us_fincen_msb`, or its registered FinCEN licence), or both, by `SPONSOR_LEGITIMACY_RULE`. Also done when the check already passed on the legal name alone, and when the rule is `off` | Next: `set_entity_facts`. An LEI that isn't a valid LEI is said as such |
| `real_company_check` | The firm passes [the rule](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#the-rule): the detail names each register that matches, and when | Blocked, on Mynt or the register. Not run yet: waiting for an admin's `run_firm_checks` (it also runs monthly). A register that couldn't be reached is "unavailable, not a failure", with the date, and never counts against the firm. Not passed: each register's answer in words, and that `approve_sponsorship` is refused until it passes |
| `licences_registered` | The firm has a licence registered that Mynt hasn't rejected (`facts.registered`) | Next: `register_license` |
| `licences_verified` | A licence is verified and in force. The detail also counts those waiting, suspended, lapsed or not verified | Blocked while Mynt verifies (`review_license`) or has suspended one. Register again when one lapsed or wasn't verified, with Mynt's note |
| `roster_complete` | Every stakeholder the held licences mandate is filled on the roster by a party that meets its criteria (`facts.mandated`, `facts.filled`) | Next: `add_party`. The detail names what is still needed ("AML compliance officer (a person, for fincen_msb)"); `facts.missing` lists each with its licence and stakeholder id |

Three more are informational. They are shown, never counted, and never `next`:

| Step | Says |
| --- | --- |
| `partner_ledger` | Whether Mynt reads the firm's own ledger or the sandbox. Sponsoring doesn't wait for it: Mynt reads the sandbox until the ledger is connected (see [Partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit)) |
| `agreement_template` | How many program agreement templates are in use. Optional (see [E-signature](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#e-signature)) |
| `first_sponsorship` | How many sponsorships are approved and how many requests wait (`facts.approved`, `facts.pending`). While the real-company check hasn't passed, it says an approval would be refused, before anyone tries |

With `SPONSOR_LEGITIMACY_RULE` set to `off`, `firm_facts` and `real_company_check` are done, and `facts.passes` is `null`: not measured, never a pass.

### What comes with the checklist

- `progress` counts the steps done out of the seven counted, names the `next` one (the firm's own first, else what waits on Mynt) and says whether it is `complete`.
- `ready_to_sponsor` is true when the firm is active, has a licence provider, passes the real-company check and holds a licence in force: what `approve_sponsorship` needs of the firm itself.
- `legitimacy` is the same result `get_my_entity` shows.
- `checks` lists every answer the public registers gave about the firm, newest first, up to 50: the register, its status in words, when, any note, and whether it was Mynt's own monthly re-check.

With `all_firms`, each firm has its name and status, the number of licence providers, licences and approved sponsorships, whether the real-company check passes, `ready_to_sponsor` and `progress`.

A figure Mynt doesn't measure (a firm not yet registered, a check that is off) is `null`, never 0.

### My firm in Studio

Mynt Studio shows the checklist to licence providers as My firm (`/firm`, in the sidebar only for accounts granted the licence-provider role; an admin's roles only imply it):

- the firm's card, with the real-company check's latest result in words and **Set firm facts**;
- the checklist, titled "Getting ready to sponsor", each step's status in words with a labelled button where Studio can do it: Set firm facts, Register licence, Add party, Review request;
- the tabs Licences, Sponsorship requests, Sponsored products, Roster, People and Notices, each a table.

See [My firm](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#my-firm). The platform admin's Regulated firms section shows each firm's progress and its real-company check, with Run checks (see [Regulated firms section](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#regulated-firms-section)).

## Covenants

A licence provider watches each product it sponsors and pulls its licence on bad behaviour it can see. It says what bad behaviour is: each covenant is a rule on one sponsorship, set by that firm alone. Each rule chooses whether a breach only **alerts** the firm or also **pauses** the product.

### Rules

| Rule (`rule_type`) | Threshold | Breached when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coverage_below` | basis points | coverage is under it |
| `reversal_rate_above`, `failure_rate_above` | basis points | the rate is over it |
| `unresolved_above` | cents | unresolved money is over it |
| `complaints_above` | a count | over it. Mynt doesn't track complaints yet, so this rule reads `unknown` until it does |
| `snapshot_missed_for` | seconds (at least two snapshot intervals) | no authenticated snapshot with real figures has arrived for longer than this. A missed period, a failed ledger read and a report that can't be authenticated don't count |
| `consecutive_gaps` | periods (at least 1) | this many periods in a row have no snapshot, counting a stretch the worker never wrote down |
| `unverified_for` | seconds (at least two snapshot intervals) | a live product has had no valid co-signature from this licence provider for longer than this |

Notes on `unverified_for`:

- Only time the product was live counts. A blip off sale of up to about one snapshot interval counts as live. So a relaunch doesn't breach at once, and publishing again doesn't restart the count.
- A licence provider whose books aren't the latest snapshot's reads `unknown` (only that firm can sign), and alerts through the unknown limit.

Each rule also has:

- a `severity`: `info`, `warning` or `critical`;
- a `cooldown_seconds`: the least time between alerts of that rule, default a day;
- an `unknown_limit_seconds`: default a day.

### When rules are evaluated

- On every new health snapshot.
- On their own timer (`COVENANT_POLL_MS`, default a minute). The timer runs whether or not the product-health worker is deployed, so a rule about missing snapshots fires even when the worker has never run.

A rule changed with `set_covenant` takes effect from the next evaluation, which re-judges the latest snapshot. A product that isn't live isn't evaluated and raises no alarms. Evaluation covers a product's own record, not a pool's.

### Unknown is not a pass and not a breach

These all read `unknown`, with the reason:

- a figure Mynt can't measure;
- a missed period;
- a report Mynt can't authenticate;
- another licence provider's books (a licence provider reads only its own).

Further rules:

- A figure marked `partial` can't be called a pass. A partial *total* that is already over the limit is a real breach, because it can only understate.
- A figure rule whose latest snapshot is more than two intervals old reads `unknown` and judges nothing, for or against, until a fresh snapshot arrives. A record that has stopped moving can't go on passing or start a pause.
- Snapshots too old to act on are audited with their count and range. If any would have breached, a breach of kind `historical` records it, already closed and pausing nothing.
- A rule that stays unknown past its `unknown_limit_seconds` opens a breach of kind `unknown_limit`, which alerts and **never pauses**: not knowing isn't evidence of bad behaviour.

### Sandbox figures

Sandbox figures never pause anything as figures.

- On a product that isn't published, a snapshot with `source: sandbox` is evaluated and its breach is labelled `sandbox`.
- On a published product it isn't judged at all. The rule reads `unknown` ("the sponsor's ledger isn't live"). Past a pause rule's unknown limit, that pauses the product. It is the one unknown that does, since only the licence provider can end it, by connecting its books with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit).
- Without a snapshot (time-based rules, no record yet, a missed period), a published product's result is never labelled sandbox. An unpublished one goes by the ledger the firm is on now. A ledger Mynt can't tell is never taken for sandbox.
- A sandbox result can't close a breach opened on live figures, and a pass on sandbox figures doesn't count for a release.

A firm's own books count once it connects them with the partner kit.

### Breach record

The breach record is append-only, enforced in the database. Each breach keeps:

- the rule and its threshold;
- the snapshot's epoch, sequence and fingerprint;
- the observed value;
- the action taken, the severity and the cooldown outcome;
- when it opened.

A figure from the report is stored sealed, as the report is. Durations and period counts aren't the firm's books and are stored as they are.

Everything that follows (resolved, acknowledged, paused, released, reminders, a rule loosened, a revocation) is a separate append-only event on the breach, with who and when.

`list_covenant_breaches` gives the firm the whole record. `action_taken` is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `alerted` | The alert was sent |
| `alert_undelivered` | The alert reached no webhook, or was held back at send |
| `alert_suppressed_by_cooldown` | The breach is recorded; the cooldown held back the alert |
| `paused` | The product was paused and the alert sent |
| `paused_alert_undelivered` | The product was paused; the alert wasn't delivered |
| `pause_pending_publication` | A pause rule failed while the product wasn't published, so nothing was paused |
| `historical_not_acted_on` | A breach of kind `historical`: recorded, already closed, pausing nothing |
| `pause_failed_no_pins` | A live product with no pinned state, which drift can't hold |
| `sandbox_labelled` | A breach on sandbox figures |

### Alerts

`covenant.breached` and `covenant.cleared` go to the licence provider's own firm webhooks (`create_firm_webhook`), signed as every webhook is. See [Firm webhooks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#firm-webhooks).

- The numbers (`threshold`, `observed`, money in flight) travel sealed until sent and arrive as `data.result`.
- A rule still failing past its cooldown repeats `covenant.breached` with `reminder: true`.
- A cooldown holds back alerts only. A breach inside it is still recorded (`alert_suppressed_by_cooldown`), and a pause still happens and always alerts.
- After a relaunch, `snapshot_missed_for` and `consecutive_gaps` count only from the relaunch.

Who may receive them:

- A hook's `covenant.*` events need a named `license_provider` role and no admin role, on creating the hook and on deleting it.
- The creator's current roles are checked when a delivery is queued and again when it is sent, so a later role change takes effect.
- A default webhook created by anyone else doesn't include `covenant.*` events.
- When a hook's creator no longer qualifies, the hook shows `blocked` in `list_firm_webhooks` and is raised in `ops_status`.

An alert that reached no webhook, or was held back at send, says so and starts no cooldown: `alerted` is false, `action_taken` is `alert_undelivered` or `paused_alert_undelivered`, and the breach has an `alert_undelivered` event.

`ops_status` counts paused products, open breaches, rules unknown past their limit and a covenant timer that isn't running. It doesn't show anyone's figures.

### Pause

A `pause` rule that fails on live figures pauses the product, and anything built on it, through drift. The change has kind `covenant` and names the rule: `id` is the covenant and `rule_type` its type, with no threshold or figure.

- New sales stop, as with any drift.
- **It stops new sales only.** It cancels nothing. The money movements in flight when it took effect are reported in the breach (`in_flight_when_paused`: count and cents).
- New movements for customers already enrolled aren't blocked by a covenant pause, because drift never blocked them.

A paused product stays paused through the hourly drift sweep and through publishing a new version, until the licence provider calls `release_covenant_pause`:

- The release re-checks the rule first. It must pass, or the firm passes `override_reason`, which is audited and kept on the breach. Unknown counts as not passing.
- After an override, the same open breach doesn't pause again. A later relapse (a pass and then a new failure) is a new breach and pauses again.
- `release_covenant_pause` doesn't lift other reasons the product is paused.

Rules can be deleted, except one holding a pause.

### Revoking under a breach

`revoke_sponsorship` takes an optional `breach_id`. The breach keeps the revocation, who did it and why.

Revocation ends the sponsorship's rules, closes its open breaches and releases its holds. The product stays drifted by the revoked sponsorship itself.

### Who may do what with covenants

Only members of the sponsoring firm whose own roles name `license_provider` can set, change, delete, acknowledge or release, and the firm must be active.

An account with the admin role is refused even if it also holds that role or belongs to the firm, as for co-signing and reading a firm's books. There is deliberately no admin exception: a covenant is the licence provider's judgement of its own licence risk, and a Mynt admin who could change it could quietly stop a licence provider's pause. Mynt admins already have `admin_set_product_status` for pausing a product themselves.

What Mynt admins see:

- Every breach (`list_covenant_breaches`) with its rule type, status, severity, snapshot and timestamps.
- Not the rule's settings, the licence provider's reasons, the observed figure or the money in flight, for the same reason `get_product_health` refuses them. `audit_log` shows them the same way.

Put plainly: a Mynt admin can see that a firm's rule tripped, not how it is set or the number.

Other limits:

- The licence provider's own members see figures only while their firm is active and still sponsors the product.
- An admin account can't revoke a sponsorship either.
- A firm can't hold covenants over a product it owns.

### Changing a rule

Every change to a rule is audited with its old and new values.

A licence provider can't loosen a rule, or delete one, while a breach under it is open without giving a `reason`. The reason goes on the breach. Loosening means a looser threshold, alert in place of pause, lower severity, or a longer cooldown or unknown limit.

### What the builder sees

The product's own firm sees:

- `covenant_pauses` in `list_my_sponsorships`: the rule type and since when;
- the drift record on `get_product` and `get_product_regime`: kind `covenant`, the rule's id and type.

It doesn't see thresholds, observed values, severity, breach ids, alert-only breaches, or which other rules exist.

Anyone else looking at a published product, and apps' `product.drifted` webhooks, see only that a covenant paused it: `id` is shown as `redacted`, with no rule type. A run on a product can't be started from the rule name.

### Covenant tools

`set_covenant`, `list_covenants`, `delete_covenant`, `list_covenant_breaches`, `acknowledge_breach`, `release_covenant_pause`, and `revoke_sponsorship` with `breach_id`.

## Partner kit

A licence provider's engineers connect its systems themselves and see pass or fail, as vendors do. [Connecting a licence provider to Mynt](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/partners.md) is their guide: it has the request and statement formats, the signing steps, a worked example and every conformance case. This section says what Mynt does on its side.

Mynt needs three things from a licence provider:

| | What | Where it is described |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) | Its ledger, per sponsor per product, signed | This section |
| (b) | Customers' verified home states | [Partner requirements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md#partner-requirements) |
| (c) | Money rails | [Rails](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md#rails) |

The code is `core/src/partner-kit.ts` and `core/src/partner-ledger/contract.ts`. The schemas are in [`core/schemas/partner-ledger/`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/partner-ledger).

### The HTTPS feed

Mynt is the client. It sends `POST <url>/v1/ledger`, signed with `Mynt-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256, as in [the wire contract](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#the-wire-contract)) under a per-firm request secret.

Requests:

- They go through the vendor outbound rules (`core/src/vendor-call.ts`): HTTPS on 443, public addresses only, no redirects, a time limit, 1 MiB.
- The signed body names its `audience`, the exact URL it was sent to. The licence provider refuses any request whose audience isn't its own URL, or whose `environment` isn't the one that deployment serves. A request can't be relayed to the licence provider from an address someone else controls.
- Each round asks once per firm for every product it sponsors, with `PARTNER_LEDGER_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10 s). Firms are read in parallel, so a slow licence provider holds up only its own products.

Endpoints:

- An endpoint is an origin and a path only, with no query string or fragment.
- A Mynt admin proposes them (`configure_partner_ledger`, audited).
- The firm is told on its webhooks (`partner_ledger.endpoint_change_pending`).
- They take effect only when the firm's own licence-provider member confirms them (`confirm_partner_ledger_endpoints`). `get_partner_kit` shows a pending change plainly.
- The firm takes the request secret once (`reveal_partner_ledger_secret`, `rotate_partner_ledger_secret`). Mynt admins never see it.

The answer is a statement (`mynt.partner_ledger.v1`):

- integer cents per product, null with a reason where the firm can't give a figure, and an `as_of` time;
- an Ed25519 signature over the text `mynt.partner_ledger.v1`, a zero byte and the statement's canonical JSON (RFC 8785, integers only).

Keys:

- Live statements are signed with the key from `register_partner_signing_key`.
- Test statements are signed with a separate test key (`register_partner_test_signing_key`), which is MACed under a key derived from the vault and is never the same key.
- A test-key signature is never valid for live, and the other way round.

`HttpPartnerLedger` uses a statement only when all of these pass; otherwise the snapshot is `unavailable`:

- the schema;
- the firm;
- the `live` environment;
- the echoed `request_id`;
- the live-key signature;
- the clock: at most 300 s ahead, and at most `PARTNER_LEDGER_MAX_AGE_HOURS` (default 24) old.

A product the statement leaves out is null: "didn't cover this product".

### The daily file

A firm without an API uploads the same statement, with `request_id: null`, using `upload_partner_ledger_file` (licence-provider members only, never Mynt admins).

The upload is refused unless it:

- passes the same checks with that environment's key;
- isn't older than `PARTNER_LEDGER_FILE_MAX_AGE_HOURS` (default 36);
- is newer than the firm's last file for that environment.

The file is stored sealed under `MYNT_VAULT_KEY`. Mynt admins see only its time and product count.

On every read it is checked again against the firm's current live key (a replaced key stops it counting at once) and its age. A `test` file is for conformance only.

### Conformance

`run_partner_conformance { source: "http" | "file" }` is run by the firm, or by a Mynt admin naming it. The firm must be active.

**(a) The ledger, for `http`.** Mynt calls the test endpoint for every product the firm sponsors plus one it made up. It checks:

- the schema, firm, environment, `request_id`, test-key signature, clock, null handling and coverage;
- that the made-up product comes back null with a reason;
- that each of these requests is refused with an error body: a badly signed one, a stale one (600 s), a malformed one, a wrong-environment one (`live` sent to the test endpoint) and a wrong-audience one.

It also probes the live endpoint once, without asking for figures. A live request whose audience is the test endpoint's URL, naming only a product Mynt made up, must be refused (`live_wrong_audience_refused`). Whatever comes back is dropped unread.

**(a) The ledger, for `file`.** The same statement checks, on the latest upload.

The endpoint version a run tested is the one read at its start.

**(b) Home states.** Mynt calls each identity provider the firm accepts (its own identity offerings, and those approved for its sponsorships) in its test environment. It passes when one answers a passed check with a valid `residential_state`.

**(c) Rails.** Reported from the firm's rails and their offerings' latest `run_conformance`.

Each run is kept with its time and `expires_at` (`PARTNER_CONFORMANCE_MAX_AGE_DAYS`, default 30). It is shown by `get_partner_kit` (the firm, or Mynt admins naming it) and in `get_my_entity` as `partner_kit`. No case or problem ever carries a figure.

### Going live

`set_partner_ledger_source { source }` switches the firm from `sandbox` to `http` or `file` only when that source's latest run passed its ledger part and hasn't run out.

- For `http`, it also reads the live endpoint once and checks the statement, which must carry the live key's signature. The figures are discarded.
- For `file`, it needs a fresh live file.

The choice is made again on every snapshot (`partnerLedgerFor`). A firm whose endpoints changed, or whose pass ran out, reads the sandbox until it passes again. If the choice can't be made (the database fails), the ledger is `unknown` (`ledgerState`), never taken for sandbox.

(b) and (c) don't hold up the switch, because each money movement already checks them.
