- Every movement is a row in the ledger tied to its pool and firm in `pool_movements`, with its own idempotency key, so a retried call is the same movement.
- A real commitment also needs the product published.

### Positions

`list_my_positions` shows `contributed_cents`, `withdrawn_cents` and `balance_cents`. They are worked out from the movement ledger, from **settled movements only**, so nothing stored can disagree with them.

- A movement still on its way (`pending_*`), or one Mynt swept with no answer (`unresolved_*`), doesn't count as settled.
- A deposit or withdrawal returned after settling leaves the position by itself. A reversal reduces contributed or restores what was withdrawn.
- `available_to_withdraw_cents` is the balance less what is on its way out, unresolved, or already queued.
- What settled is the partner's reported amount when it is less than what was asked. A short settlement shows the amount that settled and ends the request as `paid_short`.
- A report of more than was asked is refused and flagged to Mynt admins (`ops_status`).

### A pool's capital

Each `list_pools` row of a pool the caller may see whole carries `capital: { rails, on_chain }`. The callers who see a pool whole are a Mynt admin, the pool's product's builder and its licence provider. The totals are over every firm and wallet in the pool, never any one firm's or wallet's figures.

**`rails`** is from the movement ledger, in cents, settled movements only as for positions:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `principal_cents` | Settled in less paid out |
| `settled_in_cents` | Deposits settled |
| `pending_in_cents` | Deposits asked for, not settled |
| `queued_withdrawal_cents` | What queued and parked requests still ask for |
| `pending_out_cents` | Withdrawals on their way |
| `paid_out_cents` | Withdrawals paid |
| `unresolved_cents` | Movements swept with no answer, either way |
| `firms_with_balance` | How many firms hold a balance |

**`on_chain`** is null unless the pool has an [on-chain treasury](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#on-chain-treasuries). Then it is in USDC base units (`unit: "usdc_base_units"`, a number while exact, a decimal string above 2^53):

- `principal` is the pool account's `total_principal`, read at `principal_as_of`.
- `deposited` (deposits not rejected), `indexed_principal` (what is left of them), `queued` (open and parked requests' remaining) and `paid_out` are sums of what the indexer read, as of `indexed_at`.

A figure that can't be measured is null, never 0, with its reason in `not_measured` (keyed by field): the pool account couldn't be read, or the indexer hasn't read the treasury's history yet.

Any other caller, such as a liquidity provider browsing pools, gets `capital: null` and `capital_not_shown` saying why. Rows from a Mynt before this have neither field, and Studio's My pools shows Not measured for them.

### How money actually moves

Mynt has no direct path that instructs a pool's rail. Mynt instructs no `ach`, `wire`, `rtp`, `fednow` or `push_to_card` rail, and pool movements aren't ramp customer transfers. See [Which rails Mynt instructs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md#which-rails-mynt-instructs).

1. A deposit or withdrawal is a `requested` row in the ledger.
2. The licence provider sees it (`list_money_movements`, `list_withdrawals`) and moves the money on its rail.
3. The licence provider says what happened with `report_pool_movement`: `submitted`, `settled`, `failed` or `returned`.

That report is what settles a position, so the licence provider's word on its own rail is the source of truth for these movements. A live settlement needs its `external_ref`.

A licence provider should check a movement's `pool_hold` in `list_withdrawals` before moving money on a requested row.

### Pool flags

A settlement is a fact, so it is recorded even if it takes the firm's position below zero (for example a deposit returned before a payout landed). That raises an open `negative_balance` flag with the partner's `external_ref`. The flag stays in `ops_status` and `list_pool_flags` until a Mynt admin closes it (`resolve_pool_flag`).

The one settlement refused is a double claim: a withdrawal written off for certain whose amount has since gone out another way. That is flagged too (`double_claim`), and a Mynt admin can accept or reject it.

### Pool tools

| Tool | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_pool` | Builder | Proposes a pool on its firm's sponsored component |
| `approve_pool` | Licence provider | Approves a pool it sponsors and names its approved rails |
| `set_pool_offering_cleared` | Mynt admin | Records who cleared a pool's offering and the legal basis; the gate on real commitments |
| `report_pool_movement` | Licence provider | What became of a movement of a pool it sponsors |
| `list_pool_flags` | Mynt admin, licence provider | Items open until someone deals with them: `negative_balance`, `double_claim`, `link_conflict` |
| `resolve_pool_flag` | Mynt admin | Closes a flag, with a reason, together with its effect on the ledger |
| `set_pool_firm_state` | Mynt admin, the pool's licence provider | Corrects a firm's state |
| `respond_to_state_correction` | Liquidity provider | Accepts or disputes a correction |
| `commit_to_pool` | Liquidity provider | Commits capital: a deposit on the pool's rail |
| `request_withdrawal`, `cancel_withdrawal` | Liquidity provider | Joins or leaves the queue |
| `list_my_positions` | Liquidity provider | Contributed, withdrawn, balance, and what is pending, unresolved or reversed |
| `list_pools` | All of the above | Pools, scoped to the caller |
| `list_withdrawals` | All of the above | The queue, in order, with why each request is waiting |
| `pause_pool`, `resume_pool` | Mynt admin, the pool's licence provider | Stops or restarts a pool; with `close: true`, closes it |
| `list_pools_with_health` | Liquidity provider | The pools it may see, side by side: coverage, trend, gaps, verified status and reserve headroom |

Notes on the tools:

- **`create_pool`** takes an optional `idempotency_key` (8 to 200 characters, like `commit_to_pool`'s), which makes a retry safe. The same key with the same arguments from the same person returns the pool made the first time (`replay: true`) and not a second one. The same key with different arguments is refused (`idempotency_conflict`). Keys are each caller's own, so another person's same key is a separate proposal. Without a key, every call proposes a new pool.
- **`resolve_pool_flag`** accepts or rejects a double claim, or links or closes a `link_conflict` (counted against the pool's headroom until then). It can't be called by anyone at the pool's licence provider, the product's firm or the firm it concerns.
- **`list_pools`** scope: a Mynt admin sees all; a builder its products'; a licence provider what it sponsors; a liquidity provider those it is in, or that are approved and sandbox or cleared. Each row has its `capital` totals for a Mynt admin, its builder and its licence provider.
- **`list_pools_with_health`** gives numbers only for pools of products the caller is committed to, through product health's own entitlement, so an admin account is still refused them. Otherwise each is null with its reason.

### Audit and separation from customer figures

- Every one of these tools, and every refusal that matters, is in the audit log, including the read-only ones.
- The worker's own actions are `pool_auto_paused`, `pool_auto_resumed`, `pool_withdrawal_claimed` and `pool_withdrawal_refused`.
- Pool deposits and payouts are in the ledger but left out of the product's health flows and failure rates (`flowsFor`), which describe its customers.
- Sandbox pools are left out of the product's open withdrawal count.
- Everything a position, request or movement shows carries `sandbox`, so test money can't be read as real.

## The withdrawal queue

The withdrawal queue is first in, first out per pool (`request_withdrawal`, `cancel_withdrawal`, `list_withdrawals`). A request becomes eligible after the pool's notice period.

A worker pays the queue in order: `LiquidityWorker`, a `serialLoop` like Mynt's other workers, every `LIQUIDITY_POLL_MS` (default 60 seconds).

### The latest snapshot

The latest snapshot of the pool is the newest finished one, published or missed. A period still waiting for its co-signature or the chain doesn't count yet. See [Product health](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#product-health).

Payment stops, with the reason shown in `pause_reason` and each request's `waiting_reason`, if:

- there is no snapshot;
- it is a missed period;
- a live pool's snapshot is sandbox-sourced, or not from the licence provider's live ledger, or isn't verified;
- it is older than `POOL_HEALTH_MAX_AGE_MINUTES` (default twice the health interval);
- reserves or obligations are null (the reason is the one the figure carries);
- it is from a licence provider other than the pool's.

Sandbox pools use sandbox figures and don't need `verified`, which a sandbox snapshot never is.

A pool's snapshots read its own licence provider's books, so a second licence provider's pool is judged on its own firm's figures.

**A live pool needs a verified live-ledger snapshot, so no live pool can pay out until its licence provider's real ledger is connected** with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit).

### The reserve

A request is paid only as far as the pool's reserves, less whatever may have left since that snapshot was read, stay at or above the minimum.

A licence provider's reserves for a product are one figure (per sponsor per product: see `core/src/partner-ledger/types.ts`). So that licence provider's pools on the product share one headroom, locked together in id order. What is subtracted is:

- every withdrawal of its real pools on its way, unresolved, or settled after that reading;
- its other outflows on the product since then;
- any deposit reversed since.

Money leaving those reserves in a way Mynt can't see (outside its movement ledger) is treated as none until the next reading shows it.

Payment can be partial. The rest stays at the same place in the queue, with nothing behind it passing.

### Rail limits and refusals

- A payment is capped at the rail's per-transfer limit.
- The rail's daily limit and status are checked at the chokepoint. A refusal there sends the amount back to the queue and shows in `hold_reason`.
- The worker waits 15 minutes before asking again after a refusal about the rail.
- A refusal about one firm (a state the rail doesn't serve) parks that request after three refusals (`status: parked`, `status_reason`), so the queue moves on.
- A parked request keeps its place. The worker checks it again.
- Those re-checks ask the rails without making a movement, and back off (15 minutes doubling to 6 hours). A request that stays refused leaves no new rows or audit entries.
- A suspended firm, one with a parked request, or one whose own payment outcome isn't known yet is passed over and doesn't stop the firms behind it.

### Correcting a firm's state

The pool's licence provider or a Mynt admin can correct a parked firm's state with `set_pool_firm_state`. A correction must pass the money rails' own sponsorship and licence checks.

| Who corrects | When it applies | What the firm can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The pool's licence provider | Only when the firm accepts it (`respond_to_state_correction`, listed in `list_my_positions`). So it can't be used to park or pass over a firm | Accept or dispute |
| A Mynt admin | At once | Dispute it for `POOL_CORRECTION_DISPUTE_DAYS` days (14 by default), which restores the old state and who set it |

- A licence provider's proposal never replaces an admin's applied correction, so it can't take the right to dispute away. Only a newer admin correction, or the firm's own acceptance of a pending one, does.
- Only the latest correction can be answered. A new one replaces any the firm hasn't answered.
- The state's source is kept on the commitment and each movement (`sponsor_corrected`, `admin_corrected`), so a sponsorship change doesn't cost a firm its place.

### Automatic pausing and resuming

- **Health.** When health drops, the worker sets the pool to `paused` (`pause_kind: health`). When a snapshot shows it above its minimum again, the worker sets it back to `open`.
- **Governance.** A revoked sponsorship, an inactive licence provider or a drifted product pauses the pool the same way (`pause_kind: governance`). That clears itself once the cause is gone.
- **Covenants.** A [covenant](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#covenants) pause doesn't pause a pool. It stops new sign-ups and never money movements, so on its own it stops neither a pool's deposits nor its withdrawals (health gates still apply). Pool capital isn't in the money in flight a covenant reports.

A real deposit is checked against the pool's latest health every time, open or paused:

- It is let in only if a snapshot Mynt trusts shows the pool healthy, or short of its reserve, because new capital is how a pool gets back above it.
- If the snapshot is missing, stale or unverified, there is no telling what the pool could pay back, so the deposit is refused with the reason (`health_unconfirmed`).

A newly approved live pool stays paused until the worker's first check. Every other pause stops commitments too.

### Manual pauses

- A Mynt admin or the pool's licence provider can `pause_pool` and `resume_pool`. The worker never lifts a manual pause.
- A licence provider can't lift, change or close over an admin's pause. Only an admin's resume clears it.
- Approving never reopens a closed pool.
- With `close: true` a pool stops taking commitments for good but keeps paying its queue, subject to the same checks.

### Nobody gets paid twice

The claim is one Postgres function that locks the pool's row (as `reserve_money_movement` locks the rail) and takes the amount from the request before the chokepoint is asked. Concurrent workers can't both have it and can't overdraw the reserve between them.

- A worker that dies between the claim and the chokepoint is picked up on a later tick.
- A claim that already has a ledger row is tied to it first, under any pause, since that moves no money. It is never released.
- A withdrawal claim with no ledger row is released, so it is claimed again against headroom as it is now, once the pool has passed its gate.
- A deposit is re-checked against the pool's status and `offering_cleared`.
- A payment that failed for certain goes back to the same place in the queue.
- A payment whose outcome isn't known counts as gone until the licence provider says, and holds the firm's request.
- A payment returned after settling isn't paid again by itself, so the firm asks again. A request whose whole amount came back is `returned`.

## Product health

Licence providers and liquidity providers watch each product's financial health from a record that can't be rewritten, to pull a licence on bad behaviour or move capital. Mynt never holds funds and no customer data goes on chain. This feature only reports.

### What a snapshot is

On a schedule (`PRODUCT_HEALTH_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, default 60, at most 1440), Mynt computes one report for each product with an approved sponsorship, and for each of its liquidity pools. The report holds:

- reserves and customer obligations, and the coverage between them;
- flows in and out, and pending settlements;
- reversal and failure rates;
- open withdrawal requests;
- open complaints and incidents.

Money is integer cents. Ratios are integer basis points.

**A figure Mynt can't measure is null with its reason, never 0.** Coverage with no obligations is null, not infinite. Complaints and incidents are null until Mynt tracks them.

`open_withdrawal_requests` is measured from the queues of the product's real [liquidity pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#liquidity-pools).

### Where the numbers come from

Reserves and obligations come only from the licence provider's own systems, through a `PartnerLedger` (`core/src/partner-ledger/`), never from the builder's app.

| Snapshot `source` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sandbox` | The licence provider hasn't connected its own ledger. The figures are made up and can never read as live, whatever the product's status or any stored row says |
| `partner_ledger` | A ledger that declares itself live. It only ever means that |
| `unavailable` | A ledger read failed. The snapshot is `source: unavailable`, with those figures null |

A licence provider connects its books with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#partner-kit): an HTTPS feed Mynt pulls, or a signed daily file. Its snapshots read them once it passes conformance and switches.

### Flows

Flows come from the money rails' `flowsFor(store, productId, from, to)` when that module is present:

- `on_ramp` and `deposit` are money in;
- `off_ramp` and `payout` are money out;
- `requested` and `submitted` are pending.

What the rails can't measure stays null with their reason, and a direction they can't see is listed in `flows_not_measured`.

What they measure is stated in every report as `flows_basis`. The rails total movements by when they were requested, so a period's figures are that period's requests by their status when the snapshot was computed:

- `requested_*` is everything requested.
- `flows_*` is the part already settled. A payment that takes days to settle shows as pending and isn't counted in a later period.
- Movements nobody ever answered for are `unresolved_cents`, counted in `requested_*` and no other total.
- A figure that totals only the directions the rails can see is marked `partial`, with a `reason` saying what it leaves out.
- Reversal and failure rates are by value among this period's completed requests, rounded up. Coverage is rounded down.

A sandbox report carries no flows at all. The rails exclude sandbox movements, and real money doesn't belong beside test figures.

### Fingerprint

Each report is encoded as canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces, integers only, so the same report always has the same bytes). Its sha256 is the fingerprint.

The report carries a random salt, so the numbers can't be guessed from the public fingerprint.

### Encryption and who can read a report

Each product has its own random AES-256-GCM data key, sealed under `MYNT_VAULT_KEY`. Each report is encrypted with it and bound to its product, sequence and fingerprint, so it can't be edited or moved.

The server opens a report only for entitled readers, through `get_product_health`:

- the members of the sponsoring licence provider's firm;
- the firms holding a settled position in one of the product's real [pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#liquidity-pools). They need the `liquidity_provider` role and read only the books of those pools' sponsoring licence providers.

Rules on access:

- A liquidity provider that has fully exited loses access to new snapshots. It can still read those up to its exit, and a new settled commitment brings the rest back.
- A licence provider reads only the snapshots whose numbers came from its own books, so a second licence provider doesn't see the first's.
- A withdrawn sponsorship, or a firm that isn't active, ends access at once.
- Reading needs the named licence-provider role.

Mynt admins:

- An account with the admin role is refused even if it also holds the licence-provider role or belongs to the firm.
- An admin account gets status and fingerprints. It can't itself open a firm's books, replace its key or co-sign for it.
- An admin can still add a separate non-admin account to a firm, which is audited. So this is a control that leaves a trail, not an absolute bar on Mynt's staff.

Put plainly: Mynt's server computes the numbers and holds the vault key, so it could read them. The encryption keeps them from the database, its backups and everyone else. It doesn't keep them from a compromise of the server's vault key.

[Confidential computing](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/confidential-computing.md) moves the licence provider's books and the vault's root key out of the server's reach, and says exactly how far that goes.

### Partner co-signature

A licence provider registers its firm's Ed25519 public key with `register_partner_signing_key`. Small-order keys are refused. Every key it has registered is kept, so an old signature stays checkable after a rotation. Its private key never reaches Mynt.

1. A snapshot waits for the licence provider during a window (`PRODUCT_HEALTH_COSIGN_WINDOW_MINUTES`, default half the interval and never more).
2. The licence provider signs the UTF-8 text `mynt.product_health.cosign.v1`, one zero byte, then the 32 bytes of the fingerprint.
3. `submit_partner_signature` must verify with the firm's registered key while the firm still sponsors the product and before the window closes, or it is refused.

With no signature by the deadline the snapshot is published as `mynt_only` and says so.

### What verified means

`verified` is true only for a published snapshot from a real ledger on a live product, with a valid partner signature and a chain that matches. Sandbox, unsigned and missed snapshots never are.

It is worked out on every read from the authenticated report and the signature, not from stored flags.

- Someone who can only write the database can't forge it. Reports are authenticated, signing keys are MACed under a key derived from the vault, and a published row that is changed stops matching the chain.
- Someone holding `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` could still forge a snapshot before it is published.
- A snapshot that never reached the chain has only Mynt's word behind it.

`verification.integrity_ok` is a smaller claim: the report matches its fingerprint and the record matches the chain.

A missed period's report is withheld, since it never reached the chain.

### The program

`core/programs/product-health` is a Mynt-owned Anchor program that holds a head account per product. The head holds:

- the sequence number, the fingerprint, the period and the source flag;
- a per-product commitment to the partner's key and signature;
- Mynt's signing key;
- a sha256 hash chain over every field of every record, with an event for each.

Properties:

- A product appears on chain only as a keyed hash of its id (HMAC under a key derived from the vault). A guessed id can't be tested, and the commitment doesn't link a licence provider's products.
- The program moves no value and calls no token program.
- The publisher is set once at initialisation by the program's own upgrade authority. There is no hard-coded key.
- Periods must be contiguous and can't end in the future.
- It passes Mynt's own [mainnet gate hard rules](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#mainnet-program-gate), checked in CI on what the compiler read, with the bytes and IDL. It has one reviewed lead: that it reads the clock.
- It publishes to **devnet only**.

### What the chain does and does not prove

- The program can't check the co-signature. `partner_signed` on chain says only that the publisher supplied a commitment.
- A reader checks the signature against the partner's key and the commitment, as `get_product_health` does.
- An on-chain Ed25519 check would have to publish the partner's key, and needs deciding before mainnet.
- The publisher can't be rotated without a new deployment.
- The hash chain makes a changed record visible, but whoever holds the upgrade authority can replace the program until it is frozen or put behind a timelock.

### Publishing snapshots

Sequence numbers are gapless per product. The program accepts only the next one, and Mynt sends each in order.

- Sends go through Mynt's RPC client, with its retries and backoff.
- Mynt reads the head before it concludes anything. A record that landed unseen is adopted even past its deadline. While the chain can't be read, nothing is marked missed.
- A snapshot not on chain by its deadline, or a stretch Mynt never computed, is recorded as `missed` and gets a marker on chain.
- Every period starts where the last ended, so changing `PRODUCT_HEALTH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` can't overlap one.

`list_product_health` and `get_product_health` report gaps: `no_record`, `missed`, `stalled`, `sequence_gap`, `period_gap`, `overdue`, `re_anchored`, and the chain being `chain_behind` or `chain_ahead` of Mynt's record.

`ops_status` flags stalled records, snapshots past their deadline, and a worker that isn't running while products are sponsored.

### Checking it without Mynt

`get_product_health` gives entitled readers, and nobody else, each snapshot's `partner_key` and `partner_signature`, and the record's `subject` and `head_address`.

`core/scripts/product-health-verify.mjs` uses nothing but Node and an RPC of your choosing. Mynt wrote the answer it reads, so it believes nothing the answer says about where to look. Save the tool's answer to a file and run:

```sh
node product-health-verify.mjs --file answer.json --rpc <url> --program-id <address> --partner-key <your firm's key>
```

**Get `--program-id` from outside Mynt's answers.** The operator gives it to you directly, in writing, when the program is deployed (for example with your sponsorship paperwork). `--partner-key` is the key your own firm holds.

The script derives the head's address from the program id and subject. It checks that:

- the account is owned by that program and is a `Head` account;
- the report hashes to the fingerprint;
- the signature verifies under your key;
- the head holds that fingerprint, period, source and commitment.

For an older snapshot (`--sequence N`, with `--epoch E` for an earlier record) it decodes the `record_snapshot` instruction of its transaction instead.

It prints `OVERALL PASS` and exits 0 only when everything was checked. Without `--partner-key` it says the key wasn't independently checked and exits 3.

One limit it can't close: the subject is a keyed hash, so it proves this report was recorded under that subject, not that Mynt filed it under the right product.

### After a chain reset or a new program

A record the chain no longer holds stalls in the open. A Mynt admin calls `reanchor_product_health` (`product_id`, `reason`).

It works only when:

- the chain has no record for the product under the current program;
- there is no transaction history at that address (history without a head means it wasn't a reset, and a history that can't be read refuses too);
- something reached the old chain, or the program changed.

A head that disagrees with Mynt's record is refused, because that needs investigating. Anchor rows are MACed under a key derived from the vault, and one that fails reads as a mismatch. Refusals are audited.

After a re-anchor:

- The record restarts at sequence 1 in a new epoch. The old record's verdict, head sequence and chain hash are saved with it.
- Its snapshots stay readable and report `previous_chain_matched`, `previous_chain_mismatch` (it didn't match, or a row has changed since) or `previous_chain_unverifiable` (the old chain is gone).
- The re-anchor and every hole in the old record stay visible as gaps.

### The publisher key

The publisher key is its own devnet key in Mynt's vault, never the deploy authority.

`HealthPublisher` (`core/src/solana/product-health-chain.ts`) reads every message back before signing. It refuses anything but the product-health program's own instructions, paid for by the publisher.

### Product health tools

| Tool | Who | What it returns or does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_product_health` | Licence providers, committed liquidity providers, the product's own firm, Mynt admins | Fingerprints and status only |
| `get_product_health` | Entitled readers | The decrypted report, whether it matches its fingerprint, whether the fingerprint matches what is on chain, and history |
| `register_partner_signing_key` | Licence provider | Registers the firm's Ed25519 public key |
| `submit_partner_signature` | Licence provider | Co-signs a snapshot |
| `reanchor_product_health` | Mynt admin | Restarts a record after a chain reset or a new program |

`get_product_health` reports `verification.on_chain` as `matches`, `mismatch`, `pending`, `not_on_chain`, one of the `previous_chain_*` verdicts or `unavailable`. When the chain can't be reached it says so, and is never reported as a match.

### Deploying the program

Deploying is an operator step, never CI.

1. From a checkout on the server, with its environment loaded, run `core/scripts/product-health-deploy.sh --program-keypair <new-program-keypair.json> --authority <upgrade-authority-keypair.json>`. It builds the program with the pinned toolchain, checks the hard rules, deploys to devnet, creates the publisher key in the vault and names it on chain (`mynt product-health publisher`, `mynt product-health init`).
2. Set `PRODUCT_HEALTH_PROGRAM_ID` on the server and restart.

Until `PRODUCT_HEALTH_PROGRAM_ID` is set, the worker doesn't run and `get_product_health` reports the chain check as unavailable.

## Earn in Studio

In Mynt Studio, pools are on the **Earn** page (`/earn`), in the sidebar for builders and liquidity providers. The page has an assistant and, beside it, a panel of tabs:

- **Pools**: every pool open to the person, with **Commit capital** for liquidity providers.
- **My pools**: for builders, their products' pools.
- **My strategies**: what the assistant drafted. Commitments and withdrawals for liquidity providers, pool proposals for builders.

See [Earn](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/studio.md#earn) for the page as a whole.

pages.title: Treasury & Solana
pages.markdown:
## On-chain treasuries

A pool's capital can instead be held on chain, as USDC, in the app's own treasury program built from Mynt's template (`core/workspaces/coding-build/templates/solana-treasury`, program `mynt_treasury`; its README has the rules).

**Devnet by default.** A treasury is registered on mainnet only after a Mynt admin turns the switch on with `configure_treasury_mainnet` and the pool passes the mainnet checks. Otherwise every mainnet request is refused with `mainnet_disabled`. See [Treasury mainnet](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#treasury-mainnet). The [mainnet program gate](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#mainnet-program-gate) is unchanged.

**Mynt never signs for a person's funds and never holds their keys.** It prepares an unsigned transaction whose fee payer and only signer is the person's own wallet, which signs and sends it.

The code is `core/src/treasury.ts`, `core/src/treasury-tools.ts` and `core/src/solana/treasury-chain.ts`.

### Registering a treasury

1. The builder of the pool's product initialises the treasury with Mynt's attester (`get_treasury_attester`) among its `attesters`.
2. The builder calls `register_treasury_pool({ pool_id, cluster: "devnet", program_id, pool_address })`.
3. Mynt reads both the program and the pool account from devnet and checks them.

Mynt refuses:

| Refusal | When |
| --- | --- |
| `not_a_program` | The program isn't an upgradeable program |
| `not_a_treasury_pool` | The account isn't a `mynt_treasury` Pool at its own address `["pool", creator, pool_id]` |
| `wrong_cluster` | The pool's `cluster` isn't devnet's genesis hash |
| `wrong_mint` | The mint isn't devnet USDC |
| `attester_missing`, `unexpected_attesters` | The attesters aren't exactly `[Mynt's attester, none]`. Another attester could admit depositors Mynt never checked |
| `not_pool_owner` | The pool isn't the builder's own |

The pool must be the builder's own: its `creator` or `authority` is a verified Solana wallet linked to the registering builder's sign-in. A Mynt admin may register any pool.

Registration records the program's executable hash (sha256 of its bytes without trailing zeros) and its upgrade authority.

`verified_build` is true only when the deployed bytes are the template's verifiable build at that address. A registration queues Mynt's own rebuild of the template at that program id. Until the rebuild finishes, the pool shows `build_status: "unverified build"`, which devnet accepts. See [Verified builds and upgrade locks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#verified-builds-and-upgrade-locks).

### A treasury in pool listings

`list_pools` and `list_pools_with_health` rows of such a pool carry a `treasury` object, read from the pool account (cached up to 60 seconds):

`treasury: { cluster, program_id, pool_address, verified_build, build_status, build_note, program_hash, upgrade_authority, on_chain_terms, on_chain_error }`

`on_chain_terms` has:

- terms: `lock_in_seconds`, `notice_seconds`, `review_window_seconds`, `min_reserve`, `min_reserve_bps`, `commitment_min`, `commitment_max`, `min_request`, `topups_when_health_paused`;
- state: `sponsor_paused`, `health_paused`, `winding_down`, `deposits_paused`, `pending_terms_effective_at`;
- attesters: `attesters`, `mynt_attester_approved`;
- accounts: `usdc_mint`, `vault`, `authority`;
- totals: `total_principal`, `total_queued` and `as_of`.

Amounts are USDC base units (6 decimals), a number while exact and a decimal string above 2^53.

### The attester

The attester is a dedicated Ed25519 key, generated once and sealed in the vault under its own role (`treasury_attester`), like the product-health publisher. Each cluster has its own. It holds no funds, pays no fees and is never an account of a transaction.

It signs only the program's deposit approval:

`"MYNTDEP3" ‖ program id ‖ cluster ‖ pool ‖ depositor ‖ nonce (u64 LE) ‖ amount (u64 LE) ‖ expiry (i64 LE)`

- It signs at the wallet's position nonce, for exactly the amount prepared, expiring within ten minutes.
- Every deposit moves the position's nonce on, so an approval admits one deposit of that amount.
- The cluster the devnet attester signs is always devnet's genesis hash. The attester itself refuses any other, and a pool account naming another is refused (`wrong_cluster`).

**Earlier builds.** Pools registered on builds before MYNTDEP3 keep the earlier `"MYNTDEP2"` layout: no amount, reusable until it expires. `register_treasury_pool` records which layout each pool's program checks (`deposit_approval`), knows it for the template's own builds (`earlier_builds` in `core/schemas/solana-treasury-template.json`), and keeps a pool's layout when it is registered again.

**Who it signs for.** It signs only when all of these hold:

- the wallet is a verified Solana wallet linked to the caller's sign-in (`get_linked_accounts`);
- the caller's firm is active, and isn't the pool's licence provider or its product's firm;
- the pool is approved and either sandbox or cleared (as for `commit_to_pool`);
- the deposit is within the pool's on-chain commitment limits per wallet and its per-firm limit across the firm's wallets;
- the pool is open at Mynt and not paused or winding down on chain.

**Attester changes stop it.** If the pool's attesters stop being exactly `[Mynt's, none]` (a `TermsApplied` or `AttesterRemoved` event the indexer reads, or the fresh read before signing), Mynt sets the pool's `attesters_flag`. The flag is shown in the pool's `treasury` view and in `ops_status`, and audited as `treasury_attesters_flagged`. Mynt approves no deposits to the pool (`attesters_changed`) until its builder registers it again with the attesters put back.

`prepare_*` calls are limited to 20 a minute per person (`rate_limited`).

### Deposits

`prepare_treasury_deposit({ pool_id, wallet, amount_usdc_base_units, max_lock_in_seconds })` returns:

`{ cluster, transaction_base64, expires_at, last_valid_block_height, summary: { pool, pool_id, pool_address, amount, lock_in_seconds, notice_seconds, review_window_seconds, wallet, verified_build } }`

The transaction is an unsigned v0 transaction with the Ed25519 attestation instruction then `deposit`, a fresh blockhash and the wallet as fee payer. A blockhash lasts about a minute, so a wallet that takes longer prepares again.

Refusals carry `code`: `wallet_not_linked`, `not_liquidity_provider`, `offering_not_cleared`, `over_limit`, `under_minimum`, `pool_paused`, `not_on_chain`, `mainnet_disabled`, `terms_changed` (the lock-in is longer than `max_lock_in_seconds`), `insufficient_usdc`, `attester_removed`, `rpc_unavailable`.

### Withdrawals

`prepare_treasury_withdrawal({ pool_id, wallet, deposit, amount_usdc_base_units, max_notice_seconds })` returns the same shape with one `request_withdrawal` instruction and no attestation. `deposit` is the deposit record's address.

Refusals: `deposit_not_found`, `deposit_rejected`, `in_review`, `deposit_locked`, `over_limit`, `below_min_request`, `terms_changed`, and the deposit's codes above.

### Health checks on a treasury pool

The liquidity worker pauses a pool that has no finished health snapshot. There is one exception, while there is no health reading at all (no snapshot yet, or product health not running): a **sandbox** pool with a registered on-chain treasury whose attesters aren't flagged. The treasury program enforces its own reserve floor and pauses on chain.

- The worker leaves such a pool open with `hold_reason: "Health checks not configured; the on-chain treasury enforces reserves"`.
- On its next tick it reopens one it had paused only for the missing snapshot (audited as `pool_auto_resumed` with that reason).
- `prepare_treasury_deposit` follows the same rule.

Nothing else changes:

- Real-money pools, pools on rails and flagged pools are still paused for a missing snapshot.
- A snapshot that exists and fails (missed, stale, below the reserve) still pauses even an exempt pool.
- A Mynt admin's or licence provider's pause stays until they lift it.

### Balances

`get_wallet_balances({ address, cluster })` returns `{ sol_lamports, usdc_base_units, usdc_mint, usdc_account }` for one of the caller's own verified linked wallets (`wallet_not_linked` otherwise).

### Indexing

Every `TREASURY_INDEX_POLL_MS` (30 seconds by default) the HTTP server indexes each registered pool in two steps, with bounded work per poll and nothing skipped:

1. **Scan.** A scan pages backward from the newest signature to the stored cursor: five pages of 1000 a poll, resuming where it stopped on the next poll, keeping what it finds.
2. **Read.** Once the scan reaches the cursor, the cursor moves to the newest signature the scan started from. The transactions found are read oldest first, `TREASURY_INDEX_PER_POLL` a poll (200 by default). A new scan starts once they have all been read.

It reads the events the treasury itself logged for that pool, each once: `DepositMade`, `DepositRejected`, `WithdrawalRequested`, `WithdrawalPaid`, `RequestCancelled`, `RequestVoided`, `RequestParked`.

### On-chain positions

`list_my_positions` also lists `source: "on-chain", cluster: "devnet"` rows per pool and wallet. Rows from the rails carry `source: "off-chain"`.

A wallet counts for a firm, in its positions and its per-firm limit, only through its current link: the caller's own linked wallets, and those the firm's people prepared from while each is still at the firm and still links it. A record whose person left or unlinked it is dropped.

Each row has:

- `principal`, `deposited`, `paid`, `queued`, `available_to_request`;
- a `deposits` array, each with `deposit` (the record's address to pass to `prepare_treasury_withdrawal`), `amount`, `remaining`, `queued`, `unlocks_at` and its review window;
- each request with its `status` (`open`, `parked`, `paid`, `cancelled`, `voided`) and `payable_at`.

### Transaction status

`get_treasury_tx_status({ signature })` says whether a sent transaction is `not_found`, `processed`, `confirmed`, `finalized` or `failed`.

Once the transaction is confirmed, the call queues the registered pools it touched for the indexer, which reads them in the background straight away (`queued_pools`). It is limited to 30 calls a minute per person (`rate_limited`).

### Treasury tools

| Tool | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_treasury_attester` | Builder, Mynt admin | Mynt's attester key, to name in a pool's attesters |
| `register_treasury_pool` | The pool's product's builder, Mynt admin | Names a pool's treasury, checked on chain |
| `prepare_treasury_deposit` | Liquidity provider | An unsigned deposit for the person's own wallet to sign |
| `prepare_treasury_withdrawal` | Liquidity provider | An unsigned withdrawal request for the person's own wallet to sign |
| `get_wallet_balances` | Liquidity provider | SOL and USDC of one of their own linked wallets |
| `get_treasury_tx_status` | Liquidity provider, builder, licence provider, Mynt admin | Whether a sent transaction landed |
| `configure_treasury_mainnet` | Mynt admin | Whether treasury mainnet is on and ready; turns it on or off |

### Treasury settings

The server's settings, by name:

| Setting | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL_DEVNET` | The devnet RPC. The public endpoint by default |
| `SOLANA_DEVNET_USDC_MINT` | Circle's devnet USDC by default |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET` | The mainnet RPC, needed for treasury mainnet |
| `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` | Seals the attester |
| `TREASURY_INDEX_POLL_MS`, `TREASURY_INDEX_PER_POLL` | The indexer's pace |
| `TREASURY_WATCH_POLL_MS` | How often the watch reads each program |
| `TREASURY_MIN_UPGRADE_TIMELOCK_HOURS` | The shortest time lock a multisig may have (48 by default) |

### Before mainnet

Devnet takes the treasury as it is. Before any treasury holds mainnet money, three things are required. All three are built.

#### Approvals bound to the deposit

The template's `MYNTDEP3` approval signs the exact amount, and `deposit` moves the position's nonce on every deposit, so an approval admits one deposit of that amount.

Mynt records every MYNTDEP3 approval it issues (`treasury_approvals`) in the same transaction it signs it in, under a lock per firm and pool. It checks the firm's limit exactly, under one lock per pool. The limit counts:

- the on-chain principal of every wallet that counts for the firm: linked to its people now, or ever approved by Mynt for this firm in this pool (`treasury_firm_wallets`), so unlinking a wallet frees no room;
- every approval that can still land, whichever firm it was issued to.

An approval can still land when it is unexpired (by the cluster's own clock, read with the positions, or by Mynt's less two minutes) and at a nonce the wallet hasn't passed. Of several at one nonce only the largest counts, since only one can land.

Further rules:

- A program redeployed since its pool was registered gets no approvals (`program_upgraded`) until it is registered again.
- A pool reports `firm_limit: "exact"` only for a verified build on MYNTDEP3. An unverified build's layout is its builder's word, so its limit is shown as advisory.
- Pools still on the earlier `MYNTDEP2` build keep it on devnet, where Mynt's limit check stays advisory. Mainnet takes only MYNTDEP3 builds.

#### A pool's cluster checked against the chain it is on

The program binds an approval to `pool.cluster`, which the pool's creator sets and the program doesn't check. One program id can be deployed on several clusters at the same pool addresses.

- Mynt reads a treasury only through an RPC checked against the cluster's genesis hash.
- It refuses a pool whose `cluster` isn't that chain's genesis hash (`wrong_cluster`), on devnet and on mainnet.
- On mainnet it also requires a program id no devnet treasury uses.

A devnet approval can never admit a deposit into a pool Mynt registered on mainnet.

#### Only verified builds at their own address with a locked upgrade authority

Both are checked for every pool and listed in its `mainnet_blockers`. Mainnet itself stays off (`mainnet_disabled`) until a Mynt admin turns it on, a separate decision.

### Verified builds and upgrade locks

#### Verified build

Mynt rebuilds the treasury template at a pool's own program id itself.

- `core/src/treasury-template.ts` writes the template with its declared id swapped for the pool's: in the program's `declare_id!`, `Anchor.toml` and the extension probe. A template change that adds or drops one fails loudly.
- A worker (`buildTick`, once a minute, one at a time) builds it in an agent sandbox with Mynt's verifiable build script, as CI does. It reads back the program's hash, its declared id and its Cargo.lock (`treasury_builds`, one per program id and template build).
- A pool is a verified build when its deployed bytes are that build. The template's own id is checked against the manifest directly.

Queueing and retries:

- The first registration of a program id queues the rebuild (at most three waiting per person).
- Pools on that id are re-judged when it finishes, except one redeployed since it was registered, which is told to register again.
- A failed rebuild is retried when the pool is registered again, and after three failures a day after the last.
- The worker claims a rebuild before creating its sandbox, never runs two at once, and fails a rebuild whose sandbox is gone.

CI's `solana-treasury` job builds the template at a fresh id with the same code and checks it the same way. Only a verified MYNTDEP3 build has an exact firm limit.

#### Upgrade lock

At registration Mynt reads who can change the program:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `immutable` | No upgrade authority |
| `timelocked_multisig` | The authority is a vault of the Squads v4 multisig named in `upgrade_multisig`, which has no config authority, needs at least two of its voting members, and has a time lock of at least `TREASURY_MIN_UPGRADE_TIMELOCK_HOURS` (48 by default) |
| `unlocked` | Anything else, with the reason |

- A multisig's config changes go through the same proposals and time lock.
- A program whose data can't be read is unlocked, never immutable.
- Mynt approves no deposits to a pool whose program was redeployed or whose upgrade authority changed since registration (`program_upgraded`).
- Mynt approves no deposits to a pool whose multisig has since been weakened: a shorter time lock, a lower threshold, or no longer locked (`upgrade_lock_changed`). The pool is recorded as unlocked.
- A time lock shorter than the pool's lock-in plus notice is a mainnet blocker: depositors couldn't leave before an approved upgrade runs.

What stays out of Mynt's reach: Squads' own program is upgradeable by Squads, and two members may be one party.

#### Asking for mainnet

`register_treasury_pool` with `cluster: "mainnet"`, when Mynt has a mainnet RPC, reads the treasury there and returns `mainnet_checks`:

- the pool bound to mainnet's genesis hash;
- a verified build (a rebuild is queued only for the pool's own builder);
- the upgrade lock;
- MYNTDEP3;
- USDC;
- a program id no devnet treasury uses;
- attesters exactly `[Mynt's mainnet attester, none]`;
- the caller owning the pool;
- a pool that isn't sandbox.

It registers the pool on mainnet only when treasury mainnet is on and every check passes. Otherwise it registers nothing (`mainnet_disabled`).

### Treasury mainnet

#### Off until a Mynt admin turns it on

`configure_treasury_mainnet` with no arguments says whether treasury mainnet is on and whether the server is ready. Ready means:

- a mainnet RPC (`SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET`, checked against mainnet's genesis hash);
- the vault for Mynt's **mainnet attester**, a key of its own (`get_treasury_attester` with `cluster: "mainnet"`). It signs only mainnet approvals; the devnet attester signs only devnet's.

`enabled: true` turns it on only when ready (`mainnet_not_ready`). `enabled: false` turns it off at once.

Both are audited (`treasury_mainnet_enabled`, `treasury_mainnet_disabled`), as is each mainnet registration (`treasury_mainnet_registered`).

#### While it is on

A mainnet treasury works as a devnet one does, on mainnet:

- Approvals name mainnet's genesis hash and come from the mainnet attester.
- Deposits take Circle's USDC (`EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v`).
- `get_wallet_balances` and `get_treasury_tx_status` take `cluster: "mainnet"`.
- The indexer reads mainnet pools from mainnet.

Every mainnet deposit re-checks that the switch is on, the pool isn't sandbox, its offering is cleared, and it is still a verified MYNTDEP3 build with a locked upgrade authority, as well as everything a devnet deposit checks.

Separation between clusters:

- Each operation reads only its pool's own cluster. What Mynt caches or re-judges per pool is kept per cluster.
- A pool on mainnet is never registered back onto devnet.
- A devnet treasury can't share a mainnet treasury's program id (`cluster_mismatch`).
- A mainnet treasury can't move to another address while it still holds deposits, and an address with devnet records can't become one.
- A multisig's time lock must cover the pool's lock-in plus notice, at registration and at every deposit.

`get_wallet_balances` and `get_treasury_tx_status` read mainnet even with the switch off, when Mynt has a mainnet RPC.

Asking for the mainnet attester's address (`get_treasury_attester`) creates that key in the vault the first time. It holds no funds.

#### Turned off

With the switch off, or for a pool no longer passing, Mynt prepares no mainnet deposits and signs no approvals.

Withdrawal requests are never held to the conditions for depositing. They are still prepared, and the program pays them on its own terms.

#### The watch

Every five minutes (`TREASURY_WATCH_POLL_MS`), for every registered pool on either cluster, Mynt reads its program's last-deployed slot and upgrade authority, and its multisig when one holds it.

A redeploy, a new authority, or a multisig no longer locked or weaker than registered sets the pool's `program_flag`. The flag is audited as `treasury_program_flagged` and counted in `ops_status`. Mynt approves no deposits to the pool (`program_changed`) until its builder registers it again.

An unreadable chain flags nothing. Deposits still re-check the program themselves.

#### What is still the operator's before turning it on

- a mainnet RPC provider;
- the human audit of the treasury program;
- the legal review of liquidity deposits;
- the mainnet program gate letting the verified template through. It still refuses programs that move tokens.

## Solana programs

This file covers how an app's Solana program is reserved, built by the coding agents, rebuilt by Mynt, deployed, called and watched; the review every mainnet deploy passes (the mainnet program gate); and how Turnkey can hold the mainnet deploy authority. It is for builders with on-chain programs, and for Mynt admins and operators who run the gate and custody.

See also: [Apps and builds](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md), [Liquidity pools and on-chain treasuries](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md), [Firms, licences and licence providers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md), [Vendors and the marketplace](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md), [Running Mynt](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md).

Some apps need a program on Solana (a smart contract) beside them. Builders build them with the coding agents and deploy them through Mynt (`core/src/solana/`). Programs are builder- and firm-side only: customers never see crypto, only dollars.

### Lifecycle

A program goes through six steps, in this order:

1. [Reserve the address](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#reserve-the-address)
2. [Build it](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#build-it)
3. [Mynt builds it again](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#mynt-builds-it-again)
4. [Deploy and upgrade](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#deploy-and-upgrade)
5. [Call it](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#call-it)
6. [Events](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#events)

#### Reserve the address

`reserve_program_id` gives the program its address before any code exists. It takes `name`, `cluster` (`devnet` or `mainnet`) and the `app_id` or `product_id` the program belongs to.

- Mynt generates the address's keypair and seals it in its vault (`MYNT_VAULT_KEY`). It is used once, at the first deploy, then deleted.
- The program declares the address in `declare_id!` and `Anchor.toml`. Mynt deploys only a program that does.

#### Build it

`start_build` gives the coding agents the Solana toolchain (`solana: true`, on by default when the app has reserved programs) and the app's reserved addresses in the build spec.

- The agents scaffold an Anchor workspace in `solana/` from `core/workspaces/coding-build/templates/solana-program/`: a minimal ledger that emits an event per entry, with its tests and a committed `Cargo.lock`.
- They test it with `anchor test` on a local validator.
- They never deploy anything.

#### Mynt builds it again

Mynt never deploys the agent's artifact, and none of the builder's code runs on the verify machine before Mynt has the program.

##### Fetch

Mynt fetches the source into its clean verify sandbox, checks its hash, and reads the answer itself: does the archive have an Anchor workspace?

##### Build in a container only

If it does, a run of its own (`verify.sh --solana-build`, with `solana-verify.sh build` from `core/src/solana/toolchain.ts`) compiles each program crate with `cargo build-sbf` inside Anchor's verifiable-build image, pinned by digest. This is the same command `anchor build --verifiable` runs there, so the program is reproducible.

1. **A throwaway container with a network fetches the crates.** It gets only a skeleton of the source: the `Cargo.toml` files, `Cargo.lock` and empty stub files. It gets no `.cargo/` config, no `rust-toolchain.toml`, no build script and no code. The compiler and every rustc wrapper are pinned by environment. So nothing of the builder's runs while there is a network.
2. **A fresh container compiles offline.** It is created with no network at all and no mount of the host. It gets the full source as a copy, plus the crate caches and lock from the fetch container (streamed container to container; the fetch container is removed before the build starts). It compiles as its own main process.
3. **The container stops when the build ends.** Nothing the builder's build scripts, macros or wrappers left running can touch the program afterwards.

Details:

- Mynt pins the image's own Rust for cargo itself and resolves dependencies to versions the platform tools can build. A workspace's own cargo config applies only inside the offline build.
- The program comes out with `docker cp -L`, which resolves a link inside the container instead of copying it out as a link to a host path. It is kept only if it is a regular ELF file.
- Program crate names must be plain identifiers (`^[a-z0-9_]+$`).
- The skeleton the fetch container gets stubs every place cargo looks for a target: `[lib]`, `src/main.rs`, and named `[[bin]]`, `[[example]]`, `[[test]]` and `[[bench]]` targets at their paths or cargo's default ones.
- `anchor build --verifiable` itself isn't used, because after its container it builds the IDL on the host, compiling and running the builder's build scripts and macros there.

##### Capture

When that run ends, Mynt kills every process and container of the sandbox's user, reads each program back into its own server and hashes it there.

- It reads only a regular file, never through a link, and stores it only if it is an ELF program.
- The hash is sha256 of the program with its trailing zero padding removed: the same "executable hash" `solana-verify` reports and the on-chain bytes give.
- Mynt stores those bytes with the build, and records the `solana_build` check itself. A row of that name in the later report is ignored.

##### Test

Mynt writes its scripts into the sandbox again, then runs the checks. Among them, the workspace's IDL is built (`anchor idl build`) and its `anchor test` runs on a local validator against the bytes Mynt hashed.

Test setups that would run other code at the programs' addresses are refused: `[[test.genesis]]`, validator clones, preloaded accounts, or `[programs.localnet]` pointing elsewhere.

##### Re-check

Afterwards Mynt hashes every copy of the program again. If any changed, the build is `blocked`.

##### The lock the build used

Mynt records the sha256 of the `Cargo.lock` the build compiled with (read back from the build container) next to each program's hash, on the program and on each version (`get_program`), so anyone can rebuild exactly those bytes.

- A source without a committed `Cargo.lock` still builds, with a warning in `solana_build` to commit it. The fetch container resolves one first, and that is the lock the build uses and records. See [Lock pins](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#lock-pins).
- A committed `Cargo.lock` is used exactly as committed.

##### Readiness checks

Two checks join the build's readiness, `solana_build` and `solana_tests`. Either failing fails the build. Deploys use only the bytes Mynt stored.

CI's `solana-program` job follows the same path, and checks that a build script rewriting the program on the host neither changes what is captured nor goes unnoticed.

#### Deploy and upgrade

`deploy_program` (`program_id`, `build_id`) deploys the program Mynt built from a **succeeded** build whose program declares the reserved address.

- Mynt deploys it itself, with the upgradeable BPF loader: a buffer account, the program written in chunks, then deploy, with twice the program's size reserved for upgrades.
- A failed deploy closes its buffer to recover the rent.

`upgrade_program` replaces the code from a newer verified build at the same address. The same bytes, or a program larger than the reserved space, are refused.

Both run in the background. `get_program` shows progress, every version with its build, hash and transaction, and recent events. `list_programs` lists a builder's programs.

##### When a deploy goes wrong

- **It landed, but Mynt didn't see it confirmed** (a timeout, a restart). Before sending anything, Mynt reads what the chain holds at the address. If that is exactly the build's program under Mynt's signer, it is recorded as deployed (or upgraded) instead of being sent again or refused. If it is an earlier build of the same program that shipped (the owner's, or someone's in the owner's firm) under Mynt's signer, that build is recorded first and the new one goes through as an upgrade, with the operation held throughout.
- **Its job died.** A running deploy refreshes its timestamp after every batch of writes. One that has gone 30 minutes without that is reconciled the same way, on the HTTP server's indexer polls only (a stdio server or a CLI command sharing the database never touches it). Otherwise it is marked interrupted and can be started again.
- **Someone sent lamports to the reserved address** (it is public once reserved). As the Solana CLI does, Mynt tops the account up, sizes it and assigns it to the loader, signed by the program's own keypair, instead of failing to create it.
- **The wrong network.** Each RPC must answer the cluster's genesis hash before Mynt sends it anything, so a devnet URL pointing at mainnet (or the reverse) is refused.
- **The RPC is rate-limiting** (see [RPC limits](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#rpc-limits)). Each call waits and tries again. A batch of writes whose blockhash expired meanwhile, or that wasn't confirmed in time, is signed again on a fresh blockhash, and only its unlanded writes are sent again. A write puts the same bytes at the same offset, so sending it twice is harmless.

A deploy that still gives up keeps the program retryable. Nothing at the program's address is created before its buffer is written, and the buffer it couldn't close is closed by the next deploy or upgrade of that program before it writes a new one.

##### The registry

The registry records, per program: its address, the app or product it belongs to, cluster, version, verifiable-build hash, deployer, upgrade authority, signer backend, deploy transaction and status.

The status is `reserved`, `deploying`, `deployed`, `failed` or `closed`.

#### Call it

- `simulate_program_call` runs an instruction without sending it. It returns logs, compute used and any error.
- `call_program` simulates first and sends only if the simulation succeeds.

An instruction is an Anchor `method` (snake_case; Mynt adds the discriminator) with `args_base64` (Borsh-encoded arguments), or raw `data_base64`, plus its accounts.

Each builder has two keys per cluster in Mynt's vault:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Fee payer | Pays every call's fees. It is never passed to a program, so no program can spend it |
| Caller key (`"$caller"` in the accounts) | Signs only when the call lists it as a signer. It is the only signer a call may have |

A call may never include Mynt's deploy authority or the fee payer, so one firm's program can never act with a key that controls another's.

##### Funding call keys

On devnet, Mynt funds a builder's keys before it simulates. A fee payer that doesn't exist on chain yet fails a simulation with `AccountNotFound`.

- The fee payer is funded to 0.005 SOL.
- The caller, when the call lists `$caller` as a signer or writable, is funded to 0.02 SOL. That is enough for the rent of a typical small account an Anchor `initialize` creates with `payer = caller`.
- A bigger account's shortfall is read from the simulation's own log and sent before simulating once more.

Mynt asks the devnet faucet first. When the faucet refuses (it rate-limits servers), Mynt's devnet deploy authority sends just the shortfall in a separate system transfer to the builder's own key:

| Limit | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At most this much at once | `SOLANA_DEVNET_TOPUP_MAX_SOL` | 0.05 |
| At most this much per builder in any 24 hours | `SOLANA_DEVNET_TOPUP_DAILY_SOL` | 0.25 |
| Never what would leave the authority with less than this | `SOLANA_DEVNET_AUTHORITY_KEEP_SOL` | 0.1 |

Every top-up is in the audit log (`solana_devnet_topup`, with its source, amount and signature). That transfer is not a call: the deploy authority still never signs, pays for or appears in a builder's transaction.

On mainnet nothing is funded automatically. A simulation or call with an unfunded fee payer is refused with the fee payer's address to fund.

#### Events

Mynt's indexer polls every deployed program's new transactions: every `SOLANA_INDEX_POLL_MS` (default 30 s), up to 1,000 per program per poll, oldest first, the rest on the next poll, none skipped.

| Event on the owning firm's webhooks | When |
| --- | --- |
| `program.event` | Each Anchor event the program itself logged (`emit!`), with the event's name from the build's IDL and its data in base64. Once each |
| `program.deployed` | A deploy |
| `program.upgraded` | An upgrade |

Devnet events are sandbox deliveries. Mainnet's are live. See [Firm webhooks](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#firm-webhooks).

### Signers

Every deploy, upgrade and call goes through one signer interface (`core/src/solana/signer.ts`):

| Backend | Cluster | How it signs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `devnet-vault` | devnet | A Mynt-generated key sealed in the vault. Mynt asks the devnet faucet for rent. When the faucet's limit is reached, the error names the address to fund. The same key tops up builders' devnet call keys when the faucet refuses them, within the limits in [Funding call keys](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#funding-call-keys) |
| `mainnet-vault` | mainnet | A key in Mynt's vault, generated by `configure_solana_signer` (only its address is ever shown) or imported by the operator on the server with `mynt solana import-key --cluster mainnet --file <keypair.json>`. Needs `SOLANA_MAINNET_VAULT_SIGNER=enabled` on the server |
| `custody-service` | mainnet | [Turnkey](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#turnkey-custody) holds the deploy authority, an Ed25519 Solana account in a Turnkey wallet, and signs each transaction without Mynt seeing the key. Needs the three `TURNKEY_*` settings on the server |
| `multisig` | mainnet | A multisig (Squads style) holds the upgrade authority and its members approve each change as a proposal. The interface is in place. Until a multisig client is connected it refuses |

### Closing a program

`close_program`, for Mynt admins, closes a deployed devnet program for good.

- It uses the upgradeable loader's Close instruction on the program's data. The accounts are the program data, the recipient, the upgrade authority as signer, and the program.
- It is signed by Mynt's devnet deploy authority, so the program data's rent comes back to that authority.
- Closing is refused unless the chain shows Mynt's devnet authority as the program's upgrade authority.
- A leftover deploy buffer is closed too.
- The program can't run or be deployed again. Its record is marked `closed`, and the close is audited with the signature and the lamports returned.
- Mainnet programs are refused. Mynt never closes one.

`remove_app` closes each deployed devnet program of the app this way before deleting anything. See [Removing a test app](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#removing-a-test-app).

### Mainnet

Mainnet is off until a Mynt admin turns it on. Every mainnet deploy, upgrade, simulation and call is refused with "Mainnet signer not configured: …", naming everything still missing, until all of these hold:

1. `SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET` is set.
2. A Mynt admin has chosen a backend with `configure_solana_signer`, and that backend is ready:
   - for `mainnet-vault`: the server flag and a key in the vault;
   - for `custody-service`: Turnkey's settings set, its API key pair matching, and a custody address configured.
3. The admin has set `enabled: true`.

Also:

- Program calls on mainnet sign with per-builder vault keys, so they need the `mainnet-vault` backend.
- Every mainnet deploy and upgrade needs an approved review from the [mainnet program gate](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#mainnet-program-gate).
- `configure_solana_signer` with no arguments shows the current state.
- `list_all_programs` shows every program on both clusters.

### Toolchain

The toolchain is pinned in `core/schemas/solana-toolchain.json`. Each download is checked against its sha256 before use. It holds:

- Agave: the Solana CLI, `solana-test-validator` and `cargo-build-sbf`;
- the Anchor CLI, built from its tagged commit where the release binary's glibc is too new;
- Rust, through rustup;
- Anchor's verifiable-build image, by digest;
- the `@coral-xyz/anchor` client the template's tests use.

It installs under `~/.mynt-solana` in the background when a Solana build's sandbox starts: about 2 GB, a few minutes. Agave publishes Linux binaries for x86_64 only.

CI's `solana-program` job installs the same toolchain with the same script, and builds and tests the template program the same way Mynt's verify sandbox does.

Every program Mynt builds, every deployed version and `get_program` record the exact toolchain (`toolchain`: versions, image digest and the pins' sha256), so an old version can be rebuilt with the same tools.

#### Lock pins

When a program's source commits no `Cargo.lock`, Mynt resolves one in the fetch container. It then moves any crate on the pin list, `core/schemas/solana-lock-pins.json`, back to the release named there. A committed `Cargo.lock` is never changed.

How Mynt resolves a lock:

1. It resolves with Cargo's MSRV-aware resolver (`CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_RUST_VERSIONS=fallback`), from each program's `rust-version` (1.84 in the template).
2. For each pin, it moves any locked version of the crate from `from` up to, but not including, `below` to `precise`.

Each pin in the file has `crate`, `from`, `below`, `precise` and `why`. `core/src/solana/toolchain.ts` reads the file.

Why pins exist: the SBF platform tools compile with their own, older Cargo (1.84 with Anchor 0.32.1). It can't even read a crate that needs edition 2024, and the resolver can't avoid one that a compatible crate requires outright.

The one pin today:

| Crate | From | Below | Pinned to | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ahash` | 0.8.13 | 0.9.0 | 0.8.12 | `ahash` 0.8.13 (Rust 1.60) requires `getrandom` 0.4 (edition 2024) for wasm32, and a `Cargo.lock` lists every target's crates |

A pin is removed when the toolchain moves to a Cargo that reads the newer release.

A committed `Cargo.lock` is used exactly as committed. If a crate in it needs a newer Cargo, the build fails and says to pin it with `cargo update -p <crate>@<version> --precise <older>`.

The starter program and Mynt's own program (`core/programs/product-health`) commit a `Cargo.lock` resolved the same way, so their builds don't change when crates.io does.

- `node core/scripts/solana-lock.mjs <workspace>...` (after `npm run build` in `core/`) regenerates them in the pinned image. A toolchain bump that moves Anchor or the image needs this.
- CI's `solana-program` job fails while a committed lock is stale.
- The same job builds the template with its committed lock (used unchanged, no warning) and once without one (resolved, built, with the warning).

#### Keeping the toolchain current

`.github/workflows/solana-toolchain-watch.yml` runs `core/scripts/solana-toolchain-watch.mjs` every Monday, and on demand.

It finds new stable releases that have been public for at least `TOOLCHAIN_MIN_RELEASE_AGE_DAYS` (default 3):

- Anchor's patch releases by default, or its newest release with `anchor_line: latest`, with its verifiable-build image (the Solana Foundation's registry preferred);
- Agave on the line that Anchor release builds its image with;
- Rust stable;
- rustup;
- the client.

It computes their sha256s and the image digest itself, and checks RustSec (through OSV) and GitHub's advisory database for the pinned and proposed versions.

It opens a pull request that rewrites:

- the pins;
- the template program;
- the treasury template's toolchain strings: its `rust-toolchain.toml` channel and the `toolchain` its manifest `core/schemas/solana-treasury-template.json` names. It never rewrites the treasury's build hashes, which CI's `solana-treasury` job checks and a person re-records after re-reviewing the treasury when Agave, Anchor or the image moves;
- the version-matched docs the coding agents read (`core/workspaces/coding-build/docs/solana`, Anchor's and Agave's docs at the pinned tags);
- the vendored `solana-dev` skill, at its latest tagged release, or a commit at least as old as the minimum age, with a link to the upstream diff.

What the pull request's title says:

- When an advisory affects a pinned tool and the proposed versions are clear of it: **URGENT (security advisory): fixes GHSA-…**
- When they aren't: **advisory GHSA-… still unfixed upstream; this bump doesn't address it**. That one isn't urgent, and the body says so too.
- **BREAKING** for a new Anchor or Agave major or minor.

How it runs:

- The watcher runs with read-only access and hands a patch to a second job that only commits it and opens the pull request.
- A failure to open the pull request fails the run and opens an issue.
- Its CI is the `solana-program` job.

**A person reviews every toolchain-watch pull request before it is merged. They are excluded from any standing instruction to merge green pull requests.**

The repository must allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests (Settings, Actions, General, "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"), or hold a GitHub App installation token scoped to this repository as the `TOOLCHAIN_WATCH_TOKEN` secret.

#### Pre-built environment

Where the sandbox host can snapshot a machine (Freestyle can; boat.dev can't), Mynt installs the toolchain and pulls the image once, in a machine that runs only Mynt's scripts.

1. Mynt hashes what the machine holds: every file, mode and link of the toolchain, the SBF platform tools, `~/.docker`, `~/.cargo` and `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, and the image's id, digests and layers.
2. It keeps that hash in its database and snapshots the machine.
3. Solana build and verify sandboxes then boot from the snapshot and re-hash it with Mynt's own script before anything else runs. The toolchain's env file, which agents wait for, is held back until it passes.

The snapshot is used only when the hash matches. On a mismatch, or any check that doesn't finish cleanly, the toolchain and image are wiped (by Mynt itself when the check didn't) and installed from the pinned, checksum-verified downloads, or the verify sandbox is replaced by a plain one.

This is drift detection, not tamper-proofing. It runs with the snapshot's own tools, and the supply chain is protected by the pinned checksums and digest, as without a snapshot.

Other details:

- A booted VM's randomness is reseeded with a per-VM nonce from Mynt.
- The snapshot is keyed by the pins, the scripts, the host's machine setup and the sandbox type.
- It is rebuilt when older than `SOLANA_BUILD_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 7).
- Another key's snapshot is deleted only after nothing has booted from it for six hours.
- Mynt admins see it, build it ahead of time or replace it with `solana_build_environment`.
- `SOLANA_BUILD_SNAPSHOT=off` turns it off.

### Solana settings

| Setting | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` | Required. Programs' and signers' keys are sealed with it |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL_DEVNET` | Default: the public devnet endpoint |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET` | No default. It may carry a provider key, so it is treated as a secret and never shown |
| `SOLANA_MAINNET_VAULT_SIGNER=enabled` | Only for the `mainnet-vault` backend |
| `TURNKEY_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `TURNKEY_API_PUBLIC_KEY`, `TURNKEY_API_PRIVATE_KEY` | Only for the `custody-service` backend. The private key is a secret |
| `TURNKEY_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Optional |
| `SOLANA_INDEX_POLL_MS`, `SOLANA_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS` | Optional |
| `SOLANA_RPC_MAX_RPS`, `SOLANA_RPC_MAX_RETRY_SECONDS` | Optional. See [RPC limits](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#rpc-limits) |
| `SOLANA_DEVNET_TOPUP_MAX_SOL`, `SOLANA_DEVNET_TOPUP_DAILY_SOL`, `SOLANA_DEVNET_AUTHORITY_KEEP_SOL` | Optional. Devnet call-key top-ups; see [Funding call keys](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#funding-call-keys) |
| `SOLANA_BUILD_SNAPSHOT`, `SOLANA_BUILD_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_DAYS` | Optional. See [Pre-built environment](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#pre-built-environment) |

RPC calls follow Mynt's outbound rules: HTTPS, no private or loopback addresses, no redirects, time and size limits.

The gate's own settings are in [Budget](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#budget) and [Retention](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#retention).

#### RPC limits

The public devnet endpoint Mynt uses by default is rate-limited per address. Solana documents 100 requests per 10 seconds in all and 40 per 10 seconds for any one method. A deploy sends one write transaction per kilobyte or so of program: about 450 for a 450 KB program.

Mynt copes in two ways.

**Pacing.** A deploy's buffer writes go out at `SOLANA_RPC_MAX_RPS` requests a second, shared by every deploy on that cluster.

- By default that is 4 a second on the public devnet endpoint (about two minutes for 450 writes).
- It is 25 a second when `SOLANA_RPC_URL_DEVNET` names another RPC, and on mainnet.
- Setting `SOLANA_RPC_MAX_RPS` sets both clusters' pace.

**Retrying.**

- A call answered with HTTP 429 or 503, or with a JSON-RPC error that means rate limiting (code -32005, or wording such as "Too many requests"), is retried with exponential backoff and jitter. It waits what a `Retry-After` header asks for (seconds or a date, at most 60 s a time).
- HTTP 502 and 504, which can come back after the node took the request, are retried only for calls that are safe to repeat: reads, and `sendTransaction`, because a signed transaction lands once by its signature however often it is sent.
- An airdrop isn't sent twice. A rate-limited airdrop fails at once instead of waiting: the faucet's limit lasts hours, so Mynt funds another way.
- One call waits at most `SOLANA_RPC_MAX_RETRY_SECONDS` in all (default 120) and then fails with a message that says the RPC was still rate-limiting. The message never includes the RPC's URL or host, which may carry a provider's key.

For faster devnet deploys, the operator sets `SOLANA_RPC_URL_DEVNET` on the server to a devnet URL from an RPC provider. Like the mainnet URL, it may carry the provider's key, so it is set by the operator in the server's environment and never shown.

#### What the operator provides for mainnet

- A mainnet RPC provider's URL as `SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET`.
- A signer choice.
- SOL for whoever pays deploys: about 0.021 SOL per KB of program. The program data reserves twice its size, and the upload buffer holds a copy until the deploy.
  - With `mainnet-vault`, that is the deploy authority's address.
  - With `custody-service`, that is the **deploy payer** (`deploy_payer` in `configure_solana_signer`). The custody address needs none.
- SOL at each builder's fee-payer address for calls, and at their caller address when their programs make the caller pay rent.

### Mainnet program gate

Every mainnet deploy and every mainnet upgrade passes a review first (`core/src/solana/mainnet-gate.ts`).

- `deploy_program` and `upgrade_program` on mainnet are refused unless an **approved** review covers exactly the build's program (its verifiable-build hash).
- Devnet is unchanged and has no gate.
- Without the gate (no sandboxes, no agent backend, or no `PUBLIC_URL`), mainnet deploys are refused. It fails closed.

The review has four parts: [hard rules](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#hard-rules), a [white-box audit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#white-box-audit), a [black-box red team](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#black-box-red-team), and [sign-off and timelock](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#sign-off-and-timelock).

#### Gate tools

| Tool | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
