pages.markdown:
## The system in one picture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph People MC["MCP clients and Mynt Studio
consumers · builders · licence providers
vendors · liquidity providers · Mynt admins"] APP["Builders' apps
api/ (app key)"] DEV["Customers' devices
web / mobile (client session)"] end subgraph Mynt["Mynt server (one Node process: core/src/index.ts serve-http)"] HTTP["HTTP front door
core/src/http.ts"] MCP["MCP server, tools per role
core/src/server.ts + feature modules"] RT["Runtime API /v1
core/src/runtime-api.ts"] PROXY["Agent proxy /agent
core/src/agent-proxy.ts"] CORE["Domain core
regulatory · regime · definition · pins · vendors · vault"] WORK["Background loops
webhooks · drift · health · queues · agent workers"] end PG[("Postgres
schema financial_products")] IDP["Identity provider
sign-in and organizations"] SBX["Agent sandboxes
a sandbox provider"] HOST["Hosted apps
one VM each, containers under gVisor"] VEND["Vendors' HTTPS endpoints
and licence providers' ledgers"] CONF["Confidential service
deploy/confidential"] SOL["Solana
devnet, mainnet behind a gate"] ESIGN["E-signature service"] EXT["GitHub App · model backend"] MC -- "/mcp (OAuth)" --> HTTP MC -- "sign in" --> IDP APP -- "/v1 app key" --> HTTP DEV -- "/v1/client/* session secret" --> HTTP HTTP --> MCP & RT & PROXY MCP --> CORE RT --> CORE CORE --> PG WORK --> PG IDP -- "/webhooks/clerk" --> HTTP WORK -- "start, steer, verify" --> SBX SBX -- "model calls, run token" --> PROXY PROXY --> EXT WORK -- "deploy verified commit" --> HOST HOST -- "/v1 (key added at the edge)" --> HTTP RT -- "signed calls" --> VEND VEND -- "/v1/vendor/callback" --> HTTP CORE -- "keys, sealed books" --> CONF WORK -- "deploys, snapshots, indexing" --> SOL CORE -- "documents to sign" --> ESIGN ESIGN -- "/esign/webhook" --> HTTP WORK -- "signed webhooks" --> APP ``` Everything runs in **one Node process** backed by **one Postgres database**. There is no message bus: background work is a set of in-process loops that take their work from Postgres rows. The agent and money workers run through `serialLoop` (`core/src/worker.ts`), which never overlaps itself; the simpler sweeps and indexers are plain timers (see [Background work](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#background-work)). Heavy or untrusted work never runs in that process. Coding agents, model runs, verification and hosted apps run in sandboxes and VMs that Mynt drives through their providers' APIs. Keys that Mynt's own server shouldn't be able to read can live in a separate confidential service. Mynt has six kinds of user: consumers, builders, licence providers, vendors, liquidity providers and Mynt admins. They reach it through any MCP (Model Context Protocol) client or through Mynt Studio (`platform/studio`), which is itself a client of `/mcp` acting as the signed-in user. ## The domain core The core turns "a product is a composition of regulated primitives" into data and checks. The rest of Mynt rests on it. ```mermaid flowchart TB RM["Regulatory model (per region)
regulators · licence types · GRC · law
core/src/regulatory.ts"] RPT["Regulated product types
category · actions · underlying · wrapper"] ENT["Entities · held licences · party roster · GRC folders
core/src/marketplace.ts, core/src/grc.ts, core/src/entity-grc.ts"] SP["Sponsorships
core/src/sponsorships.ts"] DEF["Product definition v2
core/schemas/financial-product.v2.schema.json
core/src/definition.ts"] REG["Regime
core/src/regime.ts"] STG["Stages: idea, staging, production
core/src/product-stages.ts"] CON["Developer contract
core/src/contract.ts"] PIN["Pins and drift
core/src/pins.ts"] DER["Derived: regime_summary, take_rate
core/src/derived.ts, core/src/take-rates.ts"] RM --> RPT RPT -- "perimeter of each line and action" --> REG DEF -- "components, providers" --> REG ENT -- "who holds which licence" --> REG SP -- "who sponsors which component" --> REG REG -- "publish blockers" --> STG DEF --> STG STG -- "frozen at production" --> CON REG --> PIN ENT --> PIN REG --> DER ``` - **Primitives.** A component is a product line (`credit`, `payments`, `exchange` and the rest, in `core/src/catalog.ts`) with an action (`issuance`, `sale`, `purchase`, `servicing` and the rest), in a country, optionally with an `underlying` and a `wrapper`. - **Perimeter and regime.** `core/src/regime.ts` finds every regulated product type in that country whose category is on the line and allows the action. From that perimeter come the regulators, the licence types that may provide it, and their obligations, filings and controls. GRC is governance, risk and compliance. - **Coverage.** Licences grant specific actions on specific product types, so coverage is exact, per component and per jurisdiction. A component is covered by the firm's own verified licence or by an approved sponsorship from a licence provider (`core/src/sponsorships.ts`, `core/src/access.ts`). Where a country licenses state by state, a product lists the states it is offered in (`offered_in`, ISO 3166-2 codes like `us-ny`) and coverage is checked in each: a state regulator's licences cover only its state, a national one's the whole country (or what its licence type's `covers` says). - **Definitions.** A v2 definition (`core/src/definition.ts`) is components joined by typed composition links (`funds`, `settles_into`, `converts_into`, `secures`, `discovers_price_for` and others), each with allowed primitive and action pairs at both ends (`x-from`, `x-to` in the schema). It also holds segments, algorithms, risk models, partner hand-offs, terms, rates, fees, limits, servicing and ACTUS-coded lifecycle events. Upstream records (personas, licences, parties, GRC records) are referenced by connection, never copied. - **Publishing is promotion.** A product moves through idea, staging and production, one step at a time (`core/src/product-stages.ts`). Staging needs a passing test and opens the product to sandbox builds only. Production publishes it: it needs a passing test of what goes live, a definition that still checks out, a verified licence or approved sponsorship covering every component, and published underlying products. Every check is Mynt's own, from its records. - **The developer contract.** Going to production freezes the developer contract (`core/src/contract.ts`: offers, actions, consent purposes, documents; never algorithms, costs or parties) with a `contract_hash`, and **pins** the composition and a hash of every entity, licence, party and vendor binding it rests on. - **Drift.** When any pinned fact changes (a licence lapses, a party ends, a vendor offering is suspended, a firm check fails), the product drifts: new enrolments pause and `product.drifted` goes out, until the state is restored or a new version is published. A state licence's drift names the states it covered; enrolments pause for the whole product, because the runtime can't tell a customer's state. Changes made through Mynt are checked at once; an hourly sweep catches expiries. - **Derived values.** `regime_summary` and `take_rate` are stored on each product and recomputed whenever anything they rest on changes, so they are cheap to read and always match the live checks. See [Products](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md) and [Firms, licences and licence providers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md). ## Workspaces and stages A workspace is a team that owns apps. With Clerk as the sign-in provider, each workspace is one organization at the identity provider. Mynt's tools write there (`core/src/org-directory.ts` is the interface, `core/src/clerk-orgs.ts` the adapter), and Mynt reads back through the organization webhook and a reconcile worker (`core/src/workspace-sync.ts`). Membership, invitations and offboarding are in `core/src/workspaces.ts`. An app moves through idea, staging and production only through Mynt's checks (`core/src/promotions.ts`, `core/src/promotion-schema.ts`). Production gates real money. `core/src/attention.ts` lists what needs a workspace's attention, `core/src/workspace-compliance.ts` its licences, obligations and audit trail, and `core/src/workspace-pnl.ts` its profit and loss. See [Workspaces and sign-in](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md). ## Agreements and oversight An app's workspace holds agreements with the firms behind its products (`core/src/app-agreements.ts`, with kinds, statuses and scopes in `core/src/app-agreements-schema.ts`). Either side proposes and the other accepts. Production needs a signed program agreement with every sponsoring licence provider. Program agreements can be signed by e-signature. `core/src/esign/provider.ts` is the interface and names no service; `core/src/esign/signwell.ts` is the adapter. A Mynt admin sets it up at run time (`core/src/esign-settings.ts`); its key is a row of the platform key vault (`core/src/platform-keys.ts`), where admins set the server's own keys, sealed by the confidential host and never returned. And `core/src/agreement-esign.ts` runs the signing flow and seals the signed copy. Under a program agreement, a licence provider runs oversight audits on the app (`core/src/agreement-audits.ts`) and sets service levels (`core/src/agreement-slas.ts`). Risk registers for apps, products and Mynt itself are in `core/src/risk-register.ts`, what a risk holds under it (factors, treatment tasks, controls, links) in `core/src/risk-detail.ts`, how every risk is graded in `core/src/risk-grading.ts`, and Mynt's own risk models in `core/src/risk-models.ts`. See [Agreements](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md) and [Risk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/risk.md). ## Money and liquidity Mynt never holds customer funds or assets. Money moves off Mynt, on rails a licence provider registered and a Mynt admin approved. Every movement passes one chokepoint, `authorizeMovement` in `core/src/money-rails.ts`: it is refused unless an approved rail fits its direction, the customer's state and its limits, and each movement is a row in the money ledger. Liquidity providers commit capital to a product's pools (`core/src/liquidity.ts`, `core/src/liquidity-schema.ts`). Withdrawals wait in a queue that a worker pays only as far as the pool's latest verified health snapshot keeps it above its minimum reserve. Product health is that snapshot (`core/src/product-health.ts`): each product's financial figures, read from the licence provider's ledger through the partner kit (`core/src/partner-kit.ts`, `core/src/partner-ledger/`), encrypted to the firms entitled to read them, and fingerprinted on chain. Licence providers set covenants on those figures (`core/src/covenants.ts`), which can alert or pause a product. The Mynt Ramp is the one on- and off-ramp for digital-asset liquidity. It is a `ramp` vendor service offered only by the firm a Mynt admin designates with `set_mynt_ramp`; `core/src/ramp-adapters/` holds the adapters and `core/src/ramp-sandbox.ts` its sandbox. See [Money rails](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/money-rails.md), [Liquidity pools and on-chain treasuries](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md) and [Product health](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/licence-providers.md#product-health). ## On-chain `core/src/solana/` holds everything that touches Solana. - **Programs.** `core/src/solana/service.ts` reserves an app's program address, deploys the bytes Mynt itself rebuilt, upgrades, calls and indexes events. The toolchain and its lock pins are in `core/src/solana/toolchain.ts` and `core/schemas/solana-lock-pins.json`. - **Signers.** `core/src/solana/signer.ts` and `core/src/solana/custody/` decide who signs: a key in Mynt's vault on devnet, and on mainnet whatever a Mynt admin configured. - **The mainnet program gate.** `core/src/solana/mainnet-gate.ts` reviews every mainnet deploy and upgrade: static analysis, hard rules (`core/src/solana/program-rules.ts`), a vulnerability database (`core/src/solana/vuln-db.ts`), an audit agent and a red-team agent, then a Mynt admin's sign-off and a timelock. - **Treasuries.** `core/src/treasury.ts` registers pools' on-chain treasuries, prepares unsigned transactions for a person's own wallet, rebuilds the treasury template at each pool's program id, and watches every pool's program, upgrade authority and multisig. - **Product health.** `core/src/solana/product-health-chain.ts` writes each snapshot's fingerprint on chain. See [Solana programs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md) and [On-chain treasuries](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#on-chain-treasuries). ## Confidential computing in the architecture Some things Mynt's own server shouldn't be able to read: the vault's root keys, licence providers' books, and the keys that sign what Mynt attests. They sit behind one interface, `ConfidentialHost` in `core/src/confidential/host.ts`, with three kinds chosen by `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST` (`confidentialHostFromEnv` in `core/src/confidential/index.ts`): | Kind | What it is | |---|---| | `local` | The default. In-process, keyed by `MYNT_VAULT_KEY`. For development, tests, and every server until the operator deploys the confidential service. It attests nothing, and says so | | `aws-nitro` | The documented deployment: the confidential service in an isolated enclave on a cloud VM (`core/src/confidential/aws-nitro.ts`) | | `gcp-confidential-space` | Kept as a second adapter: the service as a confidential-VM container (`core/src/confidential/gcp-confidential-space.ts`) | The service itself is `deploy/confidential`, deployed separately. Mynt reaches it over mutually authenticated TLS whose server key is pinned to the one the hardware attested (`core/src/confidential/remote.ts`). `core/src/confidential/shared/` is code that also runs inside the service. Which builds of the service Mynt trusts is a release record that Mynt admins announce and withdraw (`core/src/confidential/governance.ts`). See [Confidential computing](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/confidential-computing.md). ## Data All state is in one Postgres schema, `financial_products`, created on boot. Tests use PGlite, an in-process Postgres, through the same `Db` interface (`core/src/db.ts`). There are about 165 tables. `core/src/store.ts` creates the core ones; each feature creates its own, in the file named below. The table names are examples, not the full list. | Area | Created in | Example tables | |---|---|---| | People and access | `core/src/store.ts` | `users`, `invites`, `signup_blocks`, `audit_log`, `settings` | | Regulatory model | `core/src/store.ts` | `regions`, `regulated_product_types`, `regulator_product_types`, `product_categories`, `take_rates` | | Firms | `core/src/store.ts` | `entities`, `entity_parties`, `held_licenses`, `grc_records`, `key_vault`, `sponsorships`, `firm_checks`, `firm_notices` | | Products | `core/src/store.ts`, `core/src/desk.ts`, `core/src/app-ideas-schema.ts` | `products`, `product_versions`, `enrollments`, `requests`, `product_requests`, `product_request_offers`, `product_terms`, `product_ideas` | | Vendors and the ramp | `core/src/store.ts` | `service_types`, `vendor_offerings`, `vendor_conformance_runs`, `vendor_subscriptions`, `vendor_action_runs`, `vendor_usage`, `ramp_adapter_transfers`, `ramp_link_requests` | | Apps and runtime | `core/src/store.ts`, `core/src/modules.ts` | `apps`, `app_releases`, `app_journeys`, `api_keys`, `handoffs`, `app_events`, `client_sessions`, `client_evidence`, `customer_vault`, `webhooks`, `webhook_deliveries`, `sdks`, `sdk_modules`, `module_namespaces` | | Campaigns | `core/src/store.ts` | `segments`, `campaigns` | | Workspaces and stages | `core/src/workspaces.ts`, `core/src/promotion-schema.ts`, `core/src/chat-sessions-schema.ts` | `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, `workspace_invites`, `workspace_offboards`, `org_webhook_events`, `app_promotions`, `promotion_signoffs`, `chat_sessions` | | Agreements and risk | `core/src/app-agreements-schema.ts`, `core/src/agreement-esign-schema.ts`, `core/src/agreement-audits-schema.ts`, `core/src/agreement-slas-schema.ts`, `core/src/risk-register-schema.ts`, `core/src/risk-models-schema.ts` | `app_agreements`, `app_target_segments`, `agreement_templates`, `app_agreement_documents`, `agreement_audits`, `agreement_slas`, `risk_register`, `risk_factors`, `risk_treatments`, `risk_controls`, `risk_links`, `risk_grading_versions`, `risk_models` | | Money and liquidity | `core/src/store.ts`, `core/src/liquidity-schema.ts`, `core/src/covenant-schema.ts`, `core/src/product-health.ts` | `money_rails`, `money_movements`, `customer_verified_states`, `partner_ledger_sources`, `liquidity_pools`, `pool_commitments`, `pool_withdrawals`, `covenants`, `covenant_breaches`, `product_health_snapshots` | | On-chain | `core/src/solana/service.ts`, `core/src/solana/mainnet-gate.ts`, `core/src/treasury.ts`, `core/src/build-env.ts` | `solana_programs`, `solana_program_versions`, `solana_keys`, `solana_mainnet_reviews`, `treasury_pools`, `treasury_deposits`, `treasury_builds`, `solana_build_envs` | | Agents | `core/src/builds.ts`, `core/src/agent-meter.ts`, `core/src/desk.ts`, `core/src/explore.ts`, `core/src/review.ts`, `core/src/repo-approvals.ts` | `build_runs`, `build_events`, `agent_spend`, `repo_connections`, `app_repositories`, `desk_jobs`, `desk_workspaces`, `desk_reports`, `explore_jobs`, `explore_variants`, `review_cases` | | Hosting | `core/src/hosting.ts`, `core/src/usage-meter.ts` | `hosting_tenants`, `hosted_apps`, `hosting_commands`, `usage_samples` | | Connector | `core/src/bd.ts` | `bd_prospects`, `bd_contacts`, `bd_messages`, `bd_consents`, `bd_intros`, `bd_runs`, `bd_suppressions`, `bd_erasures`, `bd_settings` | | Confidential computing | `core/src/confidential/governance.ts` | `confidential_releases`, `confidential_keys` | **What is sealed.** The vault key seals the customer vault, firms' vendor credentials (`key_vault`), queued vendor results, Solana keys, the e-signature key and signed copies of agreements. While the confidential host is `local`, that key is `MYNT_VAULT_KEY`. Once the operator moves it into the confidential service, the service releases a data key into the process at boot, and `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` can be removed from the server. API keys and client session secrets are kept only as hashes. ## Background work `serve-http` starts these alongside the HTTP server (`core/src/index.ts`). The stdio server starts none of them. | Loop | Interval | Setting | Does | |---|---|---|---| | Build worker | 5 seconds | `BUILD_POLL_MS` | Starts, steers, meters, verifies and finishes coding-agent builds (`core/src/builds.ts`) | | Product desk worker | 5 seconds | `DESK_POLL_MS` | Runs desk jobs (`core/src/desk.ts`) | | Exploration worker | 5 seconds | `DESK_POLL_MS` | Runs algorithm explorations (`core/src/explore.ts`) | | Governance desk worker | 10 seconds | `REVIEW_POLL_MS` | Runs review cases (`core/src/review.ts`) | | Connector worker | 15 seconds | `BD_POLL_MS` | Runs the connector, when `BD_ENABLED` is set (`core/src/bd.ts`) | | Mainnet gate worker | 15 seconds | `PROGRAM_GATE_POLL_MS` | Runs mainnet program reviews (`core/src/solana/mainnet-gate.ts`) | | Webhook worker | 5 seconds | None | Delivers and retries signed webhooks (`core/src/runtime.ts`) | | Hosting usage worker | 5 minutes | `USAGE_SAMPLE_MS` | Samples what each hosted app's VM costs (`core/src/usage-meter.ts`) | | Sandbox usage | 5 minutes | `USAGE_SAMPLE_MS` | Samples what ended builds' sandboxes and reopened sandboxes cost. Started with the build worker (`core/src/builds.ts`) | | Product health worker | 1 minute poll; a snapshot every 60 minutes | `PRODUCT_HEALTH_POLL_MS`, `PRODUCT_HEALTH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` | Publishes each sponsored product's health snapshot. Doesn't run without `PRODUCT_HEALTH_PROGRAM_ID` (`core/src/product-health.ts`) | | Liquidity worker | 1 minute | `LIQUIDITY_POLL_MS` | Pays pools' withdrawal queues as far as verified health allows (`core/src/liquidity.ts`) | | Covenant worker | 1 minute | `COVENANT_POLL_MS` | Evaluates licence providers' rules, on its own timer so a rule about missing snapshots can fire (`core/src/covenants.ts`) | | Workspace reconcile | 15 minutes, backing off to 2 hours while the provider fails | None | Brings workspaces back in step with their organizations (`core/src/workspace-sync.ts`) | | Workspace sweep | 5 minutes | None | Retries unfinished offboardings, releases invitations that lapsed unanswered, finishes archives (`core/src/workspaces.ts`) | | Drift sweep | 1 hour | None | Checks every pinned product again; a lapsed licence drifts it (`core/src/pins.ts`) | | Firm checks | 1 hour poll; each firm every `FIRM_CHECKS_EVERY_DAYS` | `FIRM_CHECKS_POLL_MS` | Checks licence providers' firms again against outside registers (`core/src/firm-check-tools.ts`) | | Vendor, ramp and movement sweep | 1 minute | None | Expires vendor actions that never finished (`sweepVendorActionRuns`), reads back ramp transfers whose webhook hasn't come, and sweeps stale money movements (`core/src/vendors.ts`, `core/src/ramp-adapters/index.ts`, `core/src/money-rails.ts`) | | Agreement audits | 1 minute | None | Opens the next oversight audit of each requirement when its time comes (`core/src/agreement-audits.ts`) | | Solana event indexer | 30 seconds | `SOLANA_INDEX_POLL_MS` | Sends deployed programs' new events to their firms' webhooks (`core/src/solana/service.ts`) | | Treasury indexer | 30 seconds | `TREASURY_INDEX_POLL_MS` | Reads registered pools' deposits, requests and payments into Mynt's records (`core/src/treasury.ts`) | | Treasury builds | 1 minute | None | Rebuilds the treasury template at pools' program ids, one at a time | | Treasury watch | 5 minutes | `TREASURY_WATCH_POLL_MS` | Checks every pool's program, upgrade authority and multisig against what was registered | | Derived values | Once, on boot | None | Computes `regime_summary` and `take_rate` for products missing them (`core/src/derived.ts`) | The workers for builds, the desks, explorations, the connector, the mainnet gate, hosting and sandbox usage, product health, liquidity, covenants, firm checks, agreement audits, treasury builds and the treasury watch run through `serialLoop`: a run that is still going when the next is due is skipped, never doubled. The workspace sweep, the drift sweep, the vendor, ramp and movement sweep, the Solana event indexer and the treasury indexer are plain `setInterval` timers with no such guard. The webhook worker has its own guard, and the workspace reconcile schedules its next run only when one ends. The `serve-http` process also recovers Solana deploys that a previous run of it left unfinished.

pages.title: A sponsored US product, end to end
pages.markdown:
`core/scripts/sponsored-product.mjs` runs the whole path from an unlicensed builder to a developer-ready US product:

1. The licence provider's firm, registered by hand.
2. Its licences, registered and then verified by a Mynt admin, and the roster filling the stakeholders they mandate.
3. The builder's firm and its product: the money transmission template (`core/schemas/examples/us/money-transmission.v2.json`) with transmission provided by the sponsoring licence provider.
4. `request_sponsorship` and `approve_sponsorship` for every state the product is offered in.
5. `test_product`, then `publish_product`.
6. A check that `list_products` with `developer_ready` lists it.

`core/test/sponsored-product-e2e.test.js` runs the same function on an in-process server.

## The fixture

The script runs on a JSON fixture. The shipped one, `core/schemas/examples/us/sponsored-product.placeholder.json`, is a **placeholder for staging and tests only**:

- "Example Money Transmitter (placeholder)" isn't a real firm.
- Its registration numbers start `PLACEHOLDER-`.
- It has `"placeholder": true`, so the script refuses it unless told it is staging.
- It holds a FinCEN MSB registration and money transmitter licences for New York and California.

No public register can show the placeholder is a real company. Its sponsorship is approved only on a staging server running with `SPONSOR_LEGITIMACY_RULE=off`. The real licence provider passes the checks instead: a Mynt admin runs `run_firm_checks` once its LEI is recorded.

The US model (`core/schemas/regulatory/us.json`) has a money transmitter licence type for every state and the District of Columbia except Montana, which has no money transmitter licence (its regulator is kept with no licence types). To offer the placeholder product in another state, add that state's licence (its `_id` is `<regulator>_money_transmitter`) to the fixture's licences and the state to `offered_in`.

## Running it

Every step reads first and does only what is missing, so rerunning is safe and picks up where a run stopped.

Three people act, each in their own session: `MYNT_ADMIN_TOKEN`, `MYNT_LICENCE_PROVIDER_TOKEN` and `MYNT_BUILDER_TOKEN`, from the environment, never the command line. With only some of them set, the script does their steps and stops, naming who is needed next. The licence provider usually approves in its own session.

```sh
# in the repository's core/ folder
node scripts/apply-sponsored-product.mjs --url <a staging server's MCP URL> --staging --dry-run   # read only: what it would do
node scripts/apply-sponsored-product.mjs --url <a staging server's MCP URL> --staging             # run it with the placeholder
```

## When the real licence provider signs

A Mynt admin swaps the real firm in and reruns:

1. Copy the fixture (say `sponsored-product.partner.json`, kept out of the repository if it names the firm before that is public). Set `"placeholder": false` and delete `placeholder_note`.
2. Fill in `licence_provider`:
   - the firm's legal name, or `entity_id` if its firm is already on Mynt;
   - the email its person signs in with (`member_email`; invite them with the `license_provider` role first);
   - its legal form and incorporation;
   - each licence it holds as on the regulator's register: `regulator_id`, `license_id`, `registration_number`, and `valid_from` and `valid_to` when known;
   - the people who fill each stakeholder its licences mandate (`roster`).
3. Change `product.offered_in` to the states it will sponsor in.
4. Check every licence against the regulator's public register, then run with `--verify-licences`. Without it the run stops for `review_license`.

```sh
# in the repository's core/ folder
node scripts/apply-sponsored-product.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --fixture sponsored-product.partner.json --dry-run
node scripts/apply-sponsored-product.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --fixture sponsored-product.partner.json --verify-licences
```

A product already live under the placeholder gets a new version sponsored by the real firm: its definition changes, so it is saved as the draft version, sponsored, tested and published.

The placeholder firm's own sponsorship is then left over. Revoke it (`revoke_sponsorship`, as the placeholder's licence provider) and suspend its licences (`review_license`), so nothing can rest on it again.

pages.title: Set up a region's regulatory model
pages.markdown:
A region's regulatory model can be kept as data and applied in one step. This guide uses the United States.

## What the US file holds

[`core/schemas/regulatory/us.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/regulatory/us.json) is the US slice for money transmission, digital-asset on-ramps and off-ramps, and buy-and-hold stablecoin products. Each instrument names its source.

| Regulator | What the file models |
| --- | --- |
| FinCEN | The money services business registration (`fincen_msb`), with its AML, suspicious-activity, currency-transaction, funds-transfer and Travel Rule obligations, plus the OFAC, Regulation E and Form 1099-DA obligations every ramp carries |
| Each state and the District of Columbia, except Montana | A money transmitter licence, under that state's regulator (`jurisdiction: "us-xx"`) |
| NYDFS (`jurisdiction: "us-ny"`) | The money transmitter licence (`nydfs_money_transmitter`), the BitLicense and the limited purpose trust charter |
| California DFPI (`jurisdiction: "us-ca"`) | The money transmission licence (`ca_dfpi_money_transmitter`) and the Digital Financial Assets Law licence |
| OCC | The national trust bank charter and the GENIUS Act's federal payment stablecoin issuer |

Montana is kept as a regulator with no licence type, because Montana has no money transmitter licence.

The file also defines the product categories and regulated product types these cover. Applying it loads the US service types too, including the Mynt Ramp's four.

How coverage works in the file:

- A state regulator's licences cover only its state.
- The state money transmitter licences count only alongside the FinCEN registration (`requires`), which covers no state by itself (`covers: []`).
- The OCC charters cover every state (`covers: ["us"]`), each with a `coverage_note` saying that this is an assumption to verify.
- Each state licence's `coverage_note` names its main source and what is still to verify.

The state entries were built by following the pattern in the file's `description`, which is also how to add or correct one. See [Coverage per state](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#coverage-per-state).

## Apply the file

```sh
# in the repository's core/ folder
node scripts/apply-regulatory-model.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --login --dry-run   # check only: prints what would be added, updated or removed
node scripts/apply-regulatory-model.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --login             # apply
```

Sign-in works as for the seed definitions (see [Applying the seed definitions](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#applying-the-seed-definitions)).

## How the script merges

The script merges the file into what the server has. It never replaces it.

- For each category, product type, instrument and regulator in the file, it reads the server's version, merges the file into it by id, and sends the merged whole. Merging by id covers licence types, personas, product-type mappings, GRC registers and repositories, and stakeholders.
- Anything the file leaves out is kept.
- A file can hold only additions, like [`core/schemas/regulatory/in.additions.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/regulatory/in.additions.json).
- Items that end up unchanged aren't sent.
- The region's regulator names are merged, not replaced.

## Checks and removals

- The script checks every merged item against the server's own tool schemas first, and changes nothing if any is wrong.
- The dry run prints, per item, what would be added (`+`), updated (`~`, with the fields) and removed.
- Merging removes something only when a plain list in the file lacks an entry the server has (an action, a covered state, a product line), or when a shipped service type would overwrite a different version on the server.
- Any removal stops the run, changing nothing, unless you add `--allow-removals`. The removals are listed either way.
- Even with `--allow-removals`, items the file doesn't mention are never deleted. Use the `remove_*` admin tools for that.

[`core/test/us-regulatory-model.test.js`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/test/us-regulatory-model.test.js) runs exactly what the script does.

## A US product to start from

[`core/schemas/examples/us/usdc-account.v2.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/examples/us/usdc-account.v2.json) is a firm-less template for a Dollar Holding Account (`dollar-holding-account`). Customers add, hold and cash out US dollars and see dollars only.

Underneath, for the regulatory model:

- a ramp (`payments:sale`) funds a USDC purchase on Solana (`settlement_exchange`, `exchange:sale`, `digital_assets`);
- the purchase settles into custody (`settlement_custody`, `custody_settlement:servicing`);
- cashing out settles back through the ramp.

It has customer segments, KYC, sanctions screening and quoting algorithms, fees, limits, statements, lifecycle events and the FinCEN register obligations each part satisfies. On-ramp and off-ramp acceptance become the customer actions in its developer contract.

A firm takes it as is and adds:

- `owner_entity_id`;
- a `component_provided_by` for each component. A FinCEN registration covers the ramp and the exchange. Custody needs a custodian's licence, such as an OCC national trust bank charter or a NYDFS trust charter;
- its AML compliance officer, bound to the ramp and the exchange;
- its ramp handoffs, bound to its Mynt Ramp subscriptions.

The Dollar Account (`dollar-account`), in [`dollar-account.v2.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/examples/us/dollar-account.v2.json), is the other route. It builds on the money-transmission product instead of composing the ramp itself; see [Base products](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#base-products).

pages.title: Check the seed definitions
pages.markdown:
This guide checks the four seed definitions against a Mynt server and changes nothing. It takes about ten minutes the first time. You need an admin account on that Mynt server and its MCP address, which ends in `/mcp`.

The seed definitions are described in [The reference catalogue](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#the-reference-catalogue).

1. Install Node.js from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download) (the "LTS" download). Mynt needs version 22.13 or later. To check it worked, open a terminal (Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows) and type `node --version`. It should print `v22.13` or higher.
2. Download Mynt's code. In the terminal, type:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/never2average/mynt.git
   cd mynt/core
   ```

   If `git` isn't installed, download the ZIP from the repository's green **Code** button instead, unzip it, and `cd` into its `core` folder.
3. Install what the script needs:

   ```sh
   npm ci
   ```

4. Run the check, putting the server's MCP address in place of `<Mynt MCP URL>`:

   ```sh
   node scripts/apply-seed-definitions.mjs --url <Mynt MCP URL> --login --dry-run
   ```

5. Your browser opens on Mynt's sign-in page. If it doesn't, copy the link the terminal printed into your browser. Sign in with your admin account. The browser then says you can close the tab.
6. Back in the terminal you see `Signed in.`, then one line per product.
   - `valid, no publish blockers` means the product is ready.
   - `NOT READY` is followed by the reasons, such as a regulator or persona the server doesn't have yet.
   - The last line is `Dry run: 4 definition(s) checked, nothing changed.` or `Stopped: nothing was changed.`
7. Copy everything the terminal printed and send it back to whoever asked you to run the check. It contains no password or token. The only link in it is the sign-in link, which worked once and has already been used.

With `--dry-run`, the script only reads. It makes no change to the server's products, whatever it prints. The only thing it leaves behind is the sign-in itself: the sign-in service records it, and the script's registration as a sign-in client.

pages.title: The partner walkthrough
pages.markdown:
This file is for whoever presents Mynt to a prospective licence provider. It is a scripted, repeatable run of Mynt's whole flow, for showing in a meeting and for proving that the pieces work together.

It runs entirely on your own computer: nothing goes to Mynt's servers, no real company is named, and no money exists anywhere in it.

## Before the meeting

You need a copy of this repository and Node.js 22.13 or newer.

1. Open a terminal in the repository's `core` folder (the server).
2. Install and build (once, takes a minute or two):

   ```sh
   npm ci && npm run build
   ```

3. Do a practice run, so you know what the screen will show:

   ```sh
   npm run demo:partner
   ```

It takes a minute or two and prints seven numbered steps, a summary table and a "Cleaned up" list. Every row of the summary should say PASS.

## What it uses

- **A throwaway Mynt.** The real Mynt server code, started inside the script with an in-memory database, the same way Mynt's own tests run. It is created fresh for every run and removed at the end.
- **Placeholders.** "Example Money Transmitter (placeholder)" is the licence provider in the run. It is not a real firm; its legal entity identifier and licence numbers are made up and say so. The customers (Avery, Blake and Casey) are made up too.
- **Stand-ins for everyone outside Mynt.** The public registers (GLEIF and FinCEN), the identity and bank-transfer partner, the licence provider's webhook and (by default) the blockchain are small programs on your computer that answer the way the real ones do.
- **Sandbox books.** The licence provider's reserve figures are test numbers the script sets as the run goes.

## What each step shows

### Step 1: an admin adds the licence provider, and Mynt checks it is a real company

Mynt itself looks the firm up in GLEIF's register of legal entities and FinCEN's list of money services businesses, and keeps each answer with where it came from and a fingerprint of it. Until the firm passes, it can't sponsor anything.

### Step 2: a builder makes a money-transmission product, and the licence provider sponsors it

The builder holds no licence. The licence provider sponsors the product in New York and California under its state licences, and the product becomes available to builders' apps.

### Step 3: rails and identity

The licence provider proposes the routes money may take (in and out, New York and California only, with limits per transfer and per day) and a Mynt admin approves them. The licence provider also names the identity-check service it trusts to say which state a customer lives in.

### Step 4: customers

- Avery passes an identity check that says they live in New York. They deposit $250 and take a $100 payout.
- Blake's identity check fails, so their deposit is refused.
- Casey is verified but lives in Texas, where the product isn't sponsored, so their deposit is refused too.

The refused ones never reach the bank-transfer partner.

This step runs Mynt's checks in **live mode on your computer**. Mynt only refuses live transfers; in sandbox mode it labels what it would have refused, and lets builders test. Here every outside party is a local stand-in, so nothing real moves.

### Step 5: a health snapshot

A health snapshot is the periodic record of a product's financial health.

1. Mynt computes it from the licence provider's books: reserves against what is owed to customers.
2. Mynt encrypts it so only the licence provider can read it.
3. Mynt waits for the licence provider to co-sign it, which means signing the same snapshot with its own key to say it agrees with the figures.
4. Mynt records the snapshot's fingerprint on a blockchain.
5. A separate, standalone checker (`core/scripts/product-health-verify.mjs`, which uses nothing from Mynt) confirms the record: "OVERALL PASS".

### Step 6: a covenant

A covenant is a rule a licence provider sets on a product it sponsors. Here the rule is: tell us when reserves fall below 100% of what is owed.

A rule on a live product is judged on the licence provider's own books, never on sandbox figures. So the licence provider first connects its books, with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/partners.md)'s fallback for a firm without an API:

1. It registers a test key.
2. It uploads a signed test file.
3. It passes conformance, which is Mynt's test of the firm's integration: the firm runs it and sees pass or fail, case by case.
4. It uploads today's live file, signed with its live key.
5. It switches its ledger to the file.

Then the rule trips:

1. The next period's books show 95%.
2. The rule trips on those real (stand-in) books.
3. The alert arrives at the licence provider's own webhook, signed so the firm can tell it came from Mynt.

On a real server a new member of a licence provider waits 72 hours before they can connect the firm's books. The walkthrough's accounts are a minute old, so it turns that wait off and says so.

### Step 7: a liquidity pool

A liquidity pool is capital that liquidity providers commit to a product.

1. The licence provider uploads the day's new file.
2. The builder creates a pool backing the product, the licence provider approves it, and a Mynt admin records that the offering was cleared.
3. A liquidity provider puts $50,000 into the pool.
4. The liquidity provider asks for $20,000 back and is paid, because the reserve stays above its minimum.
5. A second request for $10,000 would take the reserve below its minimum, so it waits in the queue for a healthier snapshot instead of being paid.

## Leaving nothing behind

By default the run removes everything it made: the database, its working folder, the stand-in programs and the local servers, even if it stops with an error or you press Ctrl-C. The "Cleaned up" list at the end says what was removed, and anything that couldn't be.

To look around afterwards, add `--keep`:

```sh
npm run demo:partner -- --keep
```

It keeps the database and files in a folder it names, and prints the command that removes them later:

```sh
npm run demo:partner -- --cleanup-only --dir <the folder it printed>
```

## On Solana devnet (optional)

By default the blockchain is a stand-in that enforces the same rules as Mynt's product-health program. With `--devnet` the snapshots are recorded on Solana's public test network instead. That needs a product-health program deployed on devnet for demonstrations, and the key file its configuration names as the publisher. It never uses production keys, and refuses any network that isn't devnet.

```sh
npm run demo:partner -- --devnet --program-id <program address> --publisher-key <publisher-keypair.json> --funding-key <devnet-funding-keypair.json>
```

- `--funding-key` (optional) tops up the publisher with 0.02 devnet SOL if it is low, and at the end sends what is left back to the funding key.
- `--rpc` (optional) uses another devnet RPC address instead of the public one.
- What can't be cleaned up is listed with its address: each product's record on chain (its "head" account) stays, because the program deliberately has no way to delete a record. Your key files are yours and are never deleted.

## If something goes wrong

The summary marks the failing step FAIL and the line that starts "The walkthrough stopped" says why. The run still cleans up after itself. Run it again: every run starts from nothing.

pages.title: Run Mynt yourself
pages.markdown:
## Install and build

You need Node.js 22.13 or newer and a Postgres database. [Supabase](https://supabase.com) (self-hosted or cloud) is the intended backend; any Postgres 15 or newer works.

The server is the repository's `core/` folder, installed on its own from its own lockfile (`core/package-lock.json`). The apps built on it (Mynt Studio, the sample chat and the sign-in code they share) are under `platform/` and are the repository's npm workspaces: `npm ci` at the repository root installs them and never the server.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/never2average/mynt.git
cd mynt/core
npm ci
npm run build
```

The commands in the rest of this file run in `core/`. The build makes `dist/index.js`, which is the `mynt` command (`core/package.json` names it as the package's `bin`). `node dist/index.js --help` prints every command and the main settings.

## Users and tokens

Users, roles, products, enrolments and apps live in Postgres, in a dedicated `financial_products` schema. Supabase's generated REST API exposes only `public`, so none of this data is reachable through it.

Set `DATABASE_URL` to the connection string. The schema is created on first start. If the schema already exists and is owned by the server's database role (as the deploy scripts set it up), the role needs no database-level privileges.

### The seven roles

Every user and every invitation carries one or more of these roles. `--role` on the command line accepts exactly these names.

| Role | Who it is |
|---|---|
| `consumer` | A person who enrols in products |
| `developer` | A builder (the same role as `innovator`; each implies the other) |
| `innovator` | A builder |
| `vendor` | A member of a firm that offers standard services |
| `license_provider` | A member of a firm whose licences sponsor builders' products |
| `liquidity_provider` | A member of a firm or fund that puts capital into pools |
| `admin` | A Mynt admin |

How the roles nest, and what each one can do, is in [Roles and tools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/roles-and-tools.md).

### The first admin

A new server has no users. The operator makes the first Mynt admin from the command line:

```sh
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:password@host:5432/postgres
node dist/index.js users invite --email admin@example.com --role admin
```

`users invite` puts the email on Mynt's invitation list with those roles and, when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is set, on Clerk's allowlist. The person then signs in (see [Sign-in with Clerk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#sign-in-with-clerk)).

After that, Mynt admins invite everyone else from inside Mynt with `invite_user`, or from Mynt Studio's platform admin. See [Invitations](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#invitations).

### Local tokens

For stdio, or for an HTTP server that runs without Clerk, make a local user. Each command prints a token once; only its hash is stored.

```sh
node dist/index.js users add --name "Asha" --role consumer
node dist/index.js users add --name "Ines" --role innovator
node dist/index.js users add --name "Max" --role consumer --role innovator
node dist/index.js users add --name "Root" --role admin
node dist/index.js users list
```

`--role` can be given several times. `users list` prints the invitation list and the local users.

### User commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `users invite --email <email> --role <role>` | Invites an email with the roles given; also updates Clerk's allowlist |
| `users revoke --email <email>` | Removes the invitation; also removes the email from Clerk's allowlist |
| `users add --name <name> --role <role>` | Makes a local user and prints its token once |
| `users list` | Prints the invitation list and the local users |

## Run it

### Locally over stdio

One user per client. Pass the user's token in `FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN`. Without it, the server runs as a read-only guest.

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add mynt -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://... -e FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN=fpm_... -- node /absolute/path/to/mynt/core/dist/index.js
```

Claude Desktop and other clients:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mynt": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/mynt/core/dist/index.js"],
      "env": { "DATABASE_URL": "postgres://...", "FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN": "fpm_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

### Shared server over HTTP

Many users on one server:

```sh
node dist/index.js serve-http --port 3000 --host 0.0.0.0
```

`--port` defaults to `PORT` or 3000, and `--host` to `HOST` or `127.0.0.1`.

Clients connect to `http://host:3000/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) with `Authorization: Bearer fpm_...`. Without Clerk, a request with no token is served as a guest, and an invalid token gets `401`. Put the server behind TLS (for example Caddy or nginx) before exposing it publicly.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http mynt https://your-host/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer fpm_..."
```

`serve-http` is also the process that runs Mynt's background work (builds, webhook deliveries, health snapshots and the rest; see [Background work](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#background-work)). The stdio server runs none of it.

### The pseudonym secret

Set `MYNT_PSEUDONYM_SECRET` to a long random string (for example the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`) so builders can see product requests. Each requester appears to each builder under a pseudonym keyed with it. Without it, `list_product_requests` refuses to list anything. See [Product requests](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#product-requests).

## Sign-in with Clerk

Set `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `PUBLIC_URL` (the server's public origin, for example `https://mcp.example.com`), and the HTTP server accepts only invited people signed in with [Clerk](https://clerk.com). The rule itself, and what public sign-up changes, is in [Invite-only sign-in](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#invite-only-sign-in).

### How it works

- The server is an OAuth-protected resource with Clerk as its authorization server. MCP clients (Claude, Claude Code and others) discover this from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`, register themselves with Clerk and open Clerk's sign-in page.
- Each request's Clerk access token is verified, and must be issued for this server's `/mcp` resource.
- The caller's verified email must be on Mynt's invitation list. The invitation also decides the caller's roles, and removing it cuts them off on their next request.
- Local `fpm_` tokens and guests are refused over HTTP. They still work over stdio.

### Set it up

1. Set the three settings above on the server.
2. Run the one-time set-up. It turns on Clerk's allowlist, dynamic client registration, required PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) and audience claims, and copies every invited email to the allowlist:

   ```sh
   node dist/index.js clerk setup
   ```

3. Invite the first admin (see [The first admin](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#the-first-admin)).
4. Connect a client with only the address. It opens Clerk's sign-in page:

   ```sh
   claude mcp add --transport http mynt https://mcp.example.com/mcp
   ```

`clerk setup` follows the public sign-up setting: with public sign-up on, it leaves Clerk's allowlist off.

### Inviting people

There are three ways to invite someone. All three end with the same invitation in Mynt.

**From Mynt.** A Mynt admin runs `invite_user` (or uses the platform admin in Studio). This is the normal way once an admin exists.

**From the command line.**

```sh
node dist/index.js users invite --email ines@example.com --role innovator
node dist/index.js users invite --email asha@example.com --role consumer --role developer
node dist/index.js users revoke --email asha@example.com
node dist/index.js users list
```

`users invite` and `users revoke` also update Clerk's allowlist, so people who aren't invited can't sign up at all.

**From Clerk's dashboard.** This also works for the first admin.

1. In the Clerk dashboard, go to **Users**, then **Invite**. Enter the email and set **public metadata** to a `mynt_roles` list:

   ```json
   { "mynt_roles": ["admin"] }
   ```

   Any of the seven roles can be listed.
2. The person accepts Clerk's emailed invitation and signs up.
3. On their first Mynt request, Mynt invites them with those roles and writes `invite_via_clerk` to the audit log.

Only Clerk dashboard owners can set public metadata; users can't edit their own. After that first sign-in, manage the person in Mynt: role changes and revocations are written back to their Clerk metadata, so an old grant can't restore access. With Clerk's allowlist on, also add the email under **Configure**, **Restrictions**, **Allowlist**, in case the invitation alone isn't enough to sign up.

### Public sign-up

A Mynt admin can open sign-up with `set_public_signup` (`enabled: true`). It is a database setting, not an environment variable. What it does is described in [Public sign-up](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#public-sign-up). For the operator:

- Turning it on turns Clerk's allowlist off, and turning it off turns the allowlist back on. Both are best effort; Mynt's invitations decide access either way.
- `clerk setup` follows the setting.

### Mynt's own apps sign in without a consent screen

People signing in to Mynt Studio or the sample chat (Mynt's own apps) aren't asked to "allow Mynt to access Mynt". This is the one full explanation; each app's README lists only its own settings and steps.

How it works:

- Each first-party app is a pre-registered Clerk OAuth application. It is a confidential client (its secret stays on that app's server), with PKCE required and its consent screen off.
- Only an operator creates one, naming the app's exact redirect address.
- Every client that registers itself (MCP clients such as Claude, and any third party) still gets Clerk's consent screen. Clerk doesn't let a dynamically registered application turn it off, and Mynt never changes that.

The redirect address must be:

- `https` (`http` only for localhost);
- free of wildcards (`*`) anywhere, host or path;
- free of a user name or password;
- free of a query or fragment (not even a bare `?` or `#`);
- written in its normal form (lower-case host, no default port).

Anything else is refused before Clerk is asked.

Operator steps, once per app (the domain is a placeholder for that app's own):

1. On the server, run:

   ```sh
   node dist/index.js clerk first-party mynt-studio https://<studio-domain>/api/auth/callback
   ```

2. It prints the client id. The client id and its secret go to `~/.mynt/oauth-mynt-studio.json`, a file only you can read (or the path you give with `--file`); `~/.mynt` itself is kept at mode 700. The secret is never printed. If the file can't be written, the Clerk application is deleted again (its secret would otherwise be lost), and the error says whether that worked or which application to delete by hand.
3. Give the client id and secret to that app's server as its OAuth client, in place of registering itself: `MYNT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `MYNT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` for Mynt Studio and the sample chat (see [Studio's README](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/platform/studio/README.md#sign-in-without-a-consent-screen) and [the chat's README](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/platform/chat/README.md#sign-in-without-a-consent-screen)). Then delete the file.
4. Registering the same name again is refused, because the secret can't be read back. To replace the secret, rotate it in Clerk's dashboard.

Each app allows the scopes Mynt's apps ask for: `openid profile email`, the same list Mynt's protected-resource metadata publishes. An app registered before `openid` was included makes every sign-in fail with `invalid_scope`. Repair it in place, keeping its secret:

```sh
node dist/index.js clerk first-party --update-scopes mynt-studio
```

It takes the app's name or client id, says whether anything changed, and prints only the name and client id.

### When a sign-in is refused

When the authorization server refuses a sign-in, Mynt's apps tell the person why only as far as they can act on it.

| The refusal | What the person sees |
|---|---|
| `access_denied` (they declined) | "Sign-in was cancelled" |
| Anything else (`invalid_scope`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_request`, `server_error` and others) | "Sign-in isn't set up correctly on Mynt's side. Please tell your admin." |

For the second kind, the app's server logs the error code and a short, cleaned description, never the state or the code.

### Workspaces and organizations

With Clerk as the sign-in provider, each workspace is a Clerk organization. Turning that on (the webhook, `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STUDIO_URL` and `clerk sync-workspaces`) is in [Turning organizations on](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#turning-organizations-on).

pages.title: Deploy Mynt
pages.markdown:
## Deploying

There are two deployment paths in `deploy/`. Both set up Supabase's Docker stack and a least-privilege database role, and both are safe to run again for an update.

| | `deploy/setup-vm.sh` | `deploy/host/install-host.sh` |
|---|---|---|
| For | A fresh Ubuntu VM | A server that already runs Caddy |
| Mynt runs as | A Docker container, with Caddy in Docker beside it | A systemd service, `mynt.service` |
| What it serves | The MCP server only | The MCP server, and optionally Mynt Studio on the same domain |
| Releases and rollback | The image is rebuilt in place | One folder per commit under `/opt/mynt/releases`, with `/opt/mynt/current` pointing at the live one |
| Backups | None | Nightly, with a weekly restore test (see [Backups](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#backups)) |

The confidential service is not part of either path. It is deployed separately from `deploy/confidential`; see [Confidential computing](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/confidential-computing.md#operator-steps-for-aws-nitro-enclaves).

Deployment scripts take the domain and every other address as arguments. Nothing about a particular server is kept in the repository.

### A fresh VM with Docker

[`deploy/setup-vm.sh`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/deploy/setup-vm.sh) sets up an Ubuntu VM end to end:

```sh
# as root on the VM, with the domain's A record pointing at it
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/never2average/mynt/main/deploy/setup-vm.sh -o setup-vm.sh
bash setup-vm.sh mcp.example.com [git-ref]
```

What it does:

- Installs Docker and opens only SSH, 80 and 443 in `ufw`.
- Runs Supabase's official Docker stack in `/opt/supabase` with freshly generated secrets. Supabase's own dashboard, its API gateway and its pooler are bound to localhost; reach the dashboard with `ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 root@<vm>`.
- Creates a least-privilege Postgres role, `financial_products_app`, that owns only the `financial_products` schema.
- Builds the MCP image from `core/` and runs it with Caddy, which gets the TLS certificate automatically and serves `https://<domain>/mcp`.

Create users on the VM:

```sh
docker compose -f /opt/mynt/src/deploy/docker-compose.yml exec mcp \
  node dist/index.js users add --name "Ines" --role innovator
```

### On a server that already runs Caddy

[`deploy/host/install-host.sh`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/deploy/host/install-host.sh) installs Mynt without Docker for Mynt itself (Supabase still runs in Docker):

```sh
bash install-host.sh <domain> [git-ref] [--studio-upstream <studio host> | --no-studio]
```

Each deploy:

1. Unpacks the commit into `/opt/mynt/releases/<commit>`.
2. Installs and builds the server in that release's `core/` folder, from core's own lockfile.
3. Points `/opt/mynt/current` at the release.
4. Restarts `mynt.service`, which runs `node dist/index.js serve-http` in `/opt/mynt/current/core`.

Each new release also links `dist` to `core/dist`, so `/opt/mynt/current/dist/index.js` still works for anything that runs it.

The installer generates `MYNT_PSEUDONYM_SECRET` and, unless the confidential service already holds the vault's keys, `MYNT_VAULT_KEY`, once, and keeps them across runs in the server's environment file. Losing `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` loses everything sealed with it.

**Older releases.** Releases from before the repository was split into `core/` and `platform/` ran from the release's root. The installer refuses such a commit ("uses the old layout; run that commit's own installer") before it deletes or changes anything, and it never deletes the live release. To go back to such a commit, run that commit's own `deploy/host/install-host.sh`, which puts back its own unit file.

**The hosting gateway.** Where the hosting gateway is set up (`hosting-gateway.sh`, [gateway mode](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/apps-and-builds.md#gateway-mode)), every deploy also replaces its installed sync script (`/usr/local/sbin/mynt-gateway-sync`) with this release's `hosting-gateway.sh`, which its timer runs within a minute. A change to that script goes live with the deploy, not only when the gateway is set up again.

### Mynt Studio on Mynt's domain

On a host installed with `deploy/host/install-host.sh`, Mynt Studio can be served on the same domain as Mynt, with no separate Studio subdomain:

```sh
bash install-host.sh <domain> [git-ref] --studio-upstream <studio host>
```

`<studio host>` is where Studio actually runs, for example its hosting deployment's address. It is a host name only: no scheme, port or path.

**What stays with Mynt.** Every path Mynt serves still goes to it:

| Paths | Request body limit |
|---|---|
| `/mcp`, `/healthz`, `/v1/*`, `/agent/*`, `/bd/*` | As without Studio |
| `/v1`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/.well-known/*`, `/ramp-sandbox/*`, `/vendor-sandbox/*`, `/confidential/*` | 64 KB |
| `/webhooks/*` (the sign-in provider's events) and `/esign/*` (the e-signature service's events and the signing frame's origins) | 1 MB |

**What goes to Studio.** Everything else, `/` included, is proxied to the Studio host, with request bodies up to 4.5 MB. Streaming isn't buffered.

**Mynt's own answer at `/`.** The one-line text Mynt answers at `/` is replaced by Studio's home page. `/llms.txt` still tells MCP clients and AI assistants where the endpoint is.

**Persistence.** The setting is kept in `/etc/mynt/edge.env`, which is root-only and holds no secrets, so later deploys without the flag keep it. `--no-studio` turns it off; without Studio, Caddy's site for Mynt is exactly what it was. `deploy/host/render-site.sh` renders the site from `deploy/host/site.caddy` and `deploy/host/studio-routes.caddy`, and CI checks its routes with Caddy itself.

**The caller's address.** This server removes any `X-Mynt-Client-IP` a caller sends, on every path, and then sets it to the caller's real address on requests it passes to Studio. Studio trusts the header only when the request comes from an address in its `TRUSTED_EDGE_IPS` setting. Every response also gets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

Going live, in this order:

1. Deploy the edge first: run `install-host.sh <domain> --studio-upstream <studio host>`. Studio keeps working at its own address meanwhile.
2. Set Studio's settings and redeploy it:
   - `APP_URL`: `https://<domain>`. Sign-in then returns to Mynt's domain, and everyone signs in once more.
   - `TRUSTED_EDGE_IPS`: every public outbound address of this server, IPv4 and IPv6.

A missing address in `TRUSTED_EDGE_IPS` doesn't break Studio. Requests from it are still served, because they carry `X-Mynt-Client-IP`, but every user coming through it shares one sign-in rate-limit bucket (429 after 20 starts in 10 minutes). Studio logs a warning naming the address to add.

From then on, people reach Studio only through Mynt's domain. A request to Studio's own deployment address from anywhere but this server, without `X-Mynt-Client-IP` (a browser, for any path), gets a 308 to the same path on `APP_URL`.

Studio's own settings are in [its README](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/platform/studio/README.md#settings).

## Backups

On a host installed with `deploy/host/install-host.sh`, Supabase is backed up every night and a backup is test-restored every week. The installer sets this up on every deploy; there is nothing to switch on. The Docker path (`deploy/setup-vm.sh`) sets up no backups.

| | |
|---|---|
| What | Every database and role in Supabase's Postgres (`pg_dumpall`, so Mynt's `financial_products` schema, sign-ins and Storage's records all come along), plus Storage's files (`volumes/storage` in the Supabase directory) |
| When | Daily around 02:30 UTC (`mynt-backup.timer`) |
| Restore test | Sundays around 04:30 UTC (`mynt-backup-verify.timer`). It restores the newest backup into a throwaway `postgres:17` container with no network, counts the tables in `financial_products`, `auth`, `storage` and `public`, and removes the container |
| Where | `/var/backups/mynt/<time>/` on the server, readable by root only, kept 7 days |
| Off-site, if you set it up | Encrypted copies in your own bucket: 14 daily and 8 weekly (Sunday's) |
| Log | `/var/log/mynt/backup.log` |

Nothing leaves the server unencrypted. Without an encryption key the backups stay on the server.

### Checking backups

`ops_status` has a `backups` section and says when something needs attention:

- no backup in 26 hours;
- a failed run;
- a failed restore test;
- "backups are on this server only; add an off-site bucket".

### Turning on off-site copies

You need a bucket at any S3-compatible storage service (Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 and DigitalOcean Spaces all work) and an encryption key pair that you keep.

1. On your own computer (not the server), install [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age) and make a key pair:

   ```sh
   age-keygen -o mynt-backup-identity.txt
   ```

   It prints a public key starting `age1`; that one goes on the server. The file `mynt-backup-identity.txt` is the only thing that can decrypt the backups: keep it in your password manager or another safe place, never on the server.
2. At your storage service, create a private bucket and an access key that can read, write and delete in that bucket only.
3. On the server, as root, open `/etc/mynt/backup.env` and fill it in. The installer created the file with these lines commented out; it is readable by root only, and the installer never changes it once it exists.

   ```sh
   BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT=age1...your public key...
   BACKUP_REMOTE=myntbackup:your-bucket/mynt
   RCLONE_CONFIG_MYNTBACKUP_TYPE=s3
   RCLONE_CONFIG_MYNTBACKUP_PROVIDER=Cloudflare
   RCLONE_CONFIG_MYNTBACKUP_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
   RCLONE_CONFIG_MYNTBACKUP_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
   RCLONE_CONFIG_MYNTBACKUP_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
   ```

   For DigitalOcean Spaces use `PROVIDER=DigitalOcean` and `ENDPOINT=https://<region>.digitaloceanspaces.com`. For Backblaze B2 use `PROVIDER=Other` and `ENDPOINT=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.
4. Run one backup now and check it: `systemctl start mynt-backup.service`, then `ops_status` should show `offsite: "uploaded"`.

### Restoring

Try a test restore first. It never touches production:

```sh
bash /opt/mynt/current/deploy/host/restore.sh --test /var/backups/mynt/<time>
```

To use an off-site copy, download it on the server and copy your identity file over only for the restore:

```sh
set -a; . /etc/mynt/backup.env; set +a     # in a root shell: rclone reads the bucket settings from these
rclone --config /dev/null copy myntbackup:your-bucket/mynt/daily/<time> /root/restore-<time>
bash /opt/mynt/current/deploy/host/restore.sh --test /root/restore-<time> --identity /root/mynt-backup-identity.txt
```

To replace production with a backup, use `--yes-replace-production` instead of `--test`. It:

1. takes a safety backup of the current state;
2. stops Mynt and Supabase's other services;
3. replaces every database and Storage's files (the old files are moved aside, not deleted);
4. starts everything again and prints the table counts.

Delete the identity file and the downloaded copy from the server afterwards (`shred -u /root/mynt-backup-identity.txt`).

### Backup settings

Settings such as the Supabase directory (`SUPABASE_DIR`, default `/opt/supabase`) and the Postgres container (`BACKUP_DB_CONTAINER`, default `supabase-db`) can be changed in `/etc/mynt/backup.env` too. They are listed at the top of [`deploy/host/backup.sh`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/deploy/host/backup.sh).

## Settings by name

Mynt's settings are kept in three places.

**Environment variables.** Secrets and infrastructure settings are read from the server's environment when it starts. They are referenced by name only: values live in the server's environment file, never in the repository, a command line, a log or a chat. `node dist/index.js --help` lists the main ones. The table below names every setting the server reads and links to the section that explains it.

**The platform key vault.** A Mynt admin can set the server's own keys from Mynt instead: Studio's Platform admin, Platform settings, Key vault, or `set_platform_key`. Each key is sealed by the confidential host and never returned. The keys it takes are listed in [The key vault](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#the-key-vault).

**Operational settings.** The budgets, limits and the build audit can be changed from Mynt too, in Platform settings' Operational settings tab or with `set_platform_setting`. They are listed in [Operational settings](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#operational-settings).

**Precedence.** For every key and every operational setting, the server's environment wins where it sets the name. Otherwise Mynt uses what an admin set in Mynt (the vault's key, or the stored setting). Otherwise a key is unset and a setting takes Mynt's default. So setting nothing in Mynt changes nothing, and the operator can always override or recover from the server. An empty variable doesn't count as set.

**What takes effect when.** An operational setting applies from its next use. A key that is read where it's used (`SIGNWELL_API_KEY`, `SIGNWELL_WEBHOOK_ID`, `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `MYNT_PSEUDONYM_SECRET`) applies at once. Every other vault key is read when the server starts, so it applies after a restart, and its row says so.

**Keys that must stay on the server.** These can't be set in the vault:

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Mynt needs it to open the database the vault is kept in |
| `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` | It is the key the vault is sealed with |
| `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST`, `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST_URL`, `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST_CLIENT_CERT`, `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST_CLIENT_KEY`, `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST_CLIENT_CA`, `CONFIDENTIAL_HOST_KMS_KEY` | They are read before the vault opens; the certificate and key are files on the server's disk |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | It names a key file on the server's disk |
| `FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN` | It says who is running the stdio command |

Identifiers that go with a vault key but aren't secret stay in the environment too: `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_SLUG`, `TURNKEY_ORGANIZATION_ID` and `TURNKEY_API_PUBLIC_KEY`.

**Database settings.** The other settings Mynt admins change while the server runs are stored in the database and set through admin tools or in Studio under Platform admin, Platform settings:

| Setting | Changed with | Explained in |
|---|---|---|
| The platform's own keys | `set_platform_key`, `remove_platform_key`, or Platform settings' Key vault in Studio | [The key vault](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#the-key-vault) |
| Operational settings (budgets, limits, the build audit) | `set_platform_setting`, or Platform settings' Operational settings in Studio | [Operational settings](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#operational-settings) |
| E-signature (the provider's key, the webhook, test mode) | `set_esign_api_key`, `register_esign_webhook`, `set_esign_test_mode`, `remove_esign_api_key`, or Platform settings in Studio | [E-signature](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/agreements.md#e-signature) |
| Public sign-up | `set_public_signup` | [Public sign-up](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#public-sign-up) |
| The Mynt Ramp's firm | `set_mynt_ramp` | [The Mynt Ramp](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/vendors-and-marketplace.md#the-mynt-ramp) |
| Treasury mainnet | `configure_treasury_mainnet` | [Treasury mainnet](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/liquidity-and-treasury.md#treasury-mainnet) |
| The Solana mainnet signer | `configure_solana_signer` | [Signers](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/solana-programs.md#signers) |
| Take rates | `define_take_rate` | [Take rates](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/platform-admin.md#take-rates) |

### Environment variables

| Setting | What it turns on or controls | Explained in |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | The Postgres connection. Required | [Users and tokens](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#users-and-tokens) |
| `PGPOOL_MAX` | The size of the database connection pool | This table |
| `PORT`, `HOST` | The defaults for `serve-http`'s `--port` and `--host` | [Shared server over HTTP](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#shared-server-over-http) |
| `PUBLIC_URL` | The server's public origin. Needed by Clerk sign-in, builds, hosting and e-signature | [Sign-in with Clerk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#sign-in-with-clerk) |
| `FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_TOKEN` | The user's token in stdio mode; without it the server is a guest | [Locally over stdio](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#locally-over-stdio) |
| `FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_FILE` | Named in `mynt --help` as a JSON catalogue for seeding published products. The server no longer reads it; the reference catalogue is applied with the seed script instead | [The reference catalogue](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#the-reference-catalogue) |
| `MYNT_PSEUDONYM_SECRET` | Pseudonyms on product requests; without it `list_product_requests` lists nothing | [Answering](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/products.md#answering) |
| `MYNT_VAULT_KEY` | The key that seals the vault while the confidential host is `local` | [Confidential computing settings](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/confidential-computing.md#confidential-computing-settings) |
| `NODE_ENV` | With `production`, webhook addresses must be public `https` addresses | [Webhook addresses](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/runtime-api.md#webhook-addresses) |
| `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Clerk sign-in over HTTP, linked accounts, and workspaces as organizations | [Sign-in with Clerk](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#sign-in-with-clerk) |
| `MCP_REQUIRE_AUDIENCE` | Set to `false`, access tokens need not be issued for this server's `/mcp` resource. Leave it unset | [How it works](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/operations.md#how-it-works) |
| `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The organization webhook at `/webhooks/clerk` | [The organization webhook](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference/workspaces-and-sign-in.md#the-organization-webhook) |
